semin-durr:93-93.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {بِقَمِيصِي}: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to what precedes it, the bāʾ being transitivising, as it is in «ذهبْتُ به» ("I went off with it"); or it may be for the ḥāl (circumstantial), so that it is attached to something omitted, i.e. "go, having my shirt with you". «هذا» is a naʿt (adjective) of it, or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or a badal (substitute); «بصيراً» is a ḥāl. «أجمعين» is a tawkīd (emphasis), and the emphasis has been made with it without «كل»; it may also be a ḥāl.

semin-durr:94-94.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {تُفَنِّدُونِ}: al-tafnīd is corrupting; one says "فَنَّدت فلاناً", i.e. "I corrupted his judgement and rejected it". The poet said:
2831 - يا صاحِبيَّ دَعَا لَوْمي وتَفْنيدي ... فليسَ ما قُلْتُ من أمرٍ بمَرْدُوْدِ
(O my two companions, leave off blaming me and calling me foolish, for nothing I have said is to be rejected.)
And from it is «أَفْنَدَ الدهرُ فلاناً» ("time made so-and-so feeble-minded"). The poet said:
2832 - دَعِ الدهرَ يَفْعَلُ ما أرادَ فإنه ... إذا كُلِّفَ الإِفنادَ بالناسِ أفندا
(Let time do what it wills, for when it is charged with ruining people, it ruins them.)
And al-fanad is corruption; al-Nābigha said:
2833 - إلاَّ سليمانَ إذ قال الإِلهُ له ... قُمْ في البرِيَّةِ فاحْدُدْها عن الفَنَد
(Except Solomon, when God said to him: "Rise among creation and restrain it from corruption.")
And al-find is the peak of a mountain, and from it a man is named Find; al-Find al-Zimmānī, one of the poets of the Ḥamāsa, is from that. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "One says 'شيخ مُفَنَّد' (a feeble-minded old man) but one does not say 'عجوز مُفَنَّدة' (a feeble-minded old woman), because she was never, in her youth, a person of judgement so that she might be called feeble-minded in her old age"; and this is strange. The apodosis (jawāb) of the counterfactual «لولا» is omitted, its implied form being "you would have believed me". Its implied form may also be: "I would have told you".

semin-durr:96-96.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: {أَلْقَاهُ}: the apparent meaning is that the fāʿil (agent) is the pronoun of the bearer of good news. It is also said: it is the pronoun of Jacob. In «بصيراً» there are two views. The first: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. he returned in this state. The second: it is its (the verb's) khabar (predicate), because it means «صار» ("became") according to some of them. And «بَصير» is from «بَصُر بالشيء» ("he saw the thing"), like «ظريف» from «ظَرُف». It is also said: it is an intensive form like «عليم». In it is an indication that his sight had not gone away entirely.

semin-durr:100-100.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: {وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ}: this is of the type of taghlīb (giving one term precedence over the other), meaning his father and his mother, or his maternal aunt. «سُجَّداً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because prostration comes after falling down"; and this is open to question, because it is joined to it, not delayed from it.
His saying: {مِن قَبْلُ}: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «رُؤْياي», i.e. the interpretation of my vision at that time. Or the governing word in it may be «تَأْويل», because the interpretation was thus from the moment it occurred, and now it has become manifest to him. Or it may be a ḥāl from «رُؤْياي» — said by Abū al-Baqāʾ — but it has preceded that a word cut off from iḍāfa (genitive construction) does not occur as a ḥāl.
His saying: {قَدْ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّي} is a ḥāl from «رؤياي», and it may be resumptive. In «حقاً» there are views. The first: it is a ḥāl. The second: it is a second mafʿūl (object). The third: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising the verb in terms of meaning, i.e. my Lord has realised it truly by His making it so.
His saying: {أَحْسَنَ بي}: «أَحْسَنَ» is originally made transitive with «إلى». He said: {وَأَحْسِن كَمَآ أَحْسَنَ الله إِلَيْكَ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 77]. So it is said: it was made to imply the meaning of «لَطُف» ("to be gracious"), and so was made transitive with the bāʾ, as in His saying {وبالوالدين إِحْسَاناً} [al-Baqara: 83] and the saying of Kuthayyir ʿAzza:
2834 - أَسِيْئِي بنا أو أَحْسِني لا مَلُوْمَةً ... لَدَيْنَا ولا مَقْلِيَّةً إنْ تَقَلَّتِ
(Treat us badly or treat us well — you will not be blamed by us, nor hated, if you turn away in aversion.)
It is also said: rather, it is made transitive with it as well. It is also said: it means «إلى». It is also said: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted: "He made His dealing with me good", so that «بي» is attached to that omitted word; this is the reconstruction of Abū al-Baqāʾ. And it is open to question, in that it involves omitting the maṣdar while keeping what it governs, and this is disallowed by the Basrans. «إذ» is accusative (manṣūb) by «أَحْسَنَ» or by the omitted maṣdar — said by Abū al-Baqāʾ — and it has the objection mentioned earlier.
And «البَدْو» is the opposite of settled life, and it is from manifestness; «بدا يبدو» is said when someone dwells in the desert. «إذا بَدَوْنا جَفَوْنا» ("when we go out to the desert we become coarse") is related from ʿUmar, i.e. we take on the manners of the Bedouins.
His saying: {لَطِيفٌ لِّمَا يَشَآءُ}: «لَطُفَ» is originally made transitive with the bāʾ, and it is only made transitive with the lām because it implies the meaning of «مُدَبِّر» ("one who arranges"), i.e. You arrange, by Your subtlety, whatever You will.

semin-durr:101-101.t:
ʿAbd Allāh read «آتَيْتَنِ» and «عَلَّمْتَنِ» without a yāʾ in both. Ibn ʿAṭiyya related that Abū Dharr read «أتيتني» without an alif after the hamza. And «مِنْ» in «مِن المُلْك» and in «مِنْ تأويل» is partitive, and the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, i.e. "something great of the dominion", so it is a naʿt (adjective) of that omitted word. It is also said: it is redundant (zāʾida). It is also said: it is for explaining the genus; and these two are far-fetched.
And «فاطر» may be a naʿt of «ربّ», or it may be a badal (substitute) or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أَعْني» ("I mean"), or a second vocative.

semin-durr:102-102.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {ذَلِكَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and {مِنْ أَنْبَآءِ الغيب} is its khabar (predicate), and «نُوحيه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). It may also be a second khabar, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in the khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it (ذلك) to be a relative noun meaning «الذي». Its parallel has preceded. And «هم يَمْكُرون» is a ḥāl.

semin-durr:103-103.t: [His saying:] {وَلَوْ حَرَصْتَ}: parenthetical between «ما» and its khabar (predicate). The apodosis (jawāb) of «لو» is omitted because what precedes indicates it.

semin-durr:106-106.t: And [His saying]: {إِلاَّ وَهُمْ مُّشْرِكُونَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial).

semin-durr:107-107.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: {مِّنْ عَذَابِ الله}: a naʿt (adjective) of «غاشية», and «بَغْتة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and its parallel has preceded.
The majority read «الأرض» in the genitive (majrūr), conjoined to «السماوات», and the pronoun in «عليها» refers to «الآية», so that «يمرُّون» is a naʿt of «الآية», or a ḥāl because it has become specified by being qualified with the prepositional phrase. It is also said: the pronoun in «عليها» returns to «الأرض», so that «يمرون» is a ḥāl from it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And it is said: from it and from the heavens", i.e. the ḥāl would be from both things together; and this is not permissible, since it would then have been necessary to say «عليهما»; and also, they do not pass through the heavens — unless what is meant is "they pass by their signs", in which case the meaning reverts to the pronoun referring to «الآية». The first objection may be answered by saying that it is of the type of omission, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ} [al-Tawba: 62].
Al-Suddī read «والأرضَ» in the accusative (manṣūb), and its justification is that it is of the type of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), the verb being explained by one agreeing with it in meaning, i.e. "they tread the earth" or "they traverse the earth, passing over it", as when you say «زيداً مررت به» ("Zayd — I passed by him").
ʿIkrima and ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid read «والأرضُ» in the nominative (marfūʿ), as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being the clause after it; and the pronoun in these two readings returns to «الأرض» alone.
Abū Ḥafṣ and Mubashshir ibn ʿUbayd read: «أو يَأْتيهم الساعة» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, because it is figuratively feminine, and also because of the separation.

semin-durr:108-108.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَدْعُو إلى الله}: it may be resumptive, and this is the apparent view, or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the yāʾ. And «على بصيرة» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «أدعو», i.e. I call, being upon clear insight.
His saying: {وَمَنِ اتبعني}: conjoined to the fāʿil of «أدعو», and for that reason it was emphasised with the detached pronoun in His saying «أنا». It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "and whoever follows me calls as well". It may also be that «على بصيرة» is a fronted khabar, «أنا» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and «ومَن اتَّبعني» conjoined to it. And it may be that «على بصيرة» alone is a ḥāl, with «أنا» as its fāʿil, and «ومَنِ اتَّبعني» conjoined to it as well. As for the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «أدعو», it may be that none is intended, i.e. I am one of those who call to Allah; or it may be implied as: "that I call people".
ʿAbd Allāh read «هذا سبيلي» in the masculine, and it has preceded that it (سبيل) is treated as masculine and feminine.

semin-durr:109-109.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {نوحي}: the generality read «يوحى» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, in the passive. Ḥafṣ read «نوحي» with the nūn, in the active, in consideration of His saying «وما أَرْسَلْنا». He likewise read the one in al-Naḥl and the one at the beginning of al-Anbiyāʾ, and the two brothers [Translator's note: i.e. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] agreed with him on His saying «نوحي إليه» in al-Anbiyāʾ, as will come, if Allah the Exalted wills. The clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «رجالاً», and {مِّنْ أَهْلِ القرى} is a second naʿt; placing this naʿt before the one preceding it would have been more common in usage, because it is closer to a single word, and its detailed treatment has preceded in al-Māʾida.
His saying: {وَلَدَارُ الآخرة} and what follows it have preceded in al-Anʿām.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {ياصاحبي السجن}: it may be of the type of iḍāfa (genitive construction) to an adverb of place, since the original is «يا صاحبي في السجن» (O my two companions in the prison). And it may be of the type of iḍāfa to what resembles the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the meaning being: O you two inhabitants of the prison, as in His words: {أَصْحَابُ النار} [al-Baqara: 39].
His words {مِن شَيْءٍ} [Yūsuf: 38]: it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. any degree of association (شيئاً من الإشراك). And it may apply to the thing associated, i.e. it was not for us to associate anything other than Him, whether an angel, a human or a jinn — so how much less an idol? And «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) on both interpretations, because the two conditions are present.
His words: {أَمِ الله}: here it is the connected «أم» (muttaṣila), which conjoins the Name of Majesty (الله) to «أرباب».

semin-durr:40-40.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِلاَّ أَسْمَآءً}: either what is meant by them is the things named, or it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. entities of things named. And «سَمَّيْتموها» is a naʿt (adjective); it is transitive to two objects, the second of which is omitted, i.e. «سمَّيْتموها آلهة» (which you have named gods). And «ما أنزل» is a naʿt of «أسماء», and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) in «منْ سلطان», i.e. a proof. And «إنِ الحكم»: «إنْ» is negative. And it is not permissible to make [the vowel of the nūn] follow the ḍamma of the ḥāʾ, as in his words: «قالتُ اخْرُجْ» and the like, because the alif and the lām are an independent word, so they separate the two.
His words: {أَمَرَ أَلاَّ}: regarding «أَمَر» it may be resumptive, which is the apparent view, or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «قد» intended with it according to some. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And it is weak, because of the weakness of the governing word in it." I say: by the governing word he means the notion of being settled (الاستقرار) contained in the preposition in His words: «إلا للَّه».

semin-durr:41-41.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَيَسْقِي}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ, from «سقاه يَسْقيه». And ʿIkrima, in one transmission, read «فَيُسْقي» with ḍamma on the imperfect prefix, from «أسقى»; they are two dialectal usages: one says «سَقَاه» and «أَسْقاه». It will come that they are two readings among the Seven: «نَسْقيكم ونُسْقيكم مما [في] بطونه». And are they of one meaning, or is there a difference between them? Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted from ʿIkrima and al-Jaḥdarī that they both read «فَيُسقَى ربُّه» in the passive, with «ربُّه» in the nominative. Al-Zamakhsharī attributed it to ʿIkrima alone.
His words: {قُضِيَ الأمر}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "They did not ask for a ruling on one matter, but on two different matters, so what is the reason for the singular? I say: what is meant by 'the matter' is what they were accused of — poisoning the king — and that for which they were imprisoned."

semin-durr:42-42.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ}: the fāʿil (agent) of «ظنَّ» may be Yūsuf, upon him be peace, if his interpretation was by way of ijtihād (personal reasoning), or it may be the cup-bearer, if his interpretation was by way of revelation; or the ẓann may be in the sense of certainty. Al-Zamakhsharī said this.
I say: he means that if «الظنّ» is in its proper sense, its attribution to Yūsuf is not sound unless his interpretation was by way of ijtihād, because whenever it is by way of revelation it is certain, so the ẓann would then be attributed to the cup-bearer and not to him, upon him be peace. But if «الظنّ» is in the sense of certainty, then its attribution to Yūsuf is sound even if his interpretation was by way of revelation, and that is good. Qatāda held that «الظنّ» is in its proper sense and is attributed to Yūsuf, if his interpretation was by way of ijtihād, for he said: "«الظنّ» here is in its proper sense, because the interpretation of dreams is conjecture."
His words: {مِّنْهُمَا}: it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «ناج», or it may be attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And it is not attached to «ناجٍ», because the meaning is not on that." I say: if it were attached to «ناجٍ», it would suggest that someone other than the two of them escaped from them, i.e. got loose from them, whereas the meaning is that one of the two is the one who is saved; and this meaning he drew attention to is far-fetched to imagine. And the pronoun in «فَأَنْساه» refers to the cup-bearer. And it was said: to Yūsuf, and that is weak.
His words: {بِضْعَ سِنِينَ}: accusative (manṣūb) as an adverb of time (ẓarf zamānī), and there is disagreement about it. Qatāda said: "It is between three and nine." Abū ʿUbayd said: "«البِضْع» does not reach a decade nor half a decade; it is only from one to ten." [Translator's note: the source says this as written; the two clauses appear to be in tension.] Mujāhid said: "It is from three to seven." Al-Farrāʾ said: "«البِضْع» is mentioned only with the tens, and is not mentioned with a hundred or a thousand." Al-Rāghib said: "«البِضْع», with kasra, is what is cut off from ten, and it is said of what is between three and ten; and it was said: rather it is above five and below ten." I say: so he made it derived from the root «البَضْع», which is cutting; from it: «بَضَعْتُ اللحمَ», i.e. I cut it; and «البِضاعة»: a portion of wealth for trade; and «المِبْضَع»: that with which one cuts; and «البَعْض» — it has preceded that it is from this meaning, when «البعوضة» was mentioned.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {سِمَانٍ}: a naʿt (adjective) of «بقرات»; it is the plural of «سمينة», and «سمين» is also pluralised on it: one says «رجال سِمان» just as one says «نِساء كِرام» and «رجال كِرام». And «السِّمَنُ» is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «سَمِن يَسْمَن», so he is «سمين»; thus the maṣdar and the [active participle] came contrary to analogy, since their analogical forms would be «سَمَن» with fatḥa on the mīm, and «سَمِن» with kasra on it, like «فَرِح فَرَحاً فهو فَرِح».
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Is there a difference between making «سمان» an adjective of the tamyīz (specifier), which is «بقراتٍ», rather than of the thing specified, which is «سبعَ», and saying «سبعَ بقراتٍ سِماناً»? I say: if you make it an adjective of «بقرات», you intend to specify the seven by a kind of cows, namely the fat ones among them, not by their genus; whereas if you made it an adjective of the seven, you would intend to specify the seven by the genus of cows, not by a kind of them, and then you would go back and describe the thing specified by the genus as being fat. If you say: why was it not said «سبعَ عجافٍ» in iḍāfa (genitive construction)? I say: the tamyīz is set up to make the genus clear, and «العِجاف» is an adjective by which alone the clarification does not take place. If you say: but they do say «ثلاثة فرسان» and «خمسة أصحاب». I say: «الفارس», «الصاحب», «الراكب» and the like are adjectives that have come to function as nouns and so took their rule, and what was permitted in them is not permitted in others. Do you not see that you do not say «عندي ثلاثةُ ضخامٍ» nor «أربعةُ غلاظٍ»? If you say: that is among what is ambiguous, whereas what we are dealing with has no ambiguity in it; do you not see that He did not say «وبقرات سبعَ عجافٍ», because it is known that the cows are what is meant? I say: abandoning the original is not permissible when one can do without what is not original, and one can do without your saying «سبع عجافٍ» [Translator's note: so in the text; the sense is that «سبع عجافٍ» can do without] what you propose, namely specification by the adjective."
I say: these are fine questions and answers. The precise sense of the first question and its answer is: describing the tamyīz by something entails describing the thing specified by it, but describing the thing specified does not entail describing the tamyīz by that thing. The explanation of this is that if you say «عندي أربعةُ رجالٍ حسانٍ» with the genitive, its meaning is "four of the handsome men", so the handsomeness of the four is entailed, because they are some of the handsome men; and if you say «عندي أربعةُ رجالٍ حسانٌ» with «حسان» in the nominative, its meaning is "four of the men, handsome", and there is no indication in it that the men [in general] are described as handsome.
The precise sense of the second and its answer is: number nouns are not put in iḍāfa to adjectives except under poetic necessity; rather [adjectives] are brought following the number nouns, so one says «عندي ثلاثة قرشيون», and one does not say «ثلاثةُ قرشيين» in iḍāfa except in poetry. Then he raised the objection of «ثلاثة فرسان» and answered that it functions as nouns do.
The precise sense of the third is: «ثلاثةُ ضِخام» and the like are disallowed only because what they describe is not known, unlike the noble verse, for the thing described is known and that is why it was not stated explicitly. He answered that by saying that the original rule is that a number is not put in iḍāfa to an adjective, as has preceded, so this original is not abandoned when one can do with the derived form. In sum, there is some awkwardness in this wording; this is its summary. The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] did not cite its text nor object to it; rather he summarised some of its meanings and left it with its difficulty.
And «عَجْفاء» is pluralised as «عِجاف», whereas the analogical form is «عُجُف», like «حمراء» and «حُمُر», by treating it like «سِمان» because it is its opposite; and it is their custom to treat a like thing like its like and an opposite like its opposite. Al-Zamakhsharī said this. "And «العَجَف» is the extreme emaciation after which there is no [further degree]." [The poet] said:
2794 - عمرُو الذي هَشَم الثريدَ لقومِه ... ورجالُ مكةَ مُسْنِتون عِجافُ
(ʿAmr is the one who crumbled bread into broth for his people, while the men of Mecca were famine-stricken and emaciated.)
And al-Rāghib said: "It is from their saying «نَصْلٌ أعجفُ», i.e. a thin blade; and «عَجَفَتْ نفسي عن الطعام» and «عن فلان» when it shrank from them; and «أَعْجف الرجلُ», i.e. the man found his livestock emaciated."
His words: {وَأُخَرَ}: «أُخَرَ» is conjoined to «سبعَ», not to «سنبلات», and He will have omitted the number noun from His words «وأُخَر يابسات», the implied form being «وسبعاً أُخَرَ» (and seven others). It was omitted only because the division in the cows requires a division in the ears of grain.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: is there in the verse an indication that the dry ears were seven like the green ones? I say: the speech is built on its being directed to this number in the fat and lean cows and the green ears, so the sense of «الأُخر» must cover the seven, and His words «وأُخَرَ يابسات» mean «وسبعاً أُخَرَ»." End of quotation. And «أُخر» could not be conjoined to the tamyīz, which is «سنبلات», so that «أُخَر» would be genitive and not accusative, because by virtue of being conjoined to it, it would be part of the thing specifying «سبعَ», while by virtue of being "other" it would be distinct from «سبع», so the two would contradict each other. Had the structure of the noble verse been «سبع سنبلاتٍ خضرٍ ويابسات», the conjunction would have been sound, and it would be a distribution of the ears between these two descriptions, I mean greenness and dryness.
Al-Zamakhsharī made this clear where he said: "If you say: may His words «وأُخَرَ يابساتٍ» be conjoined to «سنبلاتٍ خَضْرٍ», so that it is genitive in position? I say: that leads to a contradiction, which is that conjoining it to «سنبلات خضر» requires that it enter into their rule, so that together with them it would be a specifier of the seven mentioned, while the word «الأُخَر» requires that they be other than the seven. The explanation is that you say «عنده سبعة رجالٍ قيامٍ وقعودٍ» with the genitive, and it is sound because you have specified the seven by men described as standing and sitting, on the understanding that some of them are standing and some sitting; but if you said «عنده سبعةٌ رجال قيام وآخرين قعود», it would be contradictory and thus unsound."
His words {لِلرُّؤْيَا}: there are four views on it. The first: that the lām in it is redundant (zāʾida), so it is attached to nothing; it was added because the governed word precedes, strengthening the governing word, just as it is added when the governing word is derivative, as in His words: {فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ} [Hūd: 107]; and it is not added outside these two cases except under poetic necessity, as in his words:
2795 - فَلَمَّا أَنْ تواقَفْنا قليلاً ... أَنَخْنا للكلاكلِ فارْتَمَيْنا
(When we had stood facing each other a little while, we made [the camels] kneel on their breasts and shot at one another.)
He means «أنخنا الكلاكل», so it was added though both conditions were lacking. This is how some phrase it, saying "except under poetic necessity", while others say: "mostly it is not added", guarding thereby against His words {رَدِفَ لَكُم} [al-Naml: 72], for the original is «رَدِفَكم» and the lām was added in it, with neither precedence nor derivativeness; and whoever states [the rule] without qualification makes the verse a case of taḍmīn (implication of another verb's meaning), and it will come in its place. A good portion of this has preceded for you in the course of this work.
The second: that «تَعْبُرون» is made to imply the meaning of a verb that is transitive with lām, its implied form being: if you undertake the interpretation of the dream.
The third: that «للرُّؤْيا» is the khabar (predicate) of «كنتم», as you say «كان فلان لهذا الأمر» when he is able to handle it and has mastery of it. On this view there are two views on «تعبرُون»: one, that it is a second khabar of «كنتم»; and the second, that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun made nominative by the preposition phrase because of its occurring as a khabar.
The fourth: that the lām is attached to an omitted word, being for clarification, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: {وَكَانُواْ فِيهِ مِنَ الزاهدين} [Yūsuf: 20], whose implied form is «أعني فيه» (I mean, regarding him); and likewise this, its implied form being «أعني للرؤيا» (I mean, for the dream). On this view the object of «تعبُرون» is omitted, its implied form being «تعْبُرونها» (you interpret it).
And Abū Jaʿfar read «الرُّؤْيا» and words of its pattern as «الرُّيَّا» with assimilation (idghām). That is because he changed the hamza to a wāw because it was vowelless after a ḍamma, so a yāʾ and a wāw came together, the first of them vowelless, so the wāw was changed to yāʾ and the yāʾ was assimilated into the yāʾ. This reading is weak in their view, because the substitution is not obligatory, so it is as though no wāw existed, in view of the hamza.
And «عَبَرْتُ الرؤيا» is without doubling. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is what the reliable authorities relied on, and I saw them reject «عَبَّرت» with doubling, and «التعبير» and «المعبِّر»." He said: "But I came across a verse that al-Mubarrad recited in the book al-Kāmil, by one of the Bedouins:
2796 - رَأَيْتُ رُؤْيا ثم عَبَّرْتُها ... وكنتُ للأحلام عَبَّارا
(I saw a dream, then I interpreted it — and I was a great interpreter of dreams.)"
He said: "And the true sense of «عبرت الرؤيا» is: you stated its outcome and the end of its matter, just as you say «عَبَرْتُ النهر» when you cross it until you reach the far side of its breadth."

semin-durr:110-110.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {حتى}: there is nothing in the speech for which «حتى» could be the limit, and for that reason people have differed over supplying something which may properly be given a limit by «حتى». Al-Zamakhsharī supplied it as: "And We sent before you none but men, and their victory was delayed, until…". Al-Qurṭubī supplied it as: "And We sent before you, O Muḥammad, none but men; We did not punish their nations with the punishment until, when…". Ibn al-Jawzī supplied it as: "And We sent before you none but men, and they called their people, who denied them, and their calling and their people's denial went on long, until, when…". And the best of them is what I put first.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya picked out something from the meaning of His saying «أفلم يسيروا» and said: "His saying «أفلم يسيروا» up to «مِنْ قبلِهم» implies that the messengers whom Allah sent from among the people of the towns called them, and they did not believe in them until exemplary punishments befell them, and so they came to be in the sphere of those whose end is taken as a lesson; and because of this implied meaning it was fitting for «حتى» to enter in His saying «حتى إذا»." The Shaykh [Translator's note: i.e. Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Nothing emerged for us from his words for which what follows «حتى» would be the limit, because he tied the limit to what he claimed to have understood from His saying «أفلم يسيروا» — the verse." I say: "they called them and they did not believe" is what is limited.
His saying: {كُذِبُواْ}: the Kufans read «كُذِبوا» with the light (single) letter, and the rest with the doubled one. As for the reading with the light letter, people's views on it have been disturbed, and a rejection of it is related from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her; she said: "God forbid! The messengers would not think that of their Lord." And this ought not to be authentic from her, because of the mutawātir (mass-transmitted) status of this reading.
People have justified it in four ways. The best of them: the pronoun in «وظنُّوا» refers to those to whom [the messengers] were sent, because they were mentioned earlier in His saying {كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الذين مِن قَبْلِهِمْ} [Yūsuf: 109], and because "messengers" call for those to whom they are sent. And the pronoun in «أنهم» and in «كُذِبوا» refers to the messengers, i.e. those to whom they were sent thought that the messengers had been lied to, i.e. those to whom they were sent [thought they had been] given false word concerning the revelation and concerning their being given victory over them.
The second: the three pronouns refer to the messengers. Al-Zamakhsharī said, in setting out this view: "Until, when they despaired of victory and thought that they had been lied to — i.e. their own selves lied to them when they told them that they would be given victory, or their hope did, for one says 'a truthful hope' and 'a lying hope'. The meaning is: the period of denial and enmity from the unbelievers, and of waiting for victory from Allah and hoping for it, had grown long for them and dragged on, until they sensed despair and imagined that there would be no victory for them in this world; then Our victory came to them." End of quotation. So he made the implied fāʿil (agent) either "their selves" or "their hope", and he made «الظنّ» mean imagining, so he took it out of its original meaning — which is the preponderance of one of two sides — and out of its figurative use, which is its use for what is certain.
The third: all the pronouns likewise refer to the messengers, and «الظنّ» is in its proper meaning of preponderance. Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn Jubayr inclined to this; they said: the messengers were human, so they weakened and their thinking became bad. And this ought not to be authentic from these men, for it is a harsh expression regarding the prophets, peace be upon them, and the prophets are far removed from that. For that reason ʿĀʾisha and a large group rejected this interpretation and considered it grave that anything of that sort be attributed to the prophets.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If this is authentic from Ibn ʿAbbās, then by «الظنّ» he meant what crosses the mind and stirs in the heart, something resembling whispering and the talk of the self, as is the way of human nature. As for «الظنّ» which is giving preponderance to one of two possibilities over the other, it is not permissible of a man among the Muslims — so how about the messengers of Allah, who know their Lord best?" I say: nor is it permissible either to say that something resembling whispering crossed their minds; for whispering is from Satan, and they are protected from him.
Al-Fārisī also said: "If someone holds that the meaning is: the messengers thought that what Allah had promised their nations by their tongues had been falsely promised to them, he has said something grave [whose like may not be attributed] to the prophets, nor to the righteous servants of Allah; and likewise whoever claims that Ibn ʿAbbās held that the messengers weakened and thought that the promise to them had been broken; because Allah the Exalted does not break the promise, and there is none to change His words." It is also related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "Its meaning is: and they thought, when they weakened and were overcome, that the victory Allah had promised them had been withheld from them"; and he said: "They were human", and he recited His saying, Exalted is He: {وَزُلْزِلُواْ حتى يَقُولَ الرسول} [al-Baqara: 214].
The fourth: all the pronouns go back to those to whom [the messengers] were sent, i.e. those to whom they were sent thought that the messengers had lied to them in their claim of prophethood and in the punishment with which they had threatened beforehand whoever did not believe in them. And this is the well-known form of the interpretation of Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid; they said: the pronouns may not refer to the messengers, because they are protected from error. It is related that Ibn Jubayr, when asked about it, said: "Yes: when the messengers despaired of their people believing them, and those to whom they were sent thought that the messengers had lied to them." And al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim, who was present, said: "Had I travelled to Yemen for this, it would have been little."
As for the reading with the doubled letter, it is clear: all the pronouns refer to the messengers, i.e. the messengers thought that their nations had denied them in what they had brought, because of the long duration of the trial upon them. In the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī, from ʿĀʾisha: "She said: They are the followers of the prophets who believed in them and gave credence; the trial went on long for them and victory was delayed from them, until, when the messengers despaired of those of their people who denied them, and the messengers thought that their people had denied them, the victory of Allah came to them at that point." I say: and with this the meaning of the two readings becomes one. And «الظنّ» here may be in its proper meaning, or it may mean certainty, or it may mean imagining, according to what has preceded.
Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Mujāhid read «كَذَبوا» with the light letter, in the active. On this reading the pronoun in «ظنُّوا» refers to the nations, and in {أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُواْ} it refers to the messengers, i.e. those to whom they were sent thought that the messengers had lied to them in the victory or the punishment which they had promised them. It may also be that the pronoun in «ظنُّوا» refers to the messengers and in {أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُواْ} to those to whom [they] were sent, i.e. the messengers thought that the nations had lied to them in what they had promised them, namely that they would believe in it; and «الظنّ» here clearly means certainty.
Abū al-Baqāʾ reported that it was read with the doubled letter in the active, and he interpreted it as: the messengers thought that the nations had denied them. Al-Zamakhsharī said, after relating the reading in the active: "Had it been read thus with the doubled letter, its meaning would have been: the messengers thought that their people had denied them in what they had promised them." So he did not know it as a reading; and it is a rare one. He had allowed, in the preceding reading, that all the pronouns refer to the messengers, and that the first refers to those to whom they were sent and what follows to the messengers; he said: "Mujāhid read «كَذَبوا» with the light letter in the active, in the sense: and the messengers thought that they had spoken falsely in the victory they had told their people of — either according to the interpretation of Ibn ʿAbbās, or in that when their people saw no trace of what they had promised, they said to them: 'You have lied to us', so they would be liars in their people's eyes; or: and those to whom they were sent thought that the messengers had lied."
His saying: {جَآءَهُمْ} is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and discussion has preceded about this «حتى»: what is it?
His saying: {فَنُجِّيَ}: Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read it with a single nūn, a doubled jīm and a yāʾ with fatḥa, as a past verb in the passive, with «مَنْ» standing in place of the fāʿil — i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The rest read it with two nūns, the second of them vowelless, the jīm light and the yāʾ vowelless, as the imperfect of «أنجى», with «مَنْ» as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil being the pronoun of the speaker Himself. Al-Ḥasan, al-Jaḥdarī and Mujāhid, among others, read it like the reading of ʿĀṣim, except that they made the yāʾ vowelless. The best way of accounting for it is as has preceded, the yāʾ being made vowelless for lightness, as in the reading {تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 89]; the sound past verb has been made vowelless, so how much more the weak one? As in the poet's saying:
2835 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... قد خُلِطْ بجُلْجُلان
(… it has been mixed with sesame.)
And its like have preceded along with it. It is also said: the origin was «ننجي» with two nūns, and the nūn was assimilated into the jīm; and this is nothing, since the nūn is not assimilated into the jīm — although that has been said about His saying {نُنجِي المؤمنين} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 88], as its explanation will come.
A group read it like the reading of the rest, except that they gave the yāʾ a fatḥa. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Ibn Hubayra related it from Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, and it is an error on the part of Ibn Hubayra." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya imagined that it is an imperfect remaining in its nominative, so he rejected the fatḥa on its final radical and declared its transmitter mistaken; but it is not a mistake. That is because, when an imperfect joined with the fāʾ occurs after both the condition and the apodosis, several ways are allowed in it, one of them being its being accusative by an implied «أنْ» after the fāʾ. This has preceded at His saying {وَإِن تُبْدُواْ مَا في أَنْفُسِكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 284] up to where He said «فيغفر», which was read in the accusative, and its justification has preceded; and there is no difference whether the conditional particle is one that makes the verb jussive, as in the verse of al-Baqara, or not, as in this verse. Al-Ḥasan also read «فَنُنَجِّي» with two nūns, the jīm doubled and the yāʾ vowelless, the imperfect of «نجّى» with doubling for multiplicity. He, Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim and Abū Ḥaywa also read «فنجا», a light past verb, with «مَنْ» as its fāʿil.
Al-Dānī reported that he read it thus for Ibn Muḥayṣin, except that he doubled the jīm, the fāʿil being the pronoun of the victory and «مَنْ» its mafʿūl bihi. Some of them gave preference to the reading of ʿĀṣim on the grounds that the codices agreed in writing it «فنجي» with a single nūn; al-Dānī reported this. Makkī reported that most codices have it, and this suggests the occurrence of disagreement in the script. It was also preferred on the grounds that it has a correspondence with the past verbs before it, and that it follows the manner of speech of kings and great men, in terms of making the verb passive.
Abū Ḥaywa read «يشاء» with the yāʾ, and it has preceded that he reads «فنجا», i.e. so whoever Allah wills to be saved was saved.
Al-Ḥasan read «بأسَه», the pronoun referring to Allah; and in it is a slight divergence from the written text (al-sawād).

semin-durr:111-111.t:
Abū ʿAmr, in the transmission of ʿAbd al-Wārith, and al-Kisāʾī, in the transmission of al-Anṭākī, read «قِصصهم» with kasra on the qāf, and it is the plural of «قِصة». By this reading al-Zamakhsharī gave preference to the pronoun in «قصصهم», in the well-known reading, referring to the messengers alone, and he related that it may refer to Joseph and his brothers. Others related that it may refer to the messengers and to Joseph and his brothers all together. The Shaykh said: "And it — meaning this reading — does not support it, since the story of Joseph, his father and his brothers comprises many stories and various reports."
His saying: {مَا كَانَ حَدِيثاً}: in «كان» there is a pronoun referring to the Quran, i.e. the Quran, which contains this wondrous story, was not a fabricated discourse. It is also said: rather it refers to «القصص», i.e. the story mentioned in His saying «لقد كان في قَصَصِهم» was not … Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: then to what does the pronoun in {مَا كَانَ حَدِيثاً يفترى} go back, for whoever read it with kasra? I say: to the Quran, i.e. the Quran was not a discourse…". I say: because had it referred to «قِصصهم» with kasra on the qāf, it would have had to be «كانت» with the tāʾ, since the verb would then be predicated of a feminine pronoun, even if it is figuratively feminine.
His saying: {ولكن تَصْدِيقَ}: the generality read «تصديق» and the three after it in the accusative (manṣūb), as coordinated to the khabar (predicate) of «كان», i.e. "but it was a confirmation". Ḥumrān ibn Aʿyan, ʿĪsā al-Kūfī and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read «تصديق» and what follows it in the nominative (marfūʿ), as predicates of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "but it is a confirmation", i.e. the discourse is one of confirmation. The like of this has been heard from the Arabs in both the accusative and the nominative. Dhū al-Rumma said:
2836 - وما كان مالي مِنْ تُراثٍ وَرِثْتُه ... ولا ديةً كانَتْ ولا كَسْبَ مأثمِ
ولكنْ عطاءَ اللَّه من كل رحلةٍ ... إلى كل محجوبِ السُّرادِقِ خِضْرَمِ
(My wealth was not from an inheritance I inherited, nor was it blood-money, nor the gain of sin; but rather the gift of Allah from every journey to every generous lord screened behind his pavilion.)
And Lūṭ ibn ʿUbayd said:
2837 - وإني بحمد اللَّه لا مالَ مسلمٍ ... أخذْتُ ولا مُعْطي اليمينِ مُحالِفِ
ولكنْ عطاء اللِّهِ مْنِ مالِ فاجرٍ ... قَصِيِّ المحلِّ مُعْوِرٍ للمَقارفِ
(And I, praise be to Allah, took neither the wealth of a Muslim nor of one who gave his right hand as an ally; but rather the gift of Allah from the wealth of a wicked man, far of abode, exposed to those who commit sins.)
«عطاء اللَّه» in both verses is related in the accusative, in the sense "but it was the gift", and in the nominative, in the sense "but it is the gift of Allah". The parallel of what remains of the sura has preceded, which makes repeating it unnecessary.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَضْغَاثُ}: «أَضْغاث» is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هي أضغاث» (they are jumbles), meaning what you have narrated to us; and the clause is accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
And «الأضغاث» is the plural of «ضِغْث» with kasra on the ḍād: it is what is gathered of plants, whether of one kind or of mixed kinds, and it is smaller than a bundle and larger than a handful. Of its occurring for a single kind are the words of Allah the Exalted: {وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثاً} [Ṣād: 44]; it is related in the exegesis that he took a fruit-stalk (عِثْكال) of a palm. And in the ḥadīth: "A sick man upon whom a ḥadd punishment was due was brought to him, and that was done to him." And Ibn Muqbil said:
2797 - خَوْدٌ كأن فِراشَها وُضِعَتْ به ... أضغاثُ رَيْحانٍ غَداةَ شَمَالٍ
(A delicate young woman — as if bunches of sweet basil had been laid on her bed on a morning of the north wind.)
And of its occurring for mixed plants is their saying among their proverbs: «ضِغْثٌ على إبَّالة» (a handful of grass on top of a bundle of firewood). Al-Zamakhsharī restricted it to what is gathered of mixed plants, saying: "The origin of «الأَضْغاث» is what is gathered of mixed plants and bundles; the singular is «ضِغْث»." And al-Rāghib said: "«الضِّغْث» is a handful of sweet basil, grass or twigs." I say: it has preceded that it is more than a handful. The use of «الأَضْغاث» here is by way of metaphor (istiʿāra). And the iḍāfa (genitive construction) in «أَضْغاث أحلام» is an iḍāfa in the sense of «مِنْ», since the implied form is «أضغاثٌ من أحلام» (jumbles of dreams).
And «الأَحْلام» is the plural of «حُلُم». And the bāʾ in «بتأويل» is attached to «عالمين», while the one in «بعالمين» is attached to nothing because it is redundant (zāʾida), either in the khabar of the Ḥijāzī [«ما»] or of the Tamīmī.
Their saying this may be a denial of knowledge of dreams absolutely, or it may be a denial of knowledge of the interpretation of the jumbles among them specifically, not of the sound dream. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "[It means] «بتأويل أضغاث الأحلام» (in the interpretation of jumbled dreams); that is necessary, [because they did not claim ignorance of the interpretation of dreams]." End of quotation. As for His saying «الأحلام» [in the plural] when it was only one, al-Zamakhsharī said: it is as you say "So-and-so rides horses and wears turbans of silk-wool" of someone who rides only one horse and wears only one turban, [as an embellishment in description]; and it is possible that he narrated to them other dreams along with this one.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وادكر}: there are two views on it. The more apparent of them: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause, either from the relative noun or from its resumptive pronoun, which is the fāʿil (agent) of «نجا». The second: that it is conjoined to «نجا», so it has no grammatical position, being conjoined to what has no position.
The majority read «ادَّكَرَ» with a doubled undotted dāl; its origin is «اذْتَكَرَ», the iftiʿāl form from «الذِّكر». The tāʾ of iftiʿāl came after the dhāl, so it was changed to dāl; then two close sounds came together, so the first was changed to the kind of the second and assimilated. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read it with a dotted dhāl. They explained it as his having changed the tāʾ to a dhāl of the kind of the first [letter] and assimilated. The same rule applies in {مُّدَّكِرٍ} [al-Qamar: 15], as will come in its sūra, if Allah the Exalted wills.
The majority read «أُمَّة» with ḍamma on the hamza, a doubled mīm and a tāʾ with tanwīn; it is a long period of time. Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī read it with kasra on the hamza, and they explained it as "favour", i.e. after a favour bestowed upon him, namely his release from prison and his deliverance from being killed. Al-Zamakhsharī recited, by ʿAdī:
2798 - ثم بعد الفَلاَح والمُلْكِ والإِمْ ... مَةِ وارَتْهُمُ هناك القبورُ
(Then, after prosperity, kingship and good fortune, the graves there concealed them.)
And another recited:
2799 - ألا لا أرى ذا إمَّةٍ أصبحَتْ به ... فَتَتْركه الأيامُ وهي كما هيا
(Lo, I see no one possessed of good fortune who has it in the morning, and then the days leave him with it as it was.)
And Ibn ʿAbbās, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Abū Rajāʾ read «أَمَهٍ» with fatḥa on the hamza, an undoubled mīm and a hāʾ with tanwīn, from «الأَمَه», which is forgetfulness; one says «أَمِهَ يَأْمَهُ أَمَهاً وأمْهاً» with fatḥa on the mīm and with sukūn, the sukūn not being analogical.
And Mujāhid, ʿIkrima and Shubayl ibn ʿAzra read «بعد أَمْهٍ» with sukūn on the mīm; it has preceded that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of «أَمِه» contrary to analogy. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Whoever reads with sukūn on the mīm has been declared mistaken." The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is according to his habit of attributing error to the readers." I say: he did not himself attribute error to them; he only related that some declared this reader mistaken, for he said «خُطِّىء» in the passive form and did not say "he has erred"; moreover, if it is authentic that the one he mentioned read thus, there is no way at all to attribute error to him. And «بعد» is accusative by «ادَّكر».
His words: {أَنَاْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ}: this clause is what is reported by the saying. The majority read it from «الإنباء» (informing). And al-Ḥasan read «أنا آتيكم», the imperfect of «أتى», from «الإتيان» (coming), which is close in meaning to the first.

semin-durr:46-46.t: And «الصِّدِّيق» is an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha), like «الشِّرِّيب» (the heavy drinker).

semin-durr:47-47.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {تَزْرَعُونَ}: its apparent sense is that this is a statement of fact from Yūsuf, upon him be peace. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«تَزْرعون» is a statement in the sense of a command, like His words: {تُؤْمِنُونَ بالله وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُجَاهِدُونَ} [al-Ṣaff: 11]. A command is put in the form of a statement only to emphasise the obligation of the thing commanded upon the one commanded, so it is treated as though it already existed and he is reporting it. The proof that it is in the sense of a command is His words: {فَذَرُوهُ فِي سُنبُلِهِ}." The Shaykh said: "The command to leave it in its ears does not prove that «تزرعون» is in the sense of «ازرعوا» (sow!); rather «تَزْرعون» is a report of the unseen, and as for «فَذَرُوه», it is a command of advice about what they ought to do." I say: this is the apparent view, and his commanding them to sow has no place here, because they would sow according to their custom whether he commanded them or not; a command is needed only for what it is not a person's custom to do, such as leaving it in its ears.
His words: {دَأَباً}: Ḥafṣ read it with fatḥa on the hamza, and the rest with sukūn; they are two dialectal forms of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «دَأَب يَدْأَبُ», i.e. he persisted in a thing and kept to it. This is as they said «ضَأْن» and «ضَأَن», «مَعْز» and «مَعَز», with fatḥa on the ʿayn and with sukūn. There are several views on its accusative. The first, the view of Sībawayh: that it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being «تَدْأَبون» (you persist). The second, the view of Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad]: that it is accusative by «تزرعون», because it is of its meaning, so it is of the type of «قَعَدْتُ القُرْفُصاء» (I sat squatting). There is a reservation about this, because it is not a kind specific to it, unlike «القرفصاء» with sitting. The third: that it occupies the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), so it admits the well-known views: either hyperbole, or its occupying the place of an adjective, or the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. «دائِبين» (persisting) or «ذوي دأب» (people of persistence), or treating them as persistence itself by way of hyperbole. The discussion of «الدأب» has preceded in Āl ʿImrān at His words: {كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ} [verse: 11].
His words: {فَمَا حَصَدتُّمْ}: «ما» may be conditional or relative. And Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «يأكلون» in the third person, i.e. the people; and it may be an iltifāt (shift of person).

semin-durr:48-48.t: And the words of Allah the Exalted: {سَبْعٌ شِدَادٌ}: the specifier, which is the thing described, was omitted because what preceded indicates it. And eating was attributed to them [the years] figuratively, as in His words: {والنهار مُبْصِراً} [Yūnus: 67]: since the eating and the seeing take place in them, they were treated as though they were performed by them.

semin-durr:49-49.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {يُغَاثُ الناس}: the alif may be from a wāw or from a yāʾ: either from «الغَوْث», which is relief, its verb being quadriliteral — one says «أغاثَنا اللَّه» (Allah relieved us), from «الغَوْث»; or from «الغَيْث», which is rain — one says «غِيْثَتِ البلاد», i.e. the lands were rained upon, its verb being triliteral — one says «غاثنا اللَّه» from «الغَيْث». A Bedouin woman said: «غِثْنا ما شِئْنا», i.e. we were rained upon as much as we wished.
His words: {يَعْصِرُونَ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «تَعْصِرون» in the second person, and the rest with the yāʾ of the third person; both are clear, since both an addressee and an absent party have preceded, so each reading refers to what suits it. And «يَعْصِرون» admits several views. The most apparent: that it is from pressing grapes, olives or the like. The second: that it is from «عَصَر الضَّرْع» when he milked it. The third: that it is from «العُصْرة», which is deliverance, and «العَصَر» is a place of refuge. Abū Zubayd said about ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him:
2800 - صادِياً يَسْتغيث غيرَ مُغَاثٍ ... ولقد كان عُصْرَة المَنْجودِ
(Thirsting, calling for help, yet not helped — and he had been the refuge of the distressed.)
This view is supported by its correspondence with His words {فِيهِ يُغَاثُ الناس}; one says «عَصَره يَعْصِرُه», i.e. he delivered him.
Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad and al-Aʿraj read «يُعْصَرون» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, and ʿĪsā al-Baṣra with the upper-dotted tāʾ; in both readings it is passive. In these two readings there are two interpretations. One: that it is from «عَصَره» when he delivered him; al-Zamakhsharī said: "And it corresponds to the relief (الإغاثة)." The second, stated by Quṭrub: that it is from «الإعصار», which is a cloud's raining down water, as in His words: {وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ المعصرات} [al-Nabaʾ: 14]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And «يُعْصَرون» has been read, [meaning] they are rained upon, from «أَعْصَرَتِ السَّحابة» (the cloud poured rain). There are two views on it: either «أَعْصَرت» is made to imply the meaning of «مُطِرَتْ» and is made transitive as that is; or it is said that the original is «أُعْصِرَتْ عليهم», then the preposition was omitted and the verb made to reach [their pronoun directly; or the pouring is attributed to them figuratively, so they were made «مُعْصَرين»]."
And Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «تِعِصِّرون» with kasra on the tāʾ and the ʿayn and a doubled ṣād; its origin is «تَعْتصرون»: the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād, the ʿayn was made to follow the ṣād [in vowel], and then the tāʾ was made to follow the ʿayn. Its full treatment has preceded at {أَمَّن لاَّ يهدي} [Yūnus: 35].
And al-Naqqāsh transmitted the reading «يُعَصِّرون» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, fatḥa on the ʿayn and kasra on the doubled ṣād, from «عَصَّر», for multiplicity. This reading and the earlier reading of Zayd may both be from pressing plants or the udder, or from deliverance, as in the words of the other:
2801 - لو بغيرِ الماءِ حَلْقي شَرِقٌ ... كنت كالغَصَّانِ بالماءِ اعتصاري
(Were my throat choked by something other than water, [I would wash it down with water]; but I am like one choking on water itself — [where then is] my relief?)
i.e. my deliverance.

semin-durr:50-50.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {مَا بَالُ النسوة}: the majority read the nūn of «النسوة» with kasra, and ʿĀṣim gave it ḍamma in the transmission of Abū Bakr [Shuʿba] from him, though it is not the well-known one; Abū Ḥaywa also read it so. And «اللائي» has been read [for «اللاتي»]; both are plurals of «التي».

semin-durr:51-51.t:
And «الخَطْبُ» is a matter or affair in which there is gravity. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
2802 - وما المَرْءُ ما دامَتْ حُشاشَةُ نفسِه ... بمُدْرِكِ أَطْرافِ الخُطوبِ ولا آلِ
(A man, as long as the last breath of his soul remains, will neither reach the ends of [life's] grave affairs nor fall short [of striving].)
It is originally the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «خَطَب يَخْطُبُ», and one speaks out (يُخْطب) only about great matters.
His words: {إِذْ رَاوَدتُنَّ}: this adverb is accusative by His words «خَطْبُكُنَّ», because it is in the sense of a verb, since the meaning is: what did you do, and what did you intend by it, at that time?
His words: {الآن حَصْحَصَ}: «الآن» is accusative by what comes after it. And «حَصْحَصَ» means: it became clear and appeared after being hidden; al-Khalīl said this. Some said: it is taken from «الحِصَّة» (share), and the meaning is: the share of truth became distinct from the share of falsehood, just as the shares of lands and the like are distinguished. And it was said: in the sense of "it became established and settled". Al-Rāghib said: "«حَصْحَصَ الحقُّ», and that is by the uncovering of what overwhelms it; «حَصَّ» and «حَصْحَصَ» are like «كَفَّ» and «كَفْكَفَ», «كَبَّ» and «كَبْكَبَ». And «حَصَّه»: he cut it off, either by direct action or by judgement. Of the first is the poet's saying:
2803 - قد حَصَّتِ البيضة رأسي. . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The helmet has shorn my head [bald]…)
And from it: «رَجُلٌ أَحَصُّ», a man some of whose hair has been cut off, and «امرأة حَصَّاءُ». And «الحِصَّة» is a portion of the whole, and it is used as «النصيب» (share) is used." And it was said: it is from «حَصْحَصَ البعير», when the camel puts down its callused knees in order to kneel. The poet said:
2804 - فَحَصْحَصَ في صُمِّ الصَّفَا ثَفِناتِه ... وناءَ بسلمى نَوُءَةً ثم صَمَّما
(He pressed his callused knees into the hard rocks, rose with Salmā in one heave, then pressed on resolutely.)

semin-durr:52-52.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {ذلك}: the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «الأمر ذلك» (the matter is that). And «ليعلم» is attached to an implied word, i.e. Allah made that manifest so that he may know. Or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. that which I have declared about his innocence is a matter from Allah that is inevitable, and «لِيَعْلمَ» is attached to that khabar. Or «ذلك» is the object of an implied verb, to which this preposition phrase is also attached, i.e. Allah did that, or I did it by Allah's facilitation, so that he may know.
His words: {بالغيب}: the bāʾ may be locative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "That is, in the place of absence, which is concealment and being hidden behind the seven locked doors." And the bāʾ may be for the ḥāl (circumstantial): either from the agent, in the sense of "while I was absent from him, hidden from his eye", or from the object, in the sense of "while he was absent from me, hidden from my eye". This is [on the view that it is] from the words of Yūsuf, and al-Zamakhsharī began with it as though it were his preferred view. Others said: it is from the words of the wife of al-ʿAzīz, and that is the apparent view. And His words «وأنَّ اللَّه» are conjoined to «أني», i.e. so that he may know both matters.

semin-durr:53-53.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِلاَّ مَا رَحِمَ}: there are several views on it. The first: that it is excepted from the latent pronoun in «أمَّارَةٌ», as though it were said: "the soul is indeed ever-commanding to evil, except a soul on which my Lord has mercy"; so by «النفس» He meant the genus, and that is why the exception from it is admissible, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: {إِنَّ الإنسان لَفِى خُسْرٍ إِلاَّ الذين آمَنُواْ} [al-ʿAṣr: 2-3]. Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, for he said: "Except the part on which my Lord has mercy through protection from sin, like the angels." There is a reservation about this, in that «ما» is applied to rational beings, whereas the well-known usage is otherwise.
The second: that «ما» is in the sense of time, so it is excepted from the implied general time. The meaning is: the soul is indeed ever-commanding to evil at every time and moment except the time of my Lord's mercy upon it through protection. Abū al-Baqāʾ compared it to the words of Allah the Exalted: {وَدِيَةٌ مُّسَلَّمَةٌ إلى أَهْلِهِ إِلاَّ أَن يَصَّدَّقُواْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 92]. It has preceded that the majority do not permit «أنْ» to occupy the place of an adverb of time.
The third: that it is excepted from the object of «أمَّارة», i.e. ever-commanding its possessor to evil, except the one on whom Allah has mercy. This too involves applying «ما» to a rational being.
The fourth: that it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "And it is the view of the majority." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And it may be a disconnected exception, i.e. but the mercy of my Lord is what averts evil-doing, as in His words: {وَلاَ هُمْ يُنقَذُونَ إِلاَّ رَحْمَةً مِّنَّا} [Yā-Sīn: 23]."
[Translator's note: the verse cited is in Yā-Sīn 43-44, not 23, as written in the source.]

semin-durr:54-54.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُ}: the fāʿil (agent) may be the pronoun of the king and the object the pronoun of Yūsuf, upon him be peace, and that is the apparent view; and the reverse is also possible.

semin-durr:56-56.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِيُوسُفَ}: regarding this lām, it may be attached to «مَكَّنَّا», on the view that the object of «مَكَّنَّا» is omitted, its implied form being «مَكَّنَّا لِيوسفَ الأمورَ» (We established matters for Yūsuf), or on the view that the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is «حيث», as will come. And it may be redundant (zāʾida) according to those who hold that; it has preceded that the majority refuse that except in two situations.
His words: {يَتَبَوَّأُ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from «يوسف». And «منها» may be attached to «يَتَبوَّأ»; and Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl from «حيث».
And «حيث» may be an adverb of «يَتَبَوَّأ», and it may be a mafʿūl bihi; its full treatment has preceded in al-Anʿām.
Ibn Kathīr read «نَشَاء» with the nūn, as the nūn of majesty of Allah the Exalted. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted the fāʿil (agent) to be the pronoun of Yūsuf, saying: "because his will is part of the will of Allah"; there is a reservation about this, because the arrangement of the speech refuses it. The rest read it with the yāʾ, as the pronoun of Yūsuf. There is no disagreement that in His words {نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَن نَشَآءُ} it is with the nūn. The Shaykh permitted the agent in the yāʾ reading to be the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, it being an iltifāt (shift of person).

semin-durr:59-59.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {بِجَهَازِهِمْ}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the jīm, and it has been read with kasra; they are two dialectal forms for what a person needs of provisions and goods; from it are «جهاز العروس» (the bride's trousseau) and «جهاز البيت» (household furnishings).
And His words: {بِأَخٍ لَّكُمْ}: He did not say «بأخيكم» with iḍāfa (genitive construction), to emphasise that he did not [show that he] know them; for this reason they distinguish between «مررت بغلامك» (I passed by your servant) and «بغلامٍ لك» (by a servant of yours), for the first requires that you know the servant and that there is some prior acquaintance between you and the person you address, while the second does not require that. One may speak of something definite in the manner of an indefinite, saying "a man said such-and-such" while you know him, because the indefinite can truthfully be applied to the definite.

semin-durr:60-60.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَلاَ تَقْرَبُونِ}: «لا» may be prohibitive, so that «تَقْربون» is jussive (majzūm); or «لا» may be negative, and then there are two views. One: that it falls within the scope of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), conjoined to it, so it is also jussive as has preceded. The second: that it is an independent negation not conjoined to the apodosis of the condition, being a statement in the sense of prohibition, as in His words: {فَلاَ رَفَثَ} [al-Baqara: 197].

semin-durr:62-62.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِفِتْيَانِهِ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read «لفتيانه», and the rest «لفِتْيَتِه». «الفِتْيان» is a plural of multitude (jamʿ kathra), and «الفِتْية» a plural of paucity (jamʿ qilla); so the multitude is in relation to those commanded, and the paucity in relation to those who handled [the goods]. And «فتى» is pluralised as «فِتْيان» and «فِتْيَة»; it has preceded whether «فِعْلَة» among plurals is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) or a broken plural. Like it is «أخ», which is pluralised as «إخْوَة» and «إخوان».
And «يَرْجِعون» may be transitive with its object omitted, i.e. they will return the merchandise, because he knew that of their religion; or it may be intransitive, in the sense of: they will return to us.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «يَكْتَلْ» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, i.e. our brother will get the measure; and the rest with the nūn, i.e. we will get the measure; and it is jussive (majzūm) as the answer to the command.
It is related that in the presence of al-Mutawakkil, or of his vizier Ibn al-Zayyāt, a question arose between al-Māzinī and Ibn al-Sikkīt, namely: what is the morphological pattern of «نَكْتَلْ»? Yaʿqūb [Ibn al-Sikkīt] said: «نَفْتَل»; al-Māzinī mocked him and said: its pattern is only «نَفْتَعِل». This is what I saw in some books, and that is not a mistake, because the morphologists have stated that if a word contains an omission or a substitution, it is omitted or substituted in the pattern; so we say: the pattern of «بِعْتُ» and «قُمْتُ» is «فِعْتُ» and «فُعْتُ», the pattern of «عِد» is «عِل», and the pattern of «ناءَ» is «فَلَعَ»; and if you wish, you give the original. On this basis there is no mistake in his saying "the pattern of «نَكْتَلْ» is «نَفْتَلْ»", because he considered the actual form, not the original. And I saw in some books that he said «نَفْعَل» with the ʿayn, and that is a sheer mistake. Yet the apparent state of Yaʿqūb is that he had not mastered this; had he mastered it, he would have said: its pattern according to the original is such-and-such, and according to the actual form such-and-such. That is why al-Māzinī came down hard on him and he gave no reply.

semin-durr:64-64.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِلاَّ كَمَآ أَمِنتُكُمْ}: accusative as the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), or as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, i.e. a trusting like my trusting you with his brother; he likened his trusting them with this one to his trusting them with that one. And «من قبلُ» is attached to «أمِنْتُكم».
His words: {فالله خَيْرٌ حَافِظاً}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read «حافظاً», and there are two views on it. The more apparent: that it is a tamyīz (specification). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And the like of this may be put in iḍāfa (genitive construction)." I say: al-Aʿmash read it so: {فاللَّه خيرُ حافظٍ}; and Allah the Exalted is described as having a guarding that exceeds the guarding of anyone else, as when you say «هو أفضل عالم» (he is the most excellent of scholars). The second: that it is a ḥāl; al-Zamakhsharī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and others mentioned that. The Shaykh, who transmitted it from al-Zamakhsharī alone, said: "And it is not good, because it restricts «خير» by this ḥāl." I say: there is nothing objectionable in that, for this ḥāl is permanent, because it is corroborative (muʾakkida), not clarifying (mubayyina), and this is not the first ḥāl to have come as permanent.
The rest read «حِفْظاً», and they permitted nothing in it but the tamyīz, because if they made it a ḥāl it would be an attribute of what «خير» applies to, and it does not apply to what «خير» applies to, because guarding is an abstract notion. But whoever interprets «زيدٌ عَدْلٌ» (Zayd is justice) as hyperbole, or as the omission of a muḍāf, or as the maṣdar occupying the place of an adjective, would also permit the ḥāl reading in «حِفْظاً» by the interpretations mentioned; and there is forcing (taʿassuf) in that.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ}: ʿAlqama, Yaḥyā and al-Aʿmash read «رِدَّتْ» with kasra on the rāʾ, by transferring the vowel of the assimilated dāl to the rāʾ after imagining it to be free of its own vowel; it is the dialect of Banū Ḍabba. Moreover, Quṭrub related from the Arabs the transfer of the vowel of the ʿayn to the fāʾ in sound verbs, so they say «ضِرْب زيدٌ» in the sense of «ضُرِب زيد» (Zayd was struck). That has preceded at His words: {وَلَوْ رُدُّواْ لَعَادُواْ} [verse: 28] in al-Anʿām.
His words: {مَا نَبْغِي}: there are two views on this «ما». The more apparent: that it is interrogative, so it is a fronted object whose fronting is obligatory, because it has the right to head the sentence, i.e. what thing do we seek? The second: that it is negative, and it has two meanings. One: nothing remains for us to seek; al-Zajjāj said this. The second: «ما نبغي» from «البغي» (transgression), i.e. we have not fabricated nor lied about this king regarding his generosity and kindness. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "We do not transgress in speech, nor do we exaggerate in what we have described to you of the king's kindness."
The readers kept this yāʾ in «نبغي» both in continuous reading and in pause, and did not make it one of the additional [optional] yāʾs (al-zawāʾid), unlike the one in al-Kahf, as will come: {قَالَ ذَلِكَ مَا كُنَّا نَبْغِ} [al-Kahf: 64]. The difference is that «ما» there is relative, and its resumptive pronoun has been omitted, and omission makes omission congenial — this is a widespread expression among the people of this craft; they say: change makes change congenial — unlike here, for it is either interrogative or negative, and on neither view is there an omission to make omission congenial.
ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd] and Abū Ḥaywa read, and ʿĀʾisha narrated it from the Prophet ﷺ, «ما تبغي» in the second person. And «ما» also admits both views in this reading.
And the clause in His words: {هذه بِضَاعَتُنَا} may be explicative of their saying «ما نبغي», or it may be resumptive.
His words: {وَنَمِيرُ}: conjoined to the nominal clause before it; and if «ما» is negative, it may be conjoined to «نَبْغي», so that it is the conjoining of a verbal clause to its like. ʿĀʾisha and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «ونُمير» from «أماره» when he provided provisions for him; one says «ماره يَميره» and «أماره يُمِيْره». And «المِيرة» is the bringing of provisions. [The poet] said:
2805 - بَعَثْتُكَ مائِراً فمكَثْت حَوْلاً ... متى يأتي غِياثُكَ مَنْ تُغِيْثُ
(I sent you out to bring provisions, and you stayed away a whole year — when will your relief reach those you are to relieve?)
And «البعير» linguistically applies to the male specifically, though some applied it to the she-camel as well and made it parallel to «إنسان» [which covers both sexes]. Its bāʾ may be given kasra to follow its ʿayn. It is pluralised, in the plural of paucity, as «أبْعِرَة», and in the plural of multitude as «بُعْران».

semin-durr:66-66.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لَتَأْتُنَّنِي بِهِ}: this is the answer to the oath implied in His words «مَوْثِقاً», because it is in the sense of: until you swear to me that you will surely bring him to me.
His words: {إِلاَّ أَن يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ}: there are several views on this exception. The first: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ); Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. He means that the implied form of the speech would be: but if you are surrounded, you are free from my reproach and my anger at you if you do not bring him to me, because your excuse is clear.
The second: that it is connected (muttaṣil), being an exception from the general mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: tell me the true nature of this exception, for there is a difficulty in it — I say: {أَن يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ} is a mafʿūl lahu, and the affirmative speech, which is His words «لَتأْتُنَّني به», is in the sense of negation, its meaning being: you shall not refrain from bringing him except because of your being surrounded; or: you shall not refrain from it for any reason whatever except one reason, namely that you are surrounded. So it is an exception from the most general of the general in the mafʿūl lahu, and exception from the most general of the general occurs only in negation, so it must be interpreted as negation. Its parallel in an affirmative interpreted in the sense of negation is their saying «أقسمتُ باللَّه لمَّا فعلتَ وإلا فعلت» (I adjure you by Allah, you shall do it, [I ask nothing] but that you do it), meaning: I ask nothing of you but the doing." Because of the clarity of this view he mentioned no other.
The third: that it is excepted from the most general of the general in states. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its implied form is: you shall surely bring him to me in every state, except in the state of your being surrounded." I say: they have stated that «أنْ» which puts the verb in the subjunctive does not occupy the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), even though, being interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), [one might think] it could occupy the place of a ḥāl; for they do not tolerate in the interpreted maṣdar what they tolerate in the explicit one: they permit «جئتُك رَكْضاً» (I came to you running) but do not permit «جئتك أن أركضَ», even though it is in its sense.
The fourth: that it is excepted from the most general of the general in times, the implied form being: you shall surely bring him to me at every time, not at the time of your being surrounded. There has preceded a disagreement on this question, and that Abū al-Fatḥ [Ibn Jinnī] permitted it, just as it is permitted with the explicit maṣdar: just as you say «أتيتُكَ صِياحَ الدِّيك» (I came to you at the cock's crowing), he permits «أنْ يَصيح الديك». He counted among this the words of Taʾabbaṭa Sharran:
2806 - وقالوا لا تَنْكِحيهِ فإنَّه ... لأَِوَّلِ نَصْلٍ أن يُلاقِيَ مَجْمعا
(They said: do not marry him, for he is [destined] for the first blade, when he meets a gathering [of foes].)
and the words of Abū Dhuʾayb al-Hudhalī:
2807 - وتاللَّهِ ما إنْ شَهْلَةٌ أمُّ واجدٍ ... بأوجدَ مني أن يُهانَ صغيرُها
(By Allah, no grey-eyed old mother in grief is more grieved than I, when her little one is humiliated.)
He said: "Its implied form is: at the time of his meeting the gathering, and at the time of the humiliation of her little one." The Shaykh said: "According to what he said, the verse may be construed [thus], and «لتأتُنَّني به» remains in its apparent affirmative sense." I say: what is apparent from this is that it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), and whenever it is emptied it must be interpreted as negation.
Ibn al-Anbārī prohibited that with «أنْ» and also with «ما». He said: "So you may say «خروجُنا صياح الديك» (our departure is at the cock's crowing), but you may not say «خروجُنا أن يصيحَ» or «ما يصيح الديك»; what is tolerated in the explicit [maṣdar] is not tolerated in the interpreted one." This is analogous to what I stated earlier about prohibiting «أنْ» and what is in its scope from occupying the place of a ḥāl. But you may distinguish between the two in that the ḥāl must be indefinite, whereas «أنْ» and what is in its scope — they have stated that it is on the level of a pronoun in definiteness — so this is incompatible with its occupying the place of a ḥāl; unlike the adverb, for its indefiniteness is not a condition, so there is nothing to prevent «أَنْ» and what is in its scope from occupying its place.

semin-durr:68-68.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَلَمَّا دَخَلُواْ مِنْ حَيْثُ}: there are three views on the answer of this «لمَّا». The first, which is the apparent one: that it is the negated clause in His words: {مَّا كَانَ يُغْنِي}. In this there is an argument for those who claim that «لمَّا» is a particle, not an adverb, since if it were an adverb its answer would govern it, as nothing else is fit to govern it; but what comes after negative «ما» does not govern what precedes it: «حين قام أخوك ما قام أبوك» (when your brother stood, your father did not stand) is not permissible, while «لمَّا قام أخوك ما قام أبوك» is permissible.
The second: that its answer is omitted. Abū al-Baqāʾ supplied it as: "they complied and fulfilled their father's need", and Ibn ʿAṭiyya also inclined to that; it is forced (taʿassuf), because the speech contains what is an explicit answer, as I stated.
The third: that the answer is His words «آوى». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And it is the answer of both the first and the second «لمَّا», as when you say «لمَّا جِئْتني، ولمَّا كَلَّمْتك أَجَبْتَني» (when you came to me, and when I spoke to you, you answered me); what makes that good is that their entering upon Yūsuf, upon him be peace, follows their entering by the gates." He means that «آوى» is the answer of the first and the second, and that is clear.
His words: {إِلاَّ حَاجَةً}: there are two views on it. One: that it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), its implied form being: but a need in the soul of Yaʿqūb which he fulfilled; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. The second: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned nothing else, and the implied form would be: it was not the definiteness, so this is incompatible with its occupying the place of a ḥāl, unlike the adverb, for its indefiniteness is not a condition, so there is nothing to prevent «أَنْ» and what is in its scope from occupying its place.
[Translator's note: the source text is corrupted here: the sentence breaks off and a fragment from the end of the discussion of verse 66 is inserted, after which the whole entry is repeated from the beginning. The text is translated as it stands.]
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَلَمَّا دَخَلُواْ مِنْ حَيْثُ}: there are three views on the answer of this «لمَّا». The first, which is the apparent one: that it is the negated clause in His words: {مَّا كَانَ يُغْنِي}. In this there is an argument for those who claim that «لمَّا» is a particle, not an adverb, since if it were an adverb its answer would govern it, as nothing else is fit to govern it; but what comes after negative «ما» does not govern what precedes it: «حين قام أخوك ما قام أبوك» is not permissible, while «لمَّا قام أخوك ما قام أبوك» is permissible.
The second: that its answer is omitted. Abū al-Baqāʾ supplied it as: "they complied and fulfilled their father's need", and Ibn ʿAṭiyya also inclined to that; it is forced, because the speech contains what is an explicit answer, as I stated.
The third: that the answer is His words «آوى». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And it is the answer of both the first and the second «لمَّا», as when you say «لمَّا جِئْتني، ولمَّا كَلَّمْتك أَجَبْتَني»; what makes that good is that their entering upon Yūsuf, upon him be peace, follows their entering by the gates." He means that «آوى» is the answer of the first and the second, and that is clear.
His words: {إِلاَّ حَاجَةً}: there are two views on it. One: that it is a disconnected exception, its implied form being: but a need in the soul of Yaʿqūb which he fulfilled; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. The second: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned nothing else, and the implied form would be: it did not avail them for any reason whatsoever except for the sake of a need that was in the soul of Yaʿqūb. And the fāʿil (agent) of «يُغْني» is the pronoun of the dispersal indicated by the preceding speech. In what Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted there is a reservation as regards meaning, which is not hidden from one who reflects on it. And «قضاها» is a naʿt (adjective) of «حاجةً».

semin-durr:70-70.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {جَعَلَ السقاية}: the majority read «جَعَل» without an added wāw before it. ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd] read «وجَعَلَ», and that admits two views. One: that the answer [of «لمَّا»] is omitted. The second: that the wāw is redundant (zāʾida) in the answer, according to the opinion of those who hold that, namely the Kufans and al-Akhfash. The Shaykh said: "ʿAbd Allāh read, according to what al-Zamakhsharī transmitted, «وجعل السِّقاية في رَحْل أخيه: أمهلهم حتى انطلقوا ثم أذَّن مؤذِّن» (and he put the drinking-cup in his brother's saddlebag — he gave them respite until they set off, then a crier called out); and in the transmission of Ibn ʿAṭiyya, «وجعل» with an added wāw in «جَعَل», without the addition that al-Zamakhsharī added after His words {فِي رَحْلِ أَخِيهِ}. So it is possible that the wāw is redundant according to the school of the Kufans, and possible that the answer of «لمَّا» is omitted, its implied form being: its keeper missed it — as it was said: Yūsuf was only inspired to put the drinking-cup [there], then its keeper missed it and called out according to his own opinion about what appeared to him; al-Ṭabarī preferred that. But the searching of the bags refutes this view."
I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not transmit all this addition as a reading from ʿAbd Allāh; he only made the addition mentioned after His words «رَحْل أخيه» a supplied answer of his own. This is his text — al-Zamakhsharī said: "And Ibn Masʿūd read «وجَعَل السِّقاية» on the omission of the answer of «لمَّا», as though it were said: so when he had furnished them with their provisions and put the drinking-cup in his brother's saddlebag, he gave them respite until they set off, then a crier called out." So this from al-Zamakhsharī is only a supplied form, not a recitation transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh; perhaps the Shaykh had a faulty copy.
And «السِّقاية» is an oblong vessel from which one drinks, and it is «الصُّواع»; the exegetes have a long disagreement about it.
His words: {أَيَّتُهَا العير}: a vocative from which the vocative particle has been omitted. «العِيْر» is feminine, and for that reason «أيّ», by means of which it is addressed, came [in the feminine]. There are two views on «العِيْر». One: that it is originally a group of camels, so called because they «تَعِيْر», i.e. go and come with it. The second: that it is originally a caravan of donkeys, as though it were the plural of «عَيْر», and «العَيْر» is the donkey. [The poet] said:
2808 - ولا يُقيم على ضَيْمٍ يُرادُ به ... إلا الأَذَلاَّن عَيْرُ الحَيِّ والوَتِدُ
(None abides an injustice intended against him except the two most abject: the tribe's donkey and the tent-peg.)
The original is «عَيْر» and «عُيْر» with ḍamma on the ʿayn; then the same was done to it as was done to «بِيض», whose original is «بُيْض» with ḍamma on the first letter.
