Then «العِير» came to be applied to every caravan, whether of donkeys or otherwise. On every interpretation, the attribution of the call to it is figurative, because the one actually addressed is its people. Al-Zamakhsharī compared it to the saying: «يا خيلَ اللَّهِ اركبي» (O horses of Allah, mount!), except that in this verse He turned to the omitted muḍāf in His words «إنكم لسارقون», whereas in «يا خيل اللَّه اركبي» it was not turned to; had it been turned to, it would have said «اركبوا». And it is possible that its people are expressed [by its name] because of contiguity, so that it is not a figure of omission but a figure based on relationship (majāz al-ʿalāqa).
The Arabs one and all pluralise it as «عَيَرات» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, and this is among what is agreed to be anomalous, because «فِعْلَة» with a weak ʿayn, when pluralised with alif and tāʾ, properly has its ʿayn vowelless, e.g. «قِيمة» and «قِيْمات», «دِيْمة» and «دِيْمات»; likewise «فَعْل» without a yāʾ [i.e. without the feminine ending], when pluralised, properly has its ʿayn vowelless. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
2809 - غَشِيْتُ ديارَ الحي بالبَكَرَاتِ ... فعارِمَةٍ فبُرْقَةِ العِيَراتِ
(I came upon the tribe's abodes at al-Bakarāt, then ʿĀrima, then Burqat al-ʿIyarāt.)
Al-Aʿlam al-Shantamarī said: "«العِيَرات» here are the places of the «أَعْيار», which are donkeys." I say: in «عِيَرات» there is another anomaly, namely pluralising it with alif and tāʾ while it is also pluralised as «أعْيار» in a broken plural; they have stated that. It was said: for that reason al-Mutanabbī was faulted for his words:
2810 - إذا كان بعضُ الناسِ سَيْفاً لدولةٍ ... ففي الناسِ بُوْقاتُ لهم وطبولُ
(If some people are a sword for a dynasty, then among people there are trumpets and drums for them too.)
They said: he pluralised «بوق» as «بوقات» although they give it the broken plural «أبواق».
[Translator's note: the source writes «عَيَرات» with fatḥa on the ʿayn at first and «العِيَرات» with kasra in the verse and after it; both are translated as written.]

semin-durr:71-71.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَأَقْبَلُواْ عَلَيْهِمْ}: this clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «قالوا», i.e. they said, having turned towards them — meaning in the state of their turning towards them.
His words: {مَّاذَا تَفْقِدُونَ}: the discussion of this question has preceded at the beginning of this work. The majority read «تَفْقِدون» with fatḥa on the imperfect prefix, because what is used from it is the triliteral «فَقَد». Al-Sulamī read it with ḍamma, from «أَفْقَدْتُه» when you find it missing, like «أَحْمَدْته» and «أَبْخَلْتُه», i.e. I found him praiseworthy, stingy. Abū Ḥātim declared this reading weak; its justification is what I have mentioned.

semin-durr:72-72.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {صُوَاعَ}: it is the measuring vessel, and it is the drinking-cup (السِّقاية) mentioned earlier; He called it sometimes this and sometimes that. This vessel was taken as a measure only because of the scarcity of what was measured with it at that time. There are many readings of it, all of them dialectal forms of this word, and it is treated as masculine and feminine:
The majority read «صُواع» on the pattern of «غُراب», with an undotted ʿayn. Ibn Jubayr and al-Ḥasan read the same, except with a dotted ghayn. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read the same [with ghayn], except that he dropped the alif and made the wāw vowelless. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «صَوْغ» likewise, except that he gave the ṣād fatḥa, making it the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «صاغ يَصُوغ» (to fashion), and the two readings before it are derived from it; it occupies the place of a passive participle, i.e. that which was fashioned for the king. Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Jubayr and al-Ḥasan, in one transmission from them, read «صِواع» like the majority, except that they gave the fāʾ [the first radical] kasra.
Abū Hurayra and Mujāhid read «صَاعَ» on the pattern of «باب», its alif being like that one's in being changed from a wāw with fatḥa. Abū Rajāʾ read «صَوْعَ» on the pattern of «قَوْسٍ». ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwn read the same, except that he gave the fāʾ ḍamma. These are eight readings, of which [only] one is mutawātir (mass-transmitted).

semin-durr:73-73.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {تالله}: the tāʾ is a particle of oath, and according to the majority it is a substitute for the wāw of oath; for that reason it is prefixed only to the holy Name of Majesty (الله), or to «الربّ» in iḍāfa to the Kaʿba, or to «الرحمن» according to a weak view. If you said «تالرحيم» it would not be permissible. It is a derivative of a derivative. This is the school of the majority; al-Suhaylī claimed that it is an original in itself. Wonder mostly accompanies it, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: {تَالله تَفْتَؤُاْ} [Yūsuf: 85].
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The tāʾ in «تاللَّه» is a substitute for a wāw, just as it was substituted in «تُراث», in «التوراة» and in «التُّخَمَة»; and the tāʾ does not enter into oaths except with the written [Name] among the names of Allah the Exalted and the like; you do not say «تالرحمن» or «تالرحيم»." You have learned that al-Suhaylī disagreed about its being a substitute for wāw. As for his saying "and in «التوراة»", he means according to the Basrans; some claimed that the tāʾ in it is redundant. As for his saying "except with the written [Name]", this is the well-known view; its entering upon other than that has preceded.
His words: {وَمَا كُنَّا سَارِقِينَ}: it may be [part of] the answer to the oath, so that they will have sworn to two things: the denial of corruption and the denial of theft.
And His words: {مَّا جِئْنَا}: it may suspend (taʿlīq) [the operation of] the knowing; or the knowing itself may be made to imply the meaning of an oath, so it is answered with what an oath is answered with. It was said that these two views apply in the poet's words:
2811 - ولقد عَلِمْتُ لَتَأْتِيَنَّ مَنِيَّتي ... إنَّ المَنايا لا تَطيشُ سِهامُها
(I know well that my death will surely come; the arrows of the fates do not miss.)

semin-durr:74-74.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَمَا جَزَآؤُهُ}: the hāʾ refers to the measuring vessel (الصُّواع), and a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. what is the penalty for stealing it? And for «إنْ كنتم», its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) may be omitted or [may have] preceded.

semin-durr:75-75.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {جَزَآؤُهُ مَن وُجِدَ}: there are four views. The first: that «جزاؤه» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the pronoun referring to the thief, and «مَنْ», conditional or relative, is a second mubtadaʾ; the fāʾ [in «فهو»] is [the fāʾ of] the apodosis of the condition, or is added in the khabar (predicate) of the relative because of its resemblance to the condition; and «مَنْ» with what is in its scope, on either of its two views, is the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this, and it is rejected because there is no link (rābiṭ) between the mubtadaʾ and the clause that is its khabar; thus did the Shaykh refute it against him. But [the refutation] is not apparent, because it can be answered that this question is of the type of putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun. This becomes clear through al-Zamakhsharī's exposition. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: "And «جزاؤه» may be a mubtadaʾ, and the conditional clause as it stands its khabar, on the basis of putting the overt noun in it in the place of the pronoun. The original is: «جزاؤه مَنْ وُجِدَ في رحله فهو هو» (its penalty: whoever it is found in his saddlebag, he is it); so «الجزاء» was put in the place of «هو», as when you say to your companion «مَنْ أخو زيد؟» (who is Zayd's brother?), and he says to you «أخوه مَنْ يقعد إلى جنبه، فهو هو» (his brother is whoever sits beside him — he is he), the first pronoun referring to «مَنْ» and the second [to] the brother; then you say «فهو أخوه», putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun."
The Shaykh made this that I have related from al-Zamakhsharī a second view after the first, and did not believe it to be the very same, nor that it is an answer to what he refuted Ibn ʿAṭiyya with. Then he said: "Putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun for linking is eloquent only in contexts of magnification and interpretation, and is not eloquent elsewhere, e.g. «زيدٌ قام زيد» (Zayd, Zayd stood), and the Qurʾān is to be kept free of it. Sībawayh said: 'If you said «كان زيدٌ منطلقاً زيد», it would not be the proper form of speech; it would be weak here, and it would not be like your saying «ما زيدٌ منطلقاً هو», because you have no need to state it overtly; you should only make it a pronoun.'" I say: the school of al-Akhfash is that it is permissible absolutely, and on that al-Zamakhsharī built.
Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted something that he imagined to be an answer to that. He said: "The third view: that «جزاؤه» is a mubtadaʾ, «مَنْ وُجد» a second mubtadaʾ, «فهو» a third mubtadaʾ, and «جزاؤه» the khabar of the third; the resumptive to the first mubtadaʾ is the last hāʾ, and to the second «هو»." End of quotation. This that Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned is not sound, since the implied meaning becomes: "so the one in whose saddlebag it is found is the penalty of the penalty", because he made «هو» an expression for the second mubtadaʾ, which is {مَن وُجِدَ فِي رَحْلِهِ}, and made the last hāʾ, which is the one in the last «جزاؤه», refer to the first «جزاؤه», so the implied meaning became as I have stated to you.
The second of the views mentioned: that «جزاؤه» is a mubtadaʾ, the hāʾ referring to the stolen object, and {مَن وُجِدَ فِي رَحْلِهِ} is its khabar, «مَنْ» meaning «الذي» (the one who); the implied form is: the penalty for the measuring vessel is the one in whose saddlebag it is found. Such was their law: the thief would be enslaved; that is why they were asked for a ruling on its penalty.
"And His words «فهو جزاؤه» are an affirmation of the ruling, i.e. the taking of the thief himself is its penalty and nothing else, as when you say: Zayd's due is to be clothed and fed and favoured, «فذلك حَقُّه» (that is his due), i.e. it is his due, to affirm what you mentioned of his entitlement and make it binding." Al-Zamakhsharī said this. When Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this view he said: "The implied form is: the enslavement of the one in whose saddlebag it is found; and His words «فهو جزاؤه» are a mubtadaʾ and khabar, corroborating the meaning of the first."
When the Shaykh mentioned this view, transmitting it from al-Zamakhsharī, he said: "Ibn ʿAṭiyya stated its meaning, except that he made the one view into two views. He said: 'And «مَنْ» may properly be a khabar, on the meaning: the penalty of the thief is the one in whose saddlebag it is found, [the pronoun] referring to «مَنْ», and His words «فهو جزاؤه» are additional clarification and emphasis.' Then he said: 'And the implied form may be: its penalty is the enslavement of the one in whose saddlebag it is found.' In what precedes it [this supplying] is also necessary, because an entity cannot be the khabar of a maṣdar (verbal noun); so the implied form in the view before it is: its penalty is the taking of the one in whose saddlebag it is found, or his enslavement; this is necessary on this analysis." I say: this is as the Shaykh said: its apparent sense is that he made the one view into two views.
The third of the views mentioned: that «جزاؤه» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "what is asked about is its penalty"; then they gave their ruling by saying «مَنْ وُجِد في رَحْله فهو جزاؤه», just as one who seeks a ruling on the penalty for game killed by a person in iḥrām says "the penalty for game killed by one in iḥrām", and then [the ruling] says: {وَمَن قَتَلَهُ مِنكُم مُّتَعَمِّداً فَجَزَآءٌ مِّثْلُ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ النعم} [al-Māʾida: 95]. Al-Zamakhsharī said this. The Shaykh said: "It is contrived, since the clause «المسؤول عنه جزاؤه», on this analysis, has little benefit in it, since it was already known from his saying «فما جزاؤه» that the thing asked about is the penalty for stealing it, so what benefit is there in their uttering that? The same applies to the example he gave of the words of the one seeking a ruling."
I say: his saying "it has little benefit in it" is not conceded; rather it has the benefit of the ellipsis (iḍmār) mentioned in the science of rhetoric (ʿilm al-bayān), and the Qurʾān contains the like of that.
The fourth view: that «جزاؤه» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "its penalty among us is like its penalty among you", the hāʾ referring to the thief or to the stolen object, and the preceding speech contains an indication of both; and His words «مَنْ وُجِدَ في رَحْله فهو جزاؤه» are as in the view before it. Abū al-Baqāʾ began with this view, and the Shaykh did not mention it. So he [the Shaykh] made four views in the noble verse, and it has preceded that the first and the second are one view, as I have explained. If we add this last view, with which Abū al-Baqāʾ began, to the four the Shaykh mentioned, they become five; but there is no precision in that. Likewise, if we take into account Ibn ʿAṭiyya's making the one view into two, they become six in wording; but when you examine them precisely they come to only four, as I have stated them to you.
His words: {كذلك نَجْزِي الظالمين}: the position of the kāf is accusative: either as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, or as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from its pronoun, i.e. like that terrible penalty We penalise the wrongdoers.

semin-durr:76-76.t:
The majority read «وِعاء» with kasra on the wāw, and al-Ḥasan read it with ḍamma, which is a dialectal form also transmitted from Nāfiʿ. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read «مِنْ إعاء», changing the wāw to a hamza; it is a Hudhalī dialect: they change a wāw with kasra at the beginning of a word into a hamza, saying «إشاح», «إسادة» and «إعاء» for «وشاح», «وِسادة» and «وِعاء». That has preceded, regarding the glorious Name of Majesty, at the beginning of this work.
His words: {ثُمَّ استخرجها}: there are two views on the accusative pronoun. One: that it refers to the measuring vessel (الصُّواع), because it is treated as both masculine and feminine, as has preceded. And it was said: rather, because it was construed according to the sense of «السقاية». Abū ʿUbayd said: "«الصُّواع» is treated as feminine in so far as it is called «سقاية», and as masculine in so far as it is «صُواع»." They said: it seems Abū ʿUbayd did not know of the feminine usage of «الصُّواع». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "They said: He referred back with the feminine to «السِّقاية»." Then he said: "Perhaps Yūsuf used to call it «سِقاية» and his servants «صُواع», so in the speech connected with him it occurs as «سقاية», and in what is connected with them as «صواع»." I say: this last is good.
The second: that the pronoun refers to «السَّرِقة» (the theft). There is a reservation about this, because a theft is not extracted, except figuratively.
His words: {كذلك كِدْنَا}: the discussion of the kāf is like the discussion of the one before it, i.e. like that great stratagem We devised for Yūsuf, i.e. We taught it to him. And His words: {مَا كَانَ لِيَأْخُذَ} are an explanation and clarification of the stratagem; that is because in the law of the king of Egypt the thief was fined twice what he took, not that he was seized and enslaved.
His words: {إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ الله}: there are two views on it. One: that it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), its implied form being: but by the will of Allah he took him under a law other than the king's, namely the law of the family of Yaʿqūb, that enslavement is the penalty of the thief. The second: that it is an emptied exception (mufarragh) from the general states, the implied form being: he would not take him in any state except in the state of its being bound up with the will of Allah, i.e. His permission for that.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya's words admit [either], for he said: "The exception is a narration of a state; the implied form is: unless Allah wills what took place of this stratagem."
The two readings in {نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَّن نَّشَآءُ} have preceded [at verse 83] in al-Anʿām. Yaʿqūb read with the lower-dotted yāʾ in «يرفع» and «يشاء», the agent being Allah the Exalted. ʿĪsā al-Baṣra read «نَرْفع» with the nūn, «درجات» with tanwīn, and «يشاء» with the yāʾ. The author of al-Lawāmiḥ said: "This is a reading that is shunned in recitation and altogether, even though it cannot be denied." I say: its justification is that in His words «يشاء» there is an iltifāt (shift of person) from the first person to the third, the referent being one.
His words: {وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ}: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read «وفوق كل ذي عالم», and there are three views on it. The first: that «عالم» here is a maṣdar (verbal noun) — they said: like «الباطل», for it is a maṣdar — so it is like the well-known reading. The second: that there is an omitted muḍāf there, its implied form being «وفوقَ كلِّ ذي مُسَمَّى عالم» (above every possessor of what is named "knower"), as in the words of Labīd:
2812 - إلى الحَوْلِ ثم اسمِ السَّلامِ عليكما ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(For a year; then the name of peace be upon you both…)
i.e. what is named "peace". The third: that «ذو» is redundant (zāʾida), as in the words of al-Kumayt:
2813 - إليكم ذوي آلِ النبيِّ. . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(To you, O family of the Prophet…)
— the verse.

semin-durr:77-77.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَقَدْ سَرَقَ}: the majority read «سَرَق» undoubled and active. Aḥmad ibn Jubayr al-Anṭākī, Ibn Abī Shurayḥ from al-Kisāʾī, and al-Walīd ibn Ḥassān from Yaʿqūb, among others, read «سُرِّق» doubled and passive, i.e. he was accused of theft. In the exegesis: his paternal aunt raised him, and his father took him from her; so she tied around his waist a belt which they had inherited from Ibrāhīm, upon him be peace; then they searched and found it under his clothes. She said: "He is mine," and she took him, as was their law. This reading fits this [account].
His words: {فَأَسَرَّهَا}: the accusative pronoun is explained by the context of the speech, i.e. he concealed the resentment that arose in him from their saying {فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَّهُ}, as in the poet's words:
2814 - أما وِيَّ ما يُغْني الثَّراء عن الفتى ... إذا حَشْرَجَتْ يوماً وضاق بها الصدرُ
(O Māwiyy, wealth avails a young man nothing when one day it [his soul] rattles in his throat and his chest is constricted by it.)
The pronoun in «حَشْرَجَتْ» refers to the soul. So the Shaykh mentioned it; but he [elsewhere] made the verse among those in which the pronoun is explained by the mention of what is a whole of which the pronoun's referent is part, so it would not be among those in which it is explained by the context. The precise treatment of this has another place.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a pronoun used on condition of explanation (iḍmār ʿalā sharīṭat al-tafsīr); its explanation is {أَنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَّكَاناً}. It was made feminine only because His saying «شَرٌ مكاناً» is a sentence (jumla), or a 'word' (kalima), according to their calling a portion of speech a kalima; as though it were said: he concealed the sentence or the word which is his saying {أَنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَّكَاناً}; because His words {قَالَ أَنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَّكَاناً} are a badal (substitute) from «أَسَرَّها»." I say: this is according to those who make an overt noun a substitute from a pronoun in other than the nominative, e.g. «ضربته زيداً» (I struck him, Zayd); and the correct view is that it occurs, as in his words:
2815 - فلا تَلُمْهُ أن يَخافَ البائسا ...
(So do not blame him — the wretched one — for being afraid.)
ʿAbd Allāh and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «فَأَسَرَّه» in the masculine. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He means the saying or the speech." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The pronoun refers to their ascribing theft to him, which the speech indicates. And it was said: there is a fronting and postponement in the speech, its implied form being: he said within himself: you are worse in position — and he concealed it, i.e. this word." I say: the like of this ought not to be said, for the Qurʾān is to be kept free of it.
His words: {مَّكَاناً}: a tamyīz (specification), i.e. in standing, compared with others than you.

semin-durr:78-78.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {مَكَانَهُ}: there are two views on it. One, which is the apparent one: that «مكانَه» is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and the governing word in it is «خُذْ». The second: that «خُذْ» is made to imply the meaning of «اجْعَلْ» (make), so that «مكانَه» is in the position of the second object. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "So take him in his stead by way of pledge or enslavement."

semin-durr:79-79.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِنَّآ إِذاً}: this [«إذاً»] is a particle of answer and requital; the discussion of its rules has preceded.

semin-durr:80-80.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {استيأسوا}: the form istafʿala here is in the sense of the bare form faʿila; one says «يَئِس» and «استيئس» with one meaning, like «عَجِب» and «استعجب», «سَخِر» and «استسخر» [Translator's note: the source prints «استخسر», apparently a misprint for «استسخر»]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The addition of the sīn and tāʾ is for intensification, as in what has passed regarding «استعصم»."
Al-Bazzī read from Ibn Kathīr, with a disagreement [in the transmission] from him, «اسْتَاْيَسوا» with an alif after the tāʾ and then a yāʾ; likewise in this sūra «لا تايَسوا», «إنه لا يايَس», «إذا اسْتايَسَ الرسلُ», and in al-Raʿd «أفلم يايَسِ الذين»; the disagreement is the same. As for the reading of the majority, it is the original, since one says «يَئِس», the fāʾ [first radical] being yāʾ and the ʿayn [second radical] hamza. There is another dialectal form, namely metathesis (qalb), by putting the ʿayn before the fāʾ, so one says «أَيِس». Two things indicate this: first, the maṣdar (verbal noun), which is «اليَأْس»; second, that if it were not metathesised, the yāʾ would have to be changed into an alif because it is vowelled with a fatḥa before it; but what prevented that is that the yāʾ is in a position in which what occupies its position is not weakened. The reading of Ibn Kathīr is from this [metathesised form]; and when he metathesised the word, he changed the hamza into an alif because it was vowelless after a fatḥa, since it had become like the hamza of «رَأْس» and «كأس», even though it is not part of his system to change a vowelless hamza into a weak letter. This is as has preceded, that he reads «القرآن» with the alif, and that it is possible that he transferred the vowel of the hamza, even though transfer is not part of his system.
Abū Shāma, after mentioning these five words in which the disagreement occurs, said: "And thus were they written in the Muṣḥaf", meaning as al-Bazzī read them, i.e. with an alif in place of the yāʾ and a yāʾ in place of the hamza. And Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: "These words differ in their written form: «يابَس» [Translator's note: so in the source, for «يايَس»] and «ولا تايَسُوا» were written with the alif, and the rest were written without alif." I say: this is the correct view; it seems to be an oversight that occurred on the part of Abū Shāma, may Allah have mercy on him.
His words: {نَجِيَّاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «خَلَصوا», i.e. they withdrew in this state. The ḥāl was made singular while its owner is plural either because «النَّجِيّ» is faʿīl in the sense of mufāʿil, like «العشير» and «الخليط» in the sense of «المُخالِط» and «المُعاشِر», as in His words: {وَقَرَّبْنَاهُ نَجِيّاً} [Maryam: 52], i.e. conversing privately — and in usage this is made singular absolutely: one says «هم خليطُكَ وعَشيرُكَ», i.e. your associates and companions; or because it is an adjective on the pattern faʿīl like «صَديق», and «صديق» and its class are kept singular because they are on the pattern of maṣdars, like «الصَّهيل», «الوَجيب» and «الذَّمِيل»; or because it is a maṣdar in the sense of «التناجي» (private conversation), as «النجوى» is said with its meaning — Allah the Exalted said: {وَإِذْ هُمْ نجوى} [al-Isrāʾ: 47] — and in that case it admits the interpretations mentioned for «رجل عَدْل» and its class. It is pluralised as «أَنْجيَة», whereas, if it were made an adjective, it would properly be pluralised as «أفْعِلاء», like «غَنِيّ» and «أَغْنِياء», «شَقِيّ» and «أَشْقِياء». Of its occurring as «أَنْجية» is the poet's saying:
2816 - إنِّي إذا ما القومُ كانوا أَنْجِيَهْ ...
(When the people have gathered in private conclaves, I…)
and the saying of the other, namely Labīd:
2817 - وشَهِدْتُ أَنْجِيَةَ الأَفَاقةِ عالياً ... كَعْبي وأَرْدَافُ المُلوكِ شُهودُ
(I attended the conclaves of al-Afāqa, my standing high, while the kings' deputies were present.)
Its being pluralised thus strengthens its being a primitive noun (jāmid), since it becomes like «رغيف» and «أَرْغِفَة».
His words: {وَمِن قَبْلُ مَا فَرَّطتُمْ}: in this verse there are six views. The first, which is the most apparent: that «ما» is redundant (zāʾida), so the adverb is attached to the verb after it, the implied form being «ومِنْ قبلِ هذا فَرَّطْتم» (and before this you fell short), i.e. you fell short regarding Yūsuf's right and his affair. The addition of «ما» is frequent; al-Zamakhsharī and others began with this.
The second: that «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is the preceding adverb. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "On the basis that the position of the maṣdar is nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is the adverb, which is «مِنْ قبل»; the meaning is: your falling short regarding Yūsuf took place before." Ibn ʿAṭiyya also inclined to this, for he said: "And His words «مِنْ قَبلُ» cannot be attached to «ما فَرَّطْتُمْ»; on this [view] it is only maṣdariyya, the implied form being: before, your falling short regarding Yūsuf [was] occurring or settled; and to this implied word His words «مِنْ قبل» are attached." The Shaykh said: "This and al-Zamakhsharī's view come back to one meaning, namely that «ما فَرَّطْتُمْ» is construed as a maṣdar nominative as mubtadaʾ, and «مِنْ قبل» is in the position of the khabar. They both overlooked an Arabic rule — and they deserved to overlook it — namely that these adverbs which are 'limits' (ghāyāt), when made indeclinable, do not occur as khabars of a mubtadaʾ, whether they take a genitive or not. You say «يومُ السبت مباركٌ، والسفر بعده» (Saturday is blessed, and the journey is after it), but you do not say «والسفر بعدُ»; [you say] «عمرو وزيد خلفَه», but «زيد وعمرو خلفُ» is not permissible. According to what they both mentioned, «تفريطكم» would be a mubtadaʾ and «من قبل» a khabar [while being indeclinable], and that is not permissible; it is established in the science of Arabic."
I say: his saying "and they deserved to overlook it" is unfair towards these two men, whose standing in knowledge is well known. As for his saying that the adverb cut off [from its genitive] does not occur as a khabar, that is conceded; they said: because it conveys no benefit, and what conveys no benefit does not occur as a khabar; for that reason it does not occur as a ṣila (relative clause), an adjective or a ḥāl either: if you said «جاء الذي قبلُ» or «مررت برجل قبلُ», it would not be permissible, for the reason I mentioned. But someone might say: it is disallowed only because of the absence of benefit, and the absence of benefit is due to the absence of knowledge of the omitted muḍāf ilayhi; so when the muḍāf ilayhi is known and indicated, that adverb in iḍāfa to that omitted [word] ought to be able to occur as a khabar, adjective, ṣila and ḥāl; and the noble verse is of this kind, I mean of those in which the muḍāf ilayhi is known, as has been set out. Moreover, this refutation with which the Shaykh refuted them was anticipated by Abū al-Baqāʾ, who said: "And this is weak, because «قبل», when it occurs as a khabar or ṣila, is not cut off from iḍāfa, lest it remain incomplete."
The third: that it is also maṣdariyya, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is His words «في يوسف», i.e. and your falling short is existent or settled regarding Yūsuf. Al-Fārisī held this; it seems he sensed that the cut-off adverb does not occur as a khabar and so turned to this. There is a reservation about it, because the context and the meaning run towards «في يوسف» being attached to «فَرَّطْتُم», so holding what al-Fārisī said leads to preparing the governing word to govern and then cutting it off from it.
The fourth: that it is also maṣdariyya, but its position is accusative, being conjoined to {أَنَّ أَبَاكُمْ قَدْ أَخَذَ}, i.e. did you not know of your father's taking the covenant and of your falling short regarding Yūsuf? Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As though it were said: did you not know of your father's taking from you a pledge, and of your falling short before regarding Yūsuf?" Ibn ʿAṭiyya also held this.
The Shaykh said: "What they both held is not good, because it involves separating, by a preposition and its genitive noun, between a conjunction consisting of one letter and the conjoined word, so it becomes parallel to «ضربتُ زيداً وبسيفٍ عمراً» (I struck Zayd, and with a sword ʿAmr); and Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī claimed that this is not permissible except under poetic necessity." I say: this refutation too was anticipated by Abū al-Baqāʾ, who did not approve of it and said: "And it was said: it is weak because it involves separating between the conjunction and the conjoined word; but we have shown in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ that this is of no account." I say: he means that the prohibition of separating between the conjunction and the conjoined word is of no account; its clarification and exposition have preceded in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, as Abū al-Baqāʾ indicated.
Then the Shaykh said: "As for al-Zamakhsharī's implied form «وتفريطكم من قبل في يوسف», it is not permissible, because it involves putting the governed word of a maṣdar resolvable into an infinitival particle and verb before it, and that is not permissible." I say: there is nothing of that in al-Zamakhsharī's implied form, because when he stated the implied word explicitly he placed the two prepositional phrases after the word of the implied maṣdar, as you see; so it is in all the copies, and so it is in what the Shaykh transmitted from him in his own hand. So where is the fronting of the governed word before the maṣdar? Had he refuted him and Ibn ʿAṭiyya by saying that this entails putting the governed word of the ṣila before the relative, it would have been a clear refutation, for «من قبلُ» is attached to «فَرَّطْتُم» and has preceded the maṣdariyya «ما», and there is a well-known disagreement about that.
The fifth: that it is also maṣdariyya, its position being accusative by conjunction to the noun of «أنَّ», i.e. did you not know that your father [took…] and that your falling short before was regarding Yūsuf? In that case there are two views on the khabar of this implied «أنَّ»: one is «من قبلُ», and the other is «في يوسف»; Abū al-Baqāʾ chose this, and what applies to each of the two has preceded. This fifth view is refuted by what the one before it was refuted by, namely the separation between the conjunction and the conjoined word, and what there is in that is known.
The sixth: that it is a nominal relative («ما» in the sense of «الذي»), its position being nominative or accusative as has preceded for the maṣdariyya. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In the sense of: and before this, that which you fell short in, i.e. what you put forward regarding Yūsuf's right of wrongdoing; its position is nominative or accusative on the two views."
I say: by the two views he means its being nominative as mubtadaʾ with its khabar «من قبل», and its being accusative by conjunction to the object of «ألم تعلموا», for he mentioned nothing else for the maṣdariyya. You have learned what was objected against both of them and what was said in reply. So in sum there are three views on «ما»: redundancy, its being maṣdariyya, or its being in the sense of «الذي»; and that its position admits two views: nominative or accusative. The detail of all that has preceded.
His words: {فَلَنْ أَبْرَحَ الأرض}: «بَرِحَ» here is complete (tāmma), made to imply the meaning of «أفارق» (I leave), so «الأرض» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It cannot be complete without implication of another meaning, because if it were so, its meaning would be "appeared" or "went away" — from it is «بَرِح الخَفاء», i.e. [the secret] came out or [concealment] went away — and the meaning of appearing does not fit, while going away does not reach a specific place-adverb except by means of «في»: you say «ذهبت في الأرض», and «ذهبت الأرض» is not permissible, though something has occurred [thus] on which no analogy is made. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And it may be an adverb." I say: it is possible that the word «لا» has dropped out of the copies, and that it was: "and it cannot be an adverb".
Know that «أبرح» cannot be incomplete (nāqiṣa) here, because a mubtadaʾ and khabar cannot be formed from the pronoun in it and «الأرض»; do you not see that if you said «أنا الأرض» it would not be permissible without «في», unlike «أنا في الأرض» and «زيد في الأرض»?
His words: {أَوْ يَحْكُمَ الله}: there are two views on its accusative. One, which is the apparent one: its being conjoined to «يَأْذَن». The second: that it is accusative by an implied «أنْ» in answer to the negation, which is His words «فلن أبرح», i.e. I will not leave the land unless He judges, as in their saying «لأَلْزَمَنَّكَ أو تقضيني حقي» (I will stick to you until you pay me my due), i.e. unless you pay me. The Shaykh said: "Its meaning and the meaning of the limit are close to each other." I say: the meaning is not on the second; rather the course of the meaning is on its conjunction to «يَأْذن», for he set two limits to the matter: one of them specific, namely the permission of Allah, and the second general, because Allah's permitting him to depart is part of Allah's judgement.

semin-durr:81-81.t:
The majority read «سَرَقَ» active and undoubled; and Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Razīn and al-Kisāʾī, in one transmission, read «سُرِّق» passive and doubled; the justification of both has preceded.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «سارِق», making it an active participle.

semin-durr:82-82.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَسْئَلِ القرية}: it admits three views. The first, which is the well-known one: that it is on the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being «واسأل أهلَ القرية وأهلَ العير» (ask the people of the town and the people of the caravan); it is a widespread figure (majāz). Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others said this. I say: this is subject to a disagreement on the question: is ellipsis (iḍmār) a kind of figurative usage or something else? The well-known view is that it is a category of it, and most people hold this. Abū al-Maʿālī said: "One of the theologians said: 'This is of omission and not of figurative usage; [figurative usage is only] a word borrowed for other than what it is [set] for.'" He said: "But the omission of the muḍāf is the very essence of figurative usage and its greater part; this is the school of Sībawayh and others," and he related that it is the view of the majority. Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī said: "Figurative usage and ellipsis are two divisions, not two co-divisions, so they are mutually distinct." [Translator's note: the source reads «قسمان لا قسيمان»; the conclusion "so they are mutually distinct" would fit better with the reverse wording, but it is translated as written.]
The second: that it is figurative, but of the type of applying the name of the place to what occupies it, because of contiguity, like «الزاوية» (the corner, used for the one sitting in it).
The third: that it is literal, with no figure in it; that is because it is possible that he should ask the town itself and the camels and that they should answer him, because he is a prophet for whom inanimate things and beasts may be made to speak.

semin-durr:83-83.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ}: this iḍrāb (turning away with «بل») must have speech preceding it from which it turns away; the implied form is: the matter is not in reality as you have mentioned; rather [your souls] have enticed [you]. The explanation of the like of this and what follows it has preceded.

semin-durr:84-84.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {ياأسفى}: the alif is changed from the yāʾ of the first person; it was changed to an alif only because the voice is fuller with it. Addressing it [grief] is figurative, as though he said: this is your time, so be present, like {ياحسرتا} [al-Zumar: 56]. And it was said: this is the alif of lamentation (nudba), and the hāʾ of pause was omitted in continuous reading. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The paronomasia (tajānus) between the two words «الأسف» and «يوسف» is among what occurs naturally, not contrived, so it is graceful and original; similar to it are: {اثاقلتم إِلَى الأرض أَرَضِيتُمْ} [al-Tawba: 38], {يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَيَنْأَوْنَ عَنْهُ} [al-Anʿām: 26], {يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ} [al-Kahf: 104], {مِن سَبَإٍ بِنَبَإٍ} [al-Naml: 22]." I say: this kind is called "morphological paronomasia" (tajnīs al-taṣrīf), namely that two words share a form and are distinguished by a letter that is not in the other; it has preceded.
Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid read «مِن الحَزَن» with two fatḥas, Qatāda with two ḍammas, and the majority with ḍamma and sukūn. «الحُزْن» and «الحَزَن» are like «العُدْم» and «العَدَم», «البُخْل» and «البَخَل»; as for the two ḍammas, the second is vowel harmony (itbāʿ).
And «كظيم» may be an intensive in the sense of an active participle (fāʿil), or it may be in the sense of a passive participle (mafʿūl), as in His words: {وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ} [al-Qalam: 48]; al-Zamakhsharī explained it so.

semin-durr:85-85.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {تَفْتَؤُاْ}: this is the answer to the oath in His words «تاللَّهِ», and it is on the omission of «لا», i.e. «لا تَفْتَأ» (you will not cease). What indicates its omission is that if it were affirmative it would be accompanied by both the lām of inception and the nūn of emphasis according to the Basrans, or by one of them according to the Kufans. You say «واللَّهِ أحبُّك» meaning «لا أحبك» (by Allah, I do not love you); and this is of the type of tawriya (double entendre), for the minds of many people hasten to [understand] an affirmation of love. «تَفْتأ» here is incomplete (nāqiṣa), in the sense of «لا تزال» (you still continue), so it puts the noun, which is the pronoun, in the nominative, and puts the khabar (predicate), which is the clause in His words «تَذْكُرُ», in the accusative, i.e. you will not cease remembering him. One says «ما فتىء زيدٌ ذاهباً» (Zayd did not cease going). Aws ibn Ḥajar said:
2818 - فما فَتِئَتْ حتى كأنَّ غبارَها ... سُرادِق يومٍ ذي رياحٍ تُرَفَّعُ
(They [the horses] did not cease, until their dust was like a pavilion raised on a windy day.)
And he also said:
2819 - فما فَتِئَتْ خيلٌ تَثُوْبُ وتَدَّعي ... ويَلْحَقُ منها لاحِقٌ وتُقَطَّعُ
(Horsemen did not cease to return and call out their battle-cries; some of them would catch up, and some fall behind.)
And from Mujāhid: «لا تَفْتُر» (you will not slacken). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as though he made «الفُتوء» and «الفُتور» brothers."
There are two dialectal forms of it: «فَتَأَ» on the pattern of «ضَرَب», and «أَفْتَأَ» on the pattern of «أكرم». It may be complete (tāmma) in the sense of "calmed" and "extinguished"; so said Ibn Mālik, but the Shaykh claimed that this is a misreading on his part, and that it is only «فَثَأ» with the three-dotted thāʾ. This word was written «تفتؤ» with a wāw, while the analogical [spelling] is «تفتأ» with an alif; for that reason, in pause, Ḥamza's [reading] is given both ways, in consideration of the noble script or of analogy.
His words: {حَرَضاً}: «الحَرَض» is being on the verge of death. One says from it «حَرَضَ الرجلُ يَحْرُض حَرَضاً» with fatḥa on the rāʾ, so he is «حَرِض» with kasra on it. So «الحَرَض» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and in the verse there come the views on «رجل عَدْل», which have preceded many times. The maṣdar of this root is applied to bodies in widespread usage, and for that reason the singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine are the same in it: you say «هو حَرَضٌ», «هما حَرَض», «هم حَرَض», «هنَّ حَرَض», «هي حَرَض». And one says «رجل حُرُض» with two ḍammas, like «جُنُب» and «شُلُل». And one says «أَحْرضه كذا», i.e. such-and-such destroyed him. The poet said:
2820 - إني امرؤٌ لَجَّ بيْ حُبٌّ فَأَحْرَضَني ... حتى بَلِيْتُ وحتى شَفَّني السَّقَمُ
(I am a man whom love has persistently beset, and it has brought me to ruin, until I wasted away and sickness wore me thin.)
So he is «مُحْرَض». [The poet] said:
2821 - أرى المَرْءَ كالأذْوادِ يُصبح مُحْرَضاً ... كإحراض بِكْرٍ في الديار مريضِ
(I see a man become, like herds of camels, wasted away — like the wasting of a sick young camel in the encampments.)
Some read «حَرِضاً» with kasra on the rāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And the reading has come with both," meaning with fatḥa on the rāʾ and with kasra. Al-Ḥasan read it with two ḍammas; it has preceded that it is like «جُنُب» and «شُلُل», and al-Zamakhsharī added «غُرُب». Al-Rāghib said: "«الحَرَض» is what is of no account and has no good in it; for that reason what is on the verge of destruction is called «حَرِض». Allah the Exalted said: {حتى تَكُونَ حَرَضاً}. And «قد أحرضه كذا»; the poet said: «أني امرؤ لجَّ» — the verse. And «الحُرْضَة» is one who eats only the meat of maysir [the gambling game] because of his baseness. And «التحريض» is urging to a thing by much embellishment and making the matter seem easy, as though it were the removal of «الحَرَض», like «قَدَّيْتُه», i.e. I removed the mote from it; and «أَحْرَضْتُه»: I spoiled it, like «أَفْذَيْتُه», i.e. you put a mote in it." End of quotation. [Translator's note: the source prints «قَدَّيْتُه» and «أَفْذَيْتُه»; the intended forms are apparently «قَذَّيْتُه» and «أَقْذَيْتُه», from «القذى» (mote).]
And «الحُرُض» is saltwort (al-ushnān, used for washing), because it removes corruption [i.e. dirt]; «المِحْرَضَة» is its container, and its anomaly is like the anomaly of «مُنْخُل», «مُسْعُط» and «مُكْحُلَة».

semin-durr:86-86.t:
And «البَثّ» is the most intense grief, as though, because of its strength, its bearing cannot be endured, so a person «يبثُّه», i.e. disperses and spreads it. It has preceded that the basic sense of this root indicates spreading. Al-Rāghib permitted two views here. One: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of a passive participle. He said: "i.e. my sorrow which I have disclosed after concealment, so it is a maṣdar in the sense of a passive participle; or he means my sorrow which has scattered my thought, so it is in the sense of an active participle."
Al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā read «وحَزَني» with two fatḥas, and Qatāda with two ḍammas; it has preceded.

semin-durr:87-87.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَتَحَسَّسُواْ}: i.e. seek out news of him thoroughly with your senses; it is used for good and evil. And it was said: with the ḥāʾ it is for good, and with the jīm for evil; for that reason He said here «فتحسَّسُوا», and in al-Ḥujurāt: {وَلاَ تَجَسَّسُواْ} [verse: 12]. But it is not so, for it has been read with the jīm here. The disagreement on His words «وَلاَ تَيْأَسُواْ» has preceded. Al-Aʿraj read «تَيْئَسوا».
The majority read «رَوْح اللَّه» with fatḥa, which is His mercy and His relief. Al-Ḥasan, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Qatāda read it with ḍamma on the rāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. of His mercy by which the servants live." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is as though the meaning of this reading is: do not despair of a living person with whom is the spirit (rūḥ) of Allah which He granted, for one whose spirit remains may still be hoped for; and of this is the poet's saying:
2822 - وفي غيرِ مَنْ قدوارَتِ الأرضُ فاطْمَعِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And have hope in anyone except the one whom the earth has already concealed…)
and of this is the saying of ʿAbīd ibn al-Abraṣ:
2823 - وكلُّ ذي غَيْبَةٍ يَؤُوْبُ ... وغائبُ الموتِ لا يَؤُوبُ
(Everyone who is absent returns, but the one absent through death does not return.)
And the reading of Ubayy, may Allah have mercy on him, {مِن رَّحْمَةِ الله}, and {عِنْدِ الله}, {مِن فَضْلِ الله}, is an explanation, not a recitation."
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The majority read it with fatḥa on the rāʾ, and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of mercy, though the use of the verb from it is rare; it is used only with augmentation, like «أراح» and «رَوَّح». It is also read with ḍamma on the rāʾ, which is a dialectal form of it. And it was said: it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), like «الشِّرْب» and «الشُّرْب»."

semin-durr:88-88.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مُّزْجَاةٍ}: i.e. pushed away: everyone pushes it away from himself because of his lack of interest in it. From it is: {أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ الله يُزْجِي سَحَاباً} [al-Nūr: 43], i.e. drives it with the wind. Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī said:
2824 - لِيَبْكِ على مِلْحانَ ضَيْفٌ مُدَفَّعٌ ... وأَرمَلَةٌ تُزْجي مع الليل أَرْمَلا
(Let a guest pushed from door to door weep for Milḥān, and a widow driving along a destitute [child] through the night.)
And one says «أَزْجَيْتُ رديءَ الدرهم فَزُجِيَ» (I passed off the bad dirham and it was passed off); from it was borrowed «زَجَا الخراج يَزْجُو زَجَاءً» (the land-tax was easily collected), and «خَراجٌ زاجٍ», and the poet's saying:
2825 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وحاجةٍ غيرِ مُزْجاةٍ من الحاجِ
(…and many a need, among needs, not to be pushed aside.)
i.e. not a slight one that can be pushed aside and dismissed because of little regard for it. So the alif of «مُزْجاةٌ» is changed from a wāw.
And His words: {فَأَوْفِ لَنَا الكيل}: it may mean its literal sense, the instrument [of measure], or it may mean what is measured, so that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

semin-durr:89-89.t: And the words of Allah the Exalted: {هَلْ عَلِمْتُمْ}: it may be a question for rebuke, and that is the more apparent. And it was said: it is a statement, and «هل» is in the sense of «قد».

semin-durr:90-90.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَإِنَّكَ}: Ibn Kathīr read «إنَّك» with a single hamza, and the rest with two hamzas as a question; you have learned their readings of these two hamzas, with lightening, facilitation (tashīl) and otherwise. As for the reading of Ibn Kathīr, it may be a pure statement; this was considered unlikely in that the two readings would differ while the speaker is one; it was answered that some of them said it as a question and some said it as a statement. And it may be a question from which the particle has been omitted because the context and the other reading indicate it. Something like this has preceded for you in al-Aʿrāf. And in «لأَنْتَ», «أنت» may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «يوسف» its khabar (predicate), the clause being the khabar of «إنَّ», into which the lām of inception has entered. And it may be a separating pronoun (faṣl). It cannot be a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of «إنَّ», because this lām does not enter upon an emphasiser.
Ubayy read «أإنك أو أنت يوسف», and there are two views on it. One is what Abū al-Fatḥ [Ibn Jinnī] said: that the original is «أإنك لغيرُ يوسف أو أنت يوسفُ» (are you other than Yūsuf, or are you Yūsuf?), and the khabar of «إن» was omitted because the meaning indicates it. The second is what al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is «إنك يوسفُ أو أنت يوسف», the first being omitted because the second indicates it; these are the words of one astonished, finding strange what he hears, so he repeats the request for confirmation."
His words: {يَتَّقِ}: Qunbul read «يَتَّقي», keeping the yāʾ in continuous reading and in pause, and the rest omitted it in both. The reading of the majority is clear, because it is jussive (majzūm). As for the reading of Qunbul, people disagreed about it on two views. The better of them: that keeping the weak letter in the jussive [Translator's note: the source has «في الحركة», apparently for «في الجزم»] is a dialect of some Arabs; they recited for that the words of Qays ibn Zuhayr:
2826 - ألم يأتيك والأنباء تَنْمي ... بما لاقَتْ لَبونُ بني زيادِ
(Has it not reached you — and news spreads — what befell the milch-camels of Banū Ziyād?)
and the words of another:
2827 - هَجَوْت زَبَّانَ ثم جِئْتَ مُعْتَذِراً ... مِنْ هَجْوِ زَبَّانَ لم تَهْجُو ولم تَدَعِ
(You satirised Zabbān, then came apologising for satirising Zabbān — you neither satirised nor left off.)
and the words of another:
2828 - إذا العجوزُ غَضِبَتْ فَطَلِّقِ ... ولا تَرَضَّاها ولا تَمَلَّقِ
(If the old woman gets angry, divorce her; do not try to placate her, nor flatter her.)
The school of Sībawayh is that the jussive is by the omission of the implied vowel, and the weak letter only followed it in omission to distinguish between the indicative and the jussive. It was objected to this that the jussive-governing particle shows that it is jussive, and its absence shows that it is not jussive. It was answered that in some cases it causes ambiguity, so the omission was made consistent. The explanation is that if you say «زُرْني أعطيك» (visit me, I give you) with the yāʾ kept, «أعطيك» may be the requital for his visit, or it may be an independent statement; but if you say «أُعْطك» with it omitted, it is determined to be its requital. So the ambiguity arises with the weak letter kept and disappears with its omission. So it is said: the weak letter is omitted at the presence of the jussive-governing particle, not by it. The school of Ibn al-Sarrāj is that the jussive-governing particle affected the letter itself and omitted it; and this is subject to the discussion above.
The second: that it is indicative, not jussive, and «مَنْ» is relative and the verb its ṣila (relative clause); for that reason its final radical was not omitted. It was objected to this that a jussive verb has been conjoined to it, namely His words «ويَصْبِرْ», for Qunbul read it only with sukūn on the rāʾ.
This was answered in that the sukūn is due to a succession of vowels, even if it spans two words, as in the reading of Abū ʿAmr: {يَنصُرْكُمُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 160], {يَأْمُرُكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 67]. It was also answered that it was made jussive by tawahhum (as though [a jussive-governing word] were present), meaning that the relative «مَنْ» resembles the conditional «مَنْ». This is an expression involving an error against the Qurʾān; one ought to say: in it there is regard for the verbal resemblance, and not say "by tawahhum". It was also answered that it was made vowelless for pause, and then continuous reading was treated like pause. It was also answered that it was made jussive only by treating the relative «مَنْ» like the conditional «مَنْ», because it is like it in meaning, and for that reason the fāʾ entered its khabar.
I say: on this [basis] it might be said: «مَنْ» may be conditional, and the yāʾ was kept, and «مَنْ» did not make [the verb] jussive, because of its resemblance to the relative «مَنْ»; then this resemblance was not taken into account in His words «ويَصْبر», so for that reason it made it jussive. But that is far-fetched, in that the governing word would not affect what comes after it and adjoins it, yet would affect what is distant from it. The discussion of a question like this has preceded at the beginning of the sūra, at His words {يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ} [Yūsuf: 12].
And His words {فَإِنَّ الله لاَ يُضِيعُ}: the link between the conditional clause and its apodosis is either the generality in «المحسنين», or an omitted pronoun, i.e. the doers of good among them, or the al standing in its place, the original being «مُحْسِنيهم» (their doers of good); the al stood in the place of that pronoun.

semin-durr:91-91.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {آثَرَكَ}: i.e. He favoured you above us. «الإيثار» is preferring with all kinds of gifts: «آثَره يُؤْثِره إيثاراً». Its root is from «الأَثَر», which is following a thing's track, as though he pursues all kinds of noble qualities thoroughly. In the ḥadīth: «ستكون بعدي أثَرة» (after me there will be selfish preference), i.e. some of you will prefer themselves over others. One says «استأثر بكذا», i.e. he kept it exclusively for himself; and «استأثر اللَّه بفلانٍ» is a metonymy for His choosing him [i.e. his death]. The poet said:
2829 - واللَّه أَسْماك سُماً مبارَكا ... آثرك اللَّه به إيثارَكا
(Allah has given you a blessed name; Allah has favoured you with it, a favouring indeed.)

semin-durr:92-92.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لاَ تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ}: «عليكم» may be the khabar (predicate) of «لا», and «اليومَ» may be attached to what this khabar is attached to, i.e. no reproach is settled upon you today. And «اليوم» may be the khabar of «لا», with «عليكم» attached to what this adverb is attached to. And «عليكم» may be a naʿt (adjective) of the noun of «لا», with «اليوم» again its khabar. It is not permissible for either the adverb or the preposition phrase to be attached to «تَثْريب», because it would then become "extended" (muṭawwal), resembling the muḍāf, and whenever it is so it is declined and given tanwīn, e.g. «لا خيراً مِنْ زيد عندك» (there is none better than Zayd with you). The adverb has an additional [problem]: it would entail separating between the maṣdar (verbal noun), which is construed as a relative, and its governed word by something extraneous, namely «عليكم», because it is either a khabar or an adjective.
Al-Zamakhsharī permitted the adverb to be attached to «تَثْريب», for he said: "If you say: to what is «اليوم» attached? I say: to «التثريب», or to the notion of being settled implied in «عليكم», or to «يَغْفر»." I say: his making it attached to «تَثْريب» is subject to what has preceded. Some treated the governing noun like the muḍāf because of its resemblance to it, so the tanwīn or nūn in it is removed; al-Fārisī counted among this his saying:
2830 - أراني ولا كُفْرانَ للَّه أيَّةً ... لنفسي، لقد طالَبْتُ غيرَ مُنِيْلِ
(I see myself — and no ingratitude to Allah [in saying it], out of pity for myself — that I have sought from one who does not give.)
He said: "«أيَّةً» is accusative by «كُفْران», i.e. I do not deny Allah, out of compassion for myself. And «أيَّةً» cannot be accusative by an implied «أَوَيْت», lest it entail separating between the two objects of «أرى» by two clauses: by «لا» and what is in its scope, and by the implied «أَوَيْت»." The meaning of «أَوَيْت» is "I felt pity". And Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik counted among this what came in the ḥadīth: «لا صَمْتَ يومٌ إلى الليل» (there is no keeping silent for a day until night), with «يومٌ» in the nominative, on the view that it is made nominative by the maṣdar resolvable into an infinitival particle and a passive verb. In some of what has preceded there is disagreement that it is not fitting to take up here.
As for attaching it to the implied notion of being settled, that is clear; for that reason most readers pause at it [«اليوم»] and begin with {يَغْفِرُ الله لَكُمْ}. As for attaching it to «يَغْفر», that is also clear; for that reason some readers pause at «عليكم» and begin with {اليوم يَغْفِرُ الله لَكُمْ}. They also permitted «عليكم» to be for clarification (bayān), like «لك» in «سقياً لك» (may [Allah] water you); on this [view] it is attached to an omitted word. And the khabar of «لا» may be omitted, with «عليكم» and «اليوم» both attached to another omitted word indicated by «تثريب», the implied form being «لا تثريب يَثْرِبُ عليكم اليومَ» (no reproach reproaches you today), as they supplied in {لاَ عَاصِمَ اليوم مِنْ أَمْرِ الله} [Hūd: 43]: «لا عاصمَ يَعْصِم اليومَ» (no protector protects today). The Shaykh said: "If it were held, it would be strong."
But the two may be distinguished in that here it entails much figurative usage: you omit the khabar, you omit this word to which the adverb and the preposition are attached, and you attribute the verb to it [the reproach], because reproach does not reproach except figuratively, like their saying «شعرٌ شاعر» (poetry that is poetic); unlike «عاصم يَعْصِم», for the attribution of the verb to the protector is literal. So there, one thing is omitted without figure; here, two things are omitted together with a figure.
And «التَّثْريب» is blame and rebuke; some expressed it as «التعيير» (taunting), from «عَيَّرته بكذا» when you reproach him for it. In the ḥadīth: «إذا زَنَتْ أَمَةُ أحدِكم فَلْيَجْلِدْها ولا يُثَرِّبْ» (if the slave-woman of one of you commits fornication, let him flog her and not reproach her), i.e. not taunt her. Its root is from «الثَّرْب», which is the fat covering the stomach; its meaning is the removal of the «ثَرْب», just as «التجليد» is the removal of the skin. So if you say «ثَرّبْتُ فلاناً», it is as though, by the severity of your reproach of him, you removed his «ثَرْب»; so it became proverbial for tearing apart people's honour.
Al-Rāghib said: "Nothing is known from its root except their saying «الثَّرْب», which is a thin layer of fat; and His words: {ياأهل يَثْرِبَ} [al-Aḥzāb: 13] — its origin may well be from this class, the yāʾ in it being augmentative."

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ تَقْصُصْ}: The majority read it with the two ṣāds unassimilated, which is the dialect of the Hijaz. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with a single doubled ṣād; assimilation (idghām) is the dialect of Tamīm. The full treatment of this has already been given in al-Māʾida at His saying {وَمَن يَرْتَدِدْ مِنْكُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 54].

And «الرؤيا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like «البُقْيا». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الرؤيا» has the meaning of «الرؤية», except that it is restricted to what occurs in sleep rather than in wakefulness; they distinguished between the two by the two feminine endings, as one says «القُرْبَة» and «القربى»."

The majority read «الرُّؤْيا» with the hamza and without imāla (vowel inclination). Al-Kisāʾī, in the transmission of al-Dūrī from him, read it with imāla. As for «الرؤيا» and «رؤياي», the two occurrences in this sūra, al-Kisāʾī inclined both without disagreement, according to the well-known account, while Abū ʿAmr, by the route of al-Sūsī, replaces this hamza with a wāw. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-Kisāʾī heard «رُيَّاك» and «رِيَّاك», with assimilation and with the rāʾ given ḍamma and kasra. This is weak, because the wāw stands in the place of a hamza, so its assimilation was not strong, just as the assimilation was not strong in «اتَّزر» from «الإزار» and «اتَّجَرَ» from «الأَجْر»." He means that the incidental (ʿāriḍ) is not taken into account, and this is the general rule. Yet the readers did take the incidental into account in places on which you will be informed, if Allah wills, such as «رِيَّا» in His saying {أَثَاثاً وَرِءْياً} [Maryam: 74] according to Ḥamza, and {عَاداً الأولى} [al-Najm: 50].

As for the kasra in «رِيَّاك», it is so that it does not lead to a sukūn yāʾ after a ḍamma; as for the ḍamma, it is the original, and the yāʾ has been absorbed by the assimilation. [Translator's note: the source reads "صد اسْتُهْلِكَتْ"; "قد" is evidently intended.]

His saying: {فَيَكِيدُواْ} is accusative, in the answer to a prohibition, and it stands in the position of a condition and its result; for this reason al-Zamakhsharī implied it as "if you narrate it to them, they will plot against you." As for «كَيْداً», there are two aspects. The first, which is the apparent one, is that it is an emphatic maṣdar. On this, there are five aspects for the lām in His saying «لك». The first: that «يكيد» has been made to include the meaning of a verb that takes its object with lām, because originally it is transitive by itself; the Exalted said: {فَكِيدُونِي جَمِيعاً} [Hūd: 55]; and the implied sense is: "so that they contrive against you with a plot." Al-Zamakhsharī said, confirming this aspect: "If you say: why was it not said «فيكيدوك» as it was said «فكيدوني»? I say: it was made to include the meaning of a verb that takes lām so as to give the meaning of the act of plotting together with the meaning of the verb that is included, and so it is more emphatic and more forceful in intimidation, namely like «فيحتالوا لك» (so that they contrive against you). Do you not see how it is reinforced by the maṣdar?"

The second aspect of the lām: that it is a transitivizing lām, and this verb is among those that take a preposition at times and take their object directly at others, like «نصح» and «شكر». So said al-Shaykh, and there is something to consider in it, because that is a category not open to analogy, restricted only to what the grammarians mentioned, and they did not mention «كاد» among them.

The third: that the lām is redundant on the direct object, like its redundancy in His saying {رَدِفَ لَكُم}. Abū l-Baqāʾ said this, and it is weak, because lām is only added under one of two conditions: that the object precede, or that the governing word be derivative (a secondary form).

The fourth: that the lām is for cause, that is, "so that they plot because of you," and on this the object is omitted, either by restriction (iqtiṣār) or by abbreviation (ikhtiṣār).

The fifth: that it is attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «كَيْداً», since in origin it could have been an adjective had it come after it.

The second of the two aspects of «كَيْداً»: that it is a direct object, that is, "so that they produce for you a plot," meaning a thing with which they plot against you, and it is a maṣdar in the place of a noun; from this is {فَأَجْمِعُواْ كَيْدَكُمْ} [Ṭā Hā: 64], that is, what you plot with. Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it and it is not clear. On this, for the lām in «لك» there are only two aspects: that it is in origin an adjective that then became a ḥāl, or that it is for cause. The remaining three are not possible, and their impossibility is evident.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وكذلك يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّك}: The kāf is in the position of the accusative or the nominative. The accusative is either as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of the implied maṣdar (verbal noun) — and it has already been mentioned that this is the opinion of Sībawayh — or as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, the meaning being: "your Lord will choose you with a choosing like that great choosing." The nominative is as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is: "the matter is thus." Parallels of it have already been given.

His saying: {وَيُعَلِّمُكَ} is resumptive, not included within the scope of the comparison, and the implied form is: "and He teaches you." And «الأحاديث» is a broken plural. It was said to be the plural of a single word that is pronounced, namely «حديث», but its pluralization as «أحاديث» is irregular, and it has sisters in irregularity such as «أباطيل», «أقاطيع» and «أعاريض» (plurals of «باطل», «قطيع» and «عَرُوض»). Abū Zayd claimed that it has an implied singular, namely «أُحْدُوثة» or the like, and that it is not a collective noun (ism jamʿ), because this pattern is specific to broken plurals; and if they were bound to this in cases where no singular of its own wording is explicitly given, such as «عباديد», «شماطيط» and «أبابيل», then in «أحاديث» it is all the more fitting. For this reason al-Zamakhsharī's statement was rejected: "It is a collective noun for «حديث» and is not a plural of «أُحْدوثة»," on the basis of what I have mentioned. But his statement "it is not a plural of «أُحْدوثة»" is correct, because the opinion of the majority is otherwise, although his words may intend by "collective noun" something other than the apparent sense.

His saying: {عَلَيْكَ} may be attached to «يُتِمَّ» and may be attached to «نعمته». And he repeated «على» in "and upon the family of" so that the conjunction on the genitive pronoun would be possible. This is the doctrine of the Basrans, and its explanation has already been given. And his saying «مِنْ قبلُ» means "before you."

His saying: {إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ} may be a badal (substitute) of «أبويك», or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or by the implication of «أعني» ("I mean").

semin-durr:7-7.t: Ibn Kathīr read «آية» in the singular, the intended sense being the genus (jins); the others read it in the plural, stating the intended meaning explicitly because they were many signs. Some claimed that there is an omitted conjoined element here, its implied form being "for those who ask and for others," but there is no need for it. And «للسائلين» is attached to an omitted element, as an adjective of «آيات».

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَحَبُّ إلى أَبِينَا}: «أحبُّ» is an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl). It is formed from «حُبَّ», the passive form, which is irregular. When you form the elative from the root of love (ḥubb) or hate (bughḍ), it is made transitive to the logical agent with «إلى», and to the logical object with lām or with «في». So when you say «زيدٌ أحبُّ إليَّ مِنْ بكر» ("Zayd is dearer to me than Bakr"), you mean that you love Zayd more than Bakr, so the speaker is the agent; and likewise «هو أبغض إليَّ منه» ("he is more hateful to me than he"): you are the hater. And when you say «زيدٌ أحبُّ لي مِنْ عَمْروٍ» or «أَحَبُّ فيَّ منه», it means that Zayd loves me more than ʿAmr does. Imruʾ al-Qays said:

2740 - لَعَمْري لَسَعْدٌ حيث حُلَّت ديارُه ... أحبُّ إلينا منكَ فافرسٍ حَمِرْ
(By my life, Saʿd, wherever his dwellings are pitched, is dearer to us than you — so go off, you wretched ass!)

The noble verse proceeds on this basis, for the father is the agent of the love. And the lām in «ليوسف» is the lām of ibtidāʾ (inception), which gives emphasis to the content of the sentence. His saying «أحبُّ» is the khabar of the dual subject, and it does not agree with it because of what you know of the rule of the elative.

The wāw in «ونحن عصبةٌ» is the wāw of ḥāl, so the sentence after it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. The majority read «عُصْبة» in the nominative as the khabar of «نحن». The Commander of the Faithful read it in the accusative, on the basis that the khabar is omitted and the implied form is "we are seen" or "we gather," so that «عصبة» is a ḥāl, but this is very rare, because the ḥāl does not take the place of the khabar except under conditions mentioned by the grammarians, such as «ضَرْبي زيداً قائماً» and «أكثر شُرْبي السَّوِيْقَ ملتوتاً». Ibn al-Anbārī said: "This is as the Arabs say «إنما العامريُّ عِمَّتَه», that is, 'he wears his turban.'"

Al-Shaykh said: "It is not like it, because «عصبة» is neither a maṣdar nor a manner, so the best is that it be of the category of «حُكْمُك مُسَمَّطاً»." I say: Ibn al-Anbārī intends only the comparison on the ground that he omitted the khabar and something else took its place in cases other than those in which that is regular, with no regard to whether the accusative word is a maṣdar or otherwise. Al-Mubarrad said: "It is of the category of «حُكْمُك مُسَمَّطاً», that is, «لك حكمُك مُسَمَّطاً» (yours is your judgment, unconditional)." Al-Farazdaq said: «يا لَهْذَمُ حُكمك مُسَمَّطاً», meaning: yours is your judgment, unconditional. He said: "This was used so often that it was omitted for lightness, because the meaning intended by the speaker was known, as in your saying «الهلالُ واللَّهِ», that is, 'this is the crescent, by Allah.'" And «المُسَمَّط» is "the sent forth, not turned back." Someone other than al-Mubarrad implied it as «حُكْمُك ثَبَتَ مُسَمَّطاً» ("your judgment stands unconditional"). There is something to consider in this example, because the grammarians make it a condition for the ḥāl to take the place of the khabar that it not be fit to serve as the khabar of that mubtadaʾ, as in «ضربي زيداً قائماً», in contrast to «ضربي زيداً شديدٌ», where it is put in the nominative as khabar and the question falls outside this category. This ḥāl, I mean «مُسَمَّطاً», is fit to be made the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, since the implied sense is "your judgment is sent forth, not turned back"; so this example, on the basis of what I have set out from their speech, would be irregular.

And «العُصْبة» is what exceeds ten, according to Ibn ʿAbbās; and from him also: what is between ten and forty. It was said: three is a «نَفَر»; when it exceeds that up to nine they are a «رَهْط»; when they reach ten and upward, an «عُصْبة». It was said: from one to ten. It was said: from ten to fifteen. It was said: six. It was said: seven. The root indicates encompassing, from «العِصابة» (headband), because it encircles the head.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَرْضاً}: there are three aspects. The first: that it is accusative by the omission of the preposition for lightness, that is, «في أرضٍ» ("in a land"), like His saying, the Exalted: {لأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَاطَكَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 16], and the saying:

2741 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . .
كما عَسَل الطريقَ الثعلبُ
(... as the fox runs along the road.)

Al-Ḥawfī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya held this view. The second: accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "A land indefinite, unknown, far from habitation, and this is the meaning of its indefiniteness and of its being empty of people; and because of its vagueness in this respect it was put in the accusative like the vague adverbials." Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejected this aspect, saying: "That is an error, because the adverbial must be vague, and this is not so; rather it is a land qualified as distant or remote or the like, so its vagueness is gone. And it is known that Yūsuf was never without being in some land, so it is clear that they intended a distant land other than the one in which he was near his father."

Al-Shaykh approved of this rejection and said: "This rejection is correct. If you said «جلست داراً بعيدة» or «مكاناً بعيداً», it would not be sound except by means of «في», and its omission is not permitted except in poetic necessity, or with «دَخَلْت», given the disagreement over «دَخَلْت» as to whether it is intransitive or transitive."

I say: there is something to consider in both statements, since the vague adverbial is an expression for that which has no limits confining it and no regions enclosing it, and «أرضاً» in the noble verse is of this kind.

The third: that it is a second object, which holds if «اطرحوه» includes the sense "lower him," and «أَنْزِلوه» takes two objects; the Exalted said: {أَنزِلْنِي مُنزَلاً مُّبَارَكاً} [al-Muʾminūn: 29]; and you say «أَنْزَلْت زيداً الدار».

And «الطَّرْح» is throwing, and it is used to express plunging into dangers. ʿUrwa ibn al-Ward said:

2742 - ومَنْ يَكُ مثلي ذا عيالٍ ومُقْتِراً ... من المال يَطْرَحْ نفسَه كلَّ مَطْرَحِ
(Whoever is like me, with dependants and short of money, will throw himself into every place of danger.)

And «يَخْلُ لكم» is the answer to the imperative, and it admits both assimilation and non-assimilation, which have already been treated at His saying, the Exalted: {يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الإسلام} [Āl ʿImrān: 85].

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فِي غَيَابَةِ}: Nāfiʿ read «غَيابات» in the plural in both places in this sūra, making that place into parts and naming each part a «غَيَابَة»; the others read it in the singular, which is clear. Ibn Hurmuz read like Nāfiʿ except that he doubled the yāʾ. The most apparent view on this reading is that it was named with the active participle of intensification, so it is originally an adjective. Al-Fārisī classed it with the nouns that come on the pattern «فَعَّال», such as what Sībawayh mentioned of «الفَيَّاد». Ibn Jinnī said: "I found of this «الفَخَّار», meaning pottery." The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "It may be on the pattern «فَعَّالات», like «حَمَّامات», and it may be on «فَيْعالات», like «شيطانات», the plural of «شَيْطانة», and each is for intensification."

Al-Ḥasan read «غَيَبَة» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, and there are two possibilities in it. The first: that it is originally a maṣdar like «الغَلَبة». The second: that it is the plural of «غائب», like «صانع» and «صَنَعَة». Al-Shaykh said: "In the codex of Ubayy it is «غَيْبة» with sukūn on the yāʾ, which is the darkness of the well." I say: vocalization is a later development, so how could that be known in the codex? Something like this has been said before.

And «الغَيَابة»: al-Harawī said: "Something like a recess or niche in the well just above the water, in which what is placed is hidden from the eyes." Al-Kalbī said: "The ghayāba is at the bottom of the pit, because its lower part is wide and its top narrow, so the onlooker can scarcely see what is at its sides." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is its depth and what is hidden from the eye of the onlooker, and the darkest part of its lower portion. Al-Munakhkhal said:

2743 - فإنْ أنا يَوْماً غَيَّبَتْني غَيابتي ... فسِيْروا بسَيْري في العَشيرة والأهلِ
(If one day my «غيابة» hides me, then walk as I walked among the clan and the family.)

He meant the «غيابة» of his grave, in which he is buried. And «الجُبُّ» is the well that has not been lined with stones. It was named so either because it is dug in the «جَبُوب» of the earth, that is, its hard ground, or because it was cut in the earth; from this comes «الجَبُّ» in the male member."

Al-Aʿshā said:

2744 - لَئِنْ كنت في جُبٍّ ثمانين قامَةً ... ورُمِّيْتَ أَسْبابَ السماء بسُلَّمِ
(Even if you were in a pit eighty fathoms deep, and were flung the ropes of heaven by a ladder...)

It is pluralized as «جِبَبَة», «جِباب» and «أَجْباب».

His saying: {يَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ [السيارة]}: The majority read «يَلْتَقِطُه» with yāʾ (masculine), which is the original. Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Abū Rajāʾ and Qatāda read it with tāʾ (feminine) for the feminine sense and because it is annexed to a feminine; and they say «قُطِعت بعض أصابعه» ("some of his fingers were cut off"), and the poet said:

2745 - إذا بعضُ السنينَ تَعَرَّقَتْنا ... كفى الأيتامَ فَقْدَ أبي اليتيمِ
(When some of the years gnawed us to the bone, it sufficed the orphans for the loss of the orphan's father.)

Fuller discussion than this has already been given in al-Anʿām and al-Aʿrāf. The object of «فاعلين» is omitted, that is, "doing what will achieve your aim."

And «السَّيَّارة» is the plural of «سَيَّار», which is a pattern of intensification.

And «الالتقاط» is taking up a thing that has been thrown down; from it come «اللُّقَطة» and «اللَّقِيط». The poet said:

2746 - ومَنْهَلٍ وَرَدْتُهُ التِقاطا ...
(And a watering place I came to by chance...)

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ تَأْمَنَّا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its like has already been given. The majority read «تأمَنَّا» with ikhfāʾ (concealment), which is an expression for weakening the sound with the vowel and separating the two nūns, not that the nūn is made sākin outright, so that this is concealment and not assimilation. Al-Dānī said: "This is the saying of most of our imams, and it is the correct one because of the strength of its indication and its soundness in analogy."

Some of them read it with ishmām, which is an expression for rounding the two lips as an indication of the vowel of the verb together with outright assimilation, as the one who stops on a word indicates it, and in it there is great difficulty. They said: the indication of the ḍamma is made after the assimilation or before its completion. Ishmām occurs with several meanings, of which this is one; among them is mixing the kasra with something of the ḍamma, as in {قِيلَ} [al-Baqara: 11] and {وَغِيضَ} [Hūd: 44] and the like, which was treated at the beginning of al-Baqara. Among them is mixing one of two letters with something of the other, as the mixing of ṣād with zāy in {الصراط} [al-Fātiḥa: 5], {وَمَنْ أَصْدَقُ} [al-Nisāʾ: 78] and the like, which was also treated in al-Fātiḥa and al-Nisāʾ. This is a mixing of a letter with a letter, just as the preceding is a mixing of a vowel with a vowel. Among them is the indication of the ḍamma in pausal position only, which only the sighted sees and not the blind.

Abū Jaʿfar read it with outright assimilation without ishmām. Al-Ḥasan read it with idhhār (no assimilation), as a stress on making the iʿrāb of the verb clear and in order to preserve the vowel of iʿrāb. The majority agreed on ikhfāʾ or ishmām, as its verification has been given above.

Ibn Hurmuz read «لا تَأْمُنَّا» with ḍamma on the mīm, transferring the vowel of the first nūn when assimilating it, after stripping the mīm of its vowel; but the script of the codex has a single nūn, so in al-Ḥasan's reading there is a divergence from it.

Abū Razīn and Ibn Wathāb read «لا تِيْمَنَّا» with kasra on the letter of the imperfect, except that Ibn Wathāb softened the hamza. Al-Shaykh said: "Its coming after «مالك» and the meaning indicate that it is a negation and not a prohibition, and it is not like their saying «ما أَحْسَنَنا» in expressing wonder, because if it were assimilated it would be confused with negation." I say: how far this is from the supposition of a prohibition, that he should need to state it explicitly! But his saying "it would be confused with negation" is correct.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ}: there are fourteen readings in it. The first: Nāfiʿ's reading with yāʾ and kasra on the ʿayn. The second: the reading of al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr, «نَرْتِع ونلعب», with nūn and kasra on the ʿayn. The third: the reading of Qunbul, on whom there is disagreement: it was reported from him that the yāʾ after the ʿayn is retained in continuation and in pause, and also that it is dropped in continuation and in pause, so he agrees with al-Bazzī in one of the two aspects from him; so from him there are two readings. The fifth: the reading of Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir, «نرتَعْ ونلعبْ», with nūn and sukūn on the ʿayn and the bāʾ. The sixth: the reading of the Kufans, «يرتعْ ويلعبْ», with yāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn and the bāʾ. [Translator's note: the source jumps from the "third" to the "fifth" reading; the fourth is not separately stated in the text.]

Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad read «نرتع» with nūn and «ويلعب» with yāʾ, and this was also transmitted from Ibn Kathīr. Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayyāba read «يَرْتَع ويلعبُ» with yāʾ in both, kasra on the ʿayn and ḍamma on the bāʾ. Mujāhid, Qatāda and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «نُرْتَعْ» with ḍamma on the nūn and sukūn on the ʿayn and the bāʾ. Abū Rajāʾ read likewise, except with yāʾ in both. Al-Nakhaʿī and Yaʿqūb read «نرتع» with nūn and «يلعب» with yāʾ. The two verbs in all these readings are active.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يُرْتَع ويُلْعَب» with yāʾ, both passive. «نرتعي ونلعبُ» was also read, with the yāʾ retained and ḍamma on the bāʾ. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «نَرْعي ونلعب». These are fourteen readings, six of them among the seven mutawātir readings and eight among the irregular ones.

Whoever read with nūn attributed the verb to the brothers of Yūsuf; whoever read with yāʾ attributed the verb to him alone, without them. Whoever put kasra on the ʿayn held that it is jussive by dropping the weak letter, and took it as the form «يَفْتَعِل» from «الرَّعْي», like «يرتمي» from «الرمي». Whoever put sukūn on the ʿayn held that he jussived it by dropping the vowel and took it from «رتعَ يَرْتَعُ», when one ranges widely in fertile pasture. He said:

2747 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وإذا يَخْلُو له لَحْمي رَتَعْ
(... and when my flesh is free for him he feasts.)

Whoever put sukūn on the bāʾ made it jussive; whoever gave it ḍamma made it nominative as a resumptive, that is, "and he plays." Whoever differentiated between the two verbs, reading «يلعب» with yāʾ but not «نرتع», did so because play suits the young. Whoever read «نُرْتِع» as a quadriliteral made its object omitted, that is, "we let our livestock graze."
