Whoever made it passive: the proper explanation is that he made the deputy-agent (nāʾib fāʿil) pronoun latent, namely the pronoun of tomorrow (al-ghad), the original being «نرتع فيه ونلعب فيه» ("we graze in it and play in it"); then it was extended, the preposition was omitted and the verb became transitive to it directly, giving «نرتعه ونلعبه»; then when he made it passive, the accusative pronoun stood in place of its agent and became nominative and was latent in its governor. This extension is like the saying:

2748 - ويومٍ شَهِدْناه سُلَيْمى وعامراً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And a day we witnessed, Sulaymā and ʿĀmir...)

Whoever put both verbs in the nominative made them two ḥāls, and the ḥāl is an anticipated (muqaddara) one. As for retaining the yāʾ in «نَرْتعي» together with the jussive «نلعب», which is Qunbul's reading, some people have dared to reject it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a weak reading, not permissible except in poetry." It was also said: it is the dialect of one who jussives with an implied vowel, and he recited:

2749 - ألم يَأْتيك والأنباءُ تَنْمي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Has it not come to you — and tidings spread...)

This question has already been treated exhaustively.

And «نَرْتع» may have the pattern «نفتعل» from «الرعي», which is eating pasture, in which case there is an omitted muḍāf: "we graze our livestock"; or from «المراعاة» (attending to) a thing. He said:

2750 - تَرْتَعِي السَّفْحَ فالكَثيبَ فَذَاقا ... رٍ فَرَوْضَ القطا فَذَاتَ الرِّئالِ
(She grazes the foot of the slope, then the dune, then Dhāqār, then the meadow of the sandgrouse, then Dhāt al-Riʾāl.)

It may also have the pattern «نَفْعَل» from «رَتَعَ يَرْتَعُ», when one stays in fertility and ease; from it comes the saying of al-Ghaḍbān ibn al-Qabaʿtharā: "The fetter, the grazing, and little protection." And the poet said:

2751 - أكفراً بعد رَدِّ الموت عني ... وبعد عطائِك المِئَةَ الرِّتاعا
(Ingratitude, after you turned death away from me and after your giving of a hundred grazing camels?)

His saying: {وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ} is a ḥāl clause, and its governor is one of two things: either the imperative or its answer. If you say: may this question be a matter of iʿmāl (competing governors), since each of the two governors can act on the ḥāl? The answer: that is not permissible, because iʿmāl necessitates a pronoun substitution, and the ḥāl is not made into a pronoun, because it can only be indefinite or interpreted as indefinite.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَن تَذْهَبُواْ}: the fāʿil (agent) of «يَحْزُنني», that is, "your going grieves me." In this verse there is an indication that the imperfect accompanied by the lām of ibtidāʾ is not a ḥāl, while the grammarians made it one of the indicators that specify the present. The point of the indication is that «أَنْ تَذْهبوا» is future because it is accompanied by a particle of futurity, namely «أنْ», and what is within its scope is the agent; so if we made «لَيَحْزُنني» a ḥāl, the verb would precede its agent, which is impossible. The answer to this is that the agent in reality is implied, it being omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi standing in its place, the implied form being: "the anticipation of your going grieves me."

Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ibn Hurmuz and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «لَيَحْزُنِّي» with assimilation. Zayd ibn ʿAlī alone read «تُذْهبوا» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, from «أذهب», which is like His saying {تُنْبُتُ بالدهن} [al-Muʾminūn: 20] in the reading of one who gives the tāʾ a ḍamma, so that the bāʾ is redundant or of ḥāl.

And «الذئب» is pronounced with a hamza and without it. Al-Sūsī, al-Kisāʾī and Warsh read it without the hamza, and in pause Ḥamza does not pronounce the hamza. They said: it is derived from «تذاءَبَتِ الرِّيح», when the wind blows from every direction, because it (the wolf) comes in that manner. It is pluralized as «ذِئاب», «ذُؤبان» and «أَذْؤُب». He said:

2752 - وأَزْوَرَ يَمْطُو في بلادٍ بعيدةٍ ... تعاوى به ذُؤْبانه وثعالِبُهْ
(And a crooked one who strides in far-off lands, where its wolves and foxes howl to one another.)

«أرضٌ مَذْأَبة» is a land with many wolves, and «ذُؤابة الشعر» (the forelock) is from this, because of its movement and shifting.

His saying: {وَأَنْتُمْ عَنْهُ غَافِلُونَ} is a ḥāl clause whose governor is «يأكله».

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ}: a ḥāl clause or a parenthetical one, and {إِنَّآ إِذَاً لَّخَاسِرُونَ} is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted. And «إذن» is a particle of response, and the discussion of this has already been given fully. Abū l-Baqāʾ reported that «عُصْبَةً» was read in the accusative, and he implied what I set out earlier in the first verse.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُواْ}: several aspects are permissible for its answer. The first: that it is omitted, that is, "We made him know, and conveyed tranquillity to him." Al-Zamakhsharī implied it as "they did to him what they did of harm," and he mentioned a long story. Others implied: "their trial grew great." Others: "they put him in it." This last is better, because the speech indicates it.

The second: that the answer is stated, namely His saying {قَالُواْ ياأبانآ إِنَّا ذَهَبْنَا}, that is, "when such and such happened, they said." There is some remoteness in this, because of the distance of the speech from itself.

The third: that the answer is His saying «وأَوْحَيْنا», with the wāw redundant in it, that is, "when they went off with him, We revealed." This is the opinion of the Kufans, and they counted among this His saying, the Exalted: {فَلَمَّا أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 103], that is, «تَلَّه»; and His saying {حتى إِذَا جَآءُوهَا فُتِحَتْ} [al-Zumar: 71]; and the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

2753 - فلمَّا أَجَزْنا ساحةَ الحيِّ وانتحى ... بنا بَطْنَ حِقْفٍ ذي رُكامٍ عَقَنِقْلِ
(And when we had crossed the encampment of the tribe and turned with us into the belly of a heaped, billowing dune...)

that is, "when we crossed, he turned." This is frequent in their view after «لَمَّا».

His saying: {أَن يَجْعَلُوهُ} is the object of «أَجْمعوا», that is, "they resolved to put him," or "they resolved that they put him," because it is transitive by itself and with «على»; so «أنْ» may be on the omission of the preposition and may not. On the first, its position may be accusative or genitive; on the second, the accusative is definite.

And «الجَعْل» may mean casting, and may mean making into. On the first, «في غيابة» is attached to the verb itself before it, and on the second to an omitted element. The verb in His saying «وأَجْمعوا» may be conjoined to what precedes it, and may be a ḥāl, with «قد» implied with it according to some. The pronoun in «إليه» apparently refers to Yūsuf. It was said: it refers to Yaʿqūb.

The majority read «لَتُنَبِّئنَّهُمْ» with the tāʾ of the second person. Ibn ʿUmar read it with the yāʾ of the third person, that is, Allah the Exalted. Al-Shaykh said: "Likewise in some codices of Basra." It has already been mentioned that dotting is a later development; if he says "a later codex other than the codex of ʿUthmān," then the discussion is not about that.

Sallām read «لنُنَبِّئَنَّهم» with nūn. And «هذا» is an adjective of «أَمْرهم». It was said: a badal (substitute). It was said: explicative.

His saying: {وَهُمْ لاَ يَشْعُرُونَ} is a ḥāl clause. Its governor may be «أَوْحَيْنا», that is, "We revealed to him without their being aware of the revelation," and it may be «لَنُنَبِّئَنَّهم», that is, "you will inform them while they do not recognize you, because of the length of time and the change of circumstances."

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {عِشَآءً}: two aspects are permissible in it. The first, which it is not fitting to say otherwise, is that it is an adverb of time, that is, "they came to him at this time," and «يبكون» is a ḥāl clause, that is, "they came to him weeping." The second: that «عشاء» is the plural of «عاشٍ», like «قائم» and «قيام». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is also read with ḍamma on the ʿayn, the original being «عُشاة», like «غازٍ» and «غُزاة»; the hā' was dropped and an alif was added as compensation for it, and then the alif was turned into a hamza. There is discussion in it which was mentioned in Āl ʿImrān at His saying {أَوْ كَانُواْ غُزًّى} [verse 156]. It may be the plural of «فاعل» on «فُعال», just as «فعيل» is pluralized on «فُعال» because of the closeness between kasra and ḍamma; and it may be like «نُؤام» and «رُباب», which is irregular." I say: this reading is the reading of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, and it comes from «العِشْوة» and «العُشْوَة», which is darkness.

Al-Ḥasan also read «عُشَا» on the pattern of «دُجَى», like «غازٍ» and «غُزاة», then the feminine tāʾ was dropped from it, just as they dropped the feminine tāʾ from «مَأْلُكة» and said «مَأْلُك». On these aspects it is accusative as a ḥāl. Al-Ḥasan also read «عُشِيَّاً» in the diminutive.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {نَسْتَبِقُ}: that is, «نَتَسابق» ("we race"). The forms ifʿāl-type «افتعال» and «تفاعل» share meaning, as in their saying «نَنْتَضِل» and «نتناضَلُ» ("we compete in shooting"), «نَرْتمي» and «نترامى» ("we throw"). And «نَسْتبق» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. And «تَرَكْنا» is a ḥāl from «نَسْتبق», with «قد» implied with it according to some.

His saying: {وَلَوْ كُنَّا صَادِقِينَ} is a ḥāl clause, that is, "you will not believe us in every circumstance, even in the circumstance of our truthfulness, because of what has come to prevail in your opinion in suspecting us of hating Yūsuf and disliking him."

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {على قَمِيصِهِ}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from «الدم». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Because the implied sense is: they brought false blood on his shirt," meaning that if it had come later it would have been an adjective of an indefinite noun. This aspect was rejected by al-Zamakhsharī, who said: "If you say: may it be a preceding ḥāl? I say: no, because the ḥāl of a genitive noun does not precede it." What al-Zamakhsharī rejected it with is one of the two views of the grammarians, and a group have held its permissibility to be sound and recited:

2754 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فَلَنْ يذهبوا فَرْغاً بقَتْلِ حِبال
(... and they will not go in vain with the killing of Ḥibāl.)

and the saying of another:

2755 - لَئِنْ كان بَرْدُ الماءِ هَيْمانَ صادِياً ... إليَّ حبيباً إنَّها لحبيبُ
(If the coolness of water, for a parched, thirsting man, is dear to me, then she is indeed dear.)

and the saying of another:

2756 - غافلاً تَعْرِضُ المنيَّةُ لِلْمَرْ ... ءِ فيدعى ولاتَ حينَ إباءُ
(Unawares, death presents itself to a man and he is summoned, and it is no time for refusal.)

Al-Ḥawfī said: "«على قميصه» is attached to «جاؤوا»," and there is something to consider in this, because their coming cannot be on the shirt.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the position of «على قميصه»? I say: its position is the accusative as an adverbial, as if it were said: they came above his shirt with blood, as you say «جاء على جِماله بأَحْمال» ('he came on his camels with loads')." Al-Shaykh said: "The meaning does not support taking «على» in the accusative as an adverbial meaning «فوق», because the governor in it then is «جاؤوا», and 'above' is not an adverbial for them; rather it is impossible that it be an adverbial for them." This rejection is the one with which I rejected al-Ḥawfī's saying that «على» is attached to «جاؤوا». Then al-Shaykh said: "As for the example mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī, namely «جاء على جِماله بأَحْمال», it is possible that it is an adverbial for the one who comes, because the adverbial is established in it in view of his moving from camel to camel, and «بأَحْمال» is in the position of ḥāl, that is, joined with loads."

The majority read «كَذِب» with the dotted dhāl; it is a description by maṣdars, so it may be by way of intensification, as in «رجلٌ عَدْلٌ» ("a man of justice"), or on the omission of a muḍāf, that is, «ذي كذب» ("having falsehood"), attributing the act of its doer to it. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «كَذِباً», so it may be an object of purpose, or a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl, which is rare, I mean the ḥāl coming from an indefinite noun.

ʿĀʾisha and al-Ḥasan read «كَدِب» with the undotted dāl. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "Its meaning is «ذي كَدِب», that is, 'having a trace,' because «الكَدِب» is a whiteness that comes out on the fingernails of youths and leaves a mark on them, so it is like an engraving, and that whiteness is called «الفُوْف»; so this is a metaphor for its marking the shirt as that marks the nails." It was said: it is the turbid blood. It was said: the fresh. It was said: the dry.

His saying: {بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ}: before this sentence there is an omitted sentence, its implied form being: "The wolf did not eat him, but..." {سَوَّلَتْ}, that is, "adorned and made easy."

His saying: {فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ}: it may be a mubtadaʾ with an omitted khabar, that is, "a fair patience is best for me"; and it may be a khabar with an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "my matter is a fair patience." Is it obligatory to omit the mubtadaʾ of this khabar or the khabar of this mubtadaʾ? The rule is that it is a maṣdar originally, a substitute for the utterance of its verb. The wording of some of them requires obligation, and that of others permissibility. Among the explicit mention of the khabar of this type, though in poetic necessity, is his saying:

2757 - فقالَتْ على اسمِ اللَّهِ أَمْرُك طاعةٌ ... وإن كنتُ قد كُلِّفْتُ ما لم أُعَوَّدِ
(She said: "In the name of Allah, your command is obeyed, even though I have been charged with what I am not accustomed to.")

and the saying of the poet:

2758 - يَشْكو إليَّ جَمَلي طولَ السُّرى ... صَبْرٌ جميلٌ فكِلانا مبتلى
(My camel complains to me of the length of the night journey — fair patience! for both of us are afflicted.)

It may be a mubtadaʾ or a khabar, as mentioned earlier.

Ubayy and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «فصبراً جميلاً» in the accusative; it was also transmitted from al-Kisāʾī, and likewise it is in the codex of Anas ibn Mālik. Its analysis is as an informative maṣdar, that is, "I am patient with a patience," and this is a weak reading if analysed in this way, since according to Sībawayh this is not open to analogy except in a request; so it is better to make the implied form: "Yaʿqūb turned back and commanded himself, as if he said: be patient, O soul, with patience." The verse (of poetry) was also transmitted in the nominative and the accusative as mentioned, and the matter in it is evident. [Translator's note: the source reads "ورُوري البيتُ"; "ورُوِي البيتُ" is evidently intended.]

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فأدلى دَلْوَهُ}: it is said «أدلى دَلْوَه», meaning he lowered it into the well. And «دَلاها» is when he drew it out full. He said:

2759 - لا تَقْلَوها وادْلُواها دَلْوا ... إنَّ مع اليوم أخاه غَدْوا
(Do not hate them; draw them up with a bucket — with today comes its brother, tomorrow.)

«الدَّلْوُ» is feminine, so its diminutive is «دُلِيَّة», and it is pluralized as «دِلاء» and «أَدْلٍ». The original is «دِلاو», in which the wāw was turned to hamza like «كساء»; and «أَدْلِوٌ», which was subjected to weakening as in «قاضٍ»; and «دُلُوْوٌ» with two wāws, which were turned into two yāʾs like «عِصِيّ».

His saying: {يابشراى}: the Kufans read it with the yāʾ of annexation dropped. The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) incline the alif of «فعلى», and Warsh inclines it between the two, according to his principle. From Abū ʿAmr both aspects are reported, but the more famous from him is no imāla, and that is not among his principles, as established in the science of readings. The others read «يا بشراي», annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker. The addressing of «البشرى» is on the same footing as His saying: {ياحسرتا على} [al-Zumar: 56] and {ياحسرة عَلَى العباد} [Yā Sīn: 30], as if he were saying: "O good news, this is the time for you to be called and cried out to." Whoever claimed that «بشرى» is the name of a man like «السدّي» has gone far astray.

Warsh, from Nāfiʿ, read «يا بُشْراْيْ» with sukūn on the yāʾ, which is a combination of two sākins in continuation, and this is as mentioned before at {وَمَحْيَايَ} [al-Anʿām: 162]; so turn your attention to it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is not the proper aspect because of the meeting of two sākins not within its proper limit, unless he intends pause."

Al-Jaḥdarī, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Ḥasan read «يا بُشْرَيَّ», turning the alif into yāʾ and assimilating it into the yāʾ of annexation, which is a Hudhalī dialect, discussed in al-Baqara at His saying: {فَمَنْ تَبِعَ هُدَيَّ} [al-Baqara: 38]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In the reading of al-Ḥasan «يا بُشْرَيَّ», with yāʾ in place of the alif, the yāʾ was put in the position of the kasra before the yāʾ of annexation, and it is a famous dialect of the Arabs; I heard the people of al-Sarawāt say in their supplication: «يا سيدي ومَوْلَيَّ»."

His saying: {وَأَسَرُّوهُ}: the nominative pronoun apparently refers to «السَّيَّارة». It was said: it is the pronoun of his brothers. And «بضاعةً» is accusative as a ḥāl, or a second object, on the basis that «أَسَرُّوه» includes the meaning "they made him, secretly." And «البضاعة» is a portion of wealth prepared for trade, from «بَضَعْت», that is, "I cut," and from it «المِبْضع» for that with which one cuts.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَشَرَوْهُ}: «شرى» has the meaning of «اشترى» (to buy), and from it is the saying of the poet:

2760 - ولو أنَّ هذا الموتَ يَقْبَلُ فِدْيَةً ... شَرَيْتُ أبا زيدٍ بما مَلَكَتْ يَدي
(If this death accepted a ransom, I would buy Abū Zayd with all my hand possesses.)

and it has the meaning "to sell," and from it is the saying of the poet:

2761 - وشَرَيْتُ بُرْداً ليتني ... مِنْ بعدِ بُرْدٍ كنتُ هامَهْ
(And I sold Burd — would that after Burd I had been an owl!)

If we make the pronoun in «شَرَوْه» refer to the brothers of Yūsuf, then «شرى» means "sold"; and if we make it refer to the caravan, it means "bought."

«البَخْسُ» is the deficient, and it is originally a maṣdar used as a description for intensification. It was said: it has the meaning of a passive participle. And «دراهم» is a badal (substitute) from «بثمن», and «فيه» is attached to what follows it, which was tolerated because of the latitude allowed with adverbials and prepositional phrases; or it is attached to an omitted element, and the like has been given before.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِن مِّصْرَ}: several aspects are possible. The first: that it is attached to the verb itself before it, that is, "he bought him from Egypt," as you say «اشتريت الثوب مِنْ بغداد» ("I bought the garment from Baghdad"), the «مِنْ» being for the beginning of the extent; and Abū l-Baqāʾ's saying "that is, in it, or by it" is unnecessary. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «الذي». The third: that it is a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun in «اشتراه», so it too is attached to an omitted element. There is something to consider in these two, since there is no benefit in this meaning. And «لأمرأتِه» is attached to «قال», so the lām is for conveying, and it is not attached to «اشتراه».

His saying: {وكذلك}: the kāf, as in its parallels mentioned before, is a ḥāl from the pronoun of the maṣdar or an adjective of it, that is, "and just like that rescue and the inclining of al-ʿAzīz to him, We established him," that is, as We rescued him and inclined al-ʿAzīz to him, We established him in the land of Egypt.

His saying: {وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُ}: there are aspects in it. The first: that it is attached to an omitted element before it, that is, "and We did that in order to teach him." The second: that it is attached to what follows it, that is, "and in order to teach him We did such and such." The third: that it is attached to «مكَّنَّا», with the wāw redundant. The hāʾ in «أمره» may refer to the Majestic Name, and may refer to Yūsuf. The meaning on the first is: "We are not prevented from what We will, nor contested over what We wish"; and on the second: "We arrange it for him and do not entrust it to another; his brothers plotted against him, yet they did not harm him in any way."

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَشُدَّهُ}: there are three views on it. The first, which is Sībawayh's saying: that it is a plural whose singular is «شِدَّة», like «نِعْمة» and «أنْعُم». The second, the saying of al-Kisāʾī: that its singular is «شَدّ» on the pattern «فَعْل», like «صَكّ» and «أصُكّ», and this is supported by the saying of the poet:

2762 - عَهْدي به شَدَّ النهارِ كأنما ... خُضِبَ البَنانُ ورأسُه بالعِظْلِمِ
(My last knowledge of him was at the height of the day, as if his fingertips and his head were dyed with indigo.)

The third: that it is a plural with no singular of its own wording; Abū ʿUbayda said it, and people disagreed with him in that, since «شدَّة» and «شَدّ» are both heard and are suitable for it, and it comes from «الشَّدّ», which is binding something and tying a knot on it. Al-Rāghib said: "His saying, the Exalted, {حتى إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ} contains a warning that when a person reaches this measure, the character he has strengthens and hardly leaves him; and how fine is what the poet noticed when he says:

2763 - إذا المَرْءُ وافى الأربعينَ ولم يكنْ ... له دونَ ما يهوى حَياءٌ ولا سِتْرُ
فَدَعْه ولا تَنْفِسْ عليه الذي مضى ... وإنْ جَرَّ أسبابَ الحياةِ له العُمْرُ
(When a man reaches forty and has, before what he desires, neither shame nor restraint, leave him, and do not begrudge him what has passed, even if life draws the means of living out for him.)

His saying: {وَكَذَلِكَ} is either an adjective of an omitted maṣdar or a ḥāl from the pronoun of the maṣdar, and its parallels have been given.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَرَاوَدَتْهُ}: that is, she asked him with gentleness and soft speech. «المُراوَدَةُ» is the maṣdar. «الرِّيادة» is seeking intercourse; and «مشى رُوَيْداً» means he was gentle in his walk. «الرَّوْدُ» is gentleness in affairs and deliberation in them; «رادَتِ المرأةُ في مَشْيها تَرُوْدُ رَوَدَاناً» is from this; and «المِرْوَدُ» is the instrument (kohl-stick) from it. «الإرادةُ» is transferred from «راد يرود», when one strives to seek a need, and this was given before in al-Baqara. Here it is made transitive with «عن» because it is made to include the meaning of «خادَعَتْ» ("she deceived"), that is, she deceived him away from himself. The form mufāʿala here is from one party, like «داوَيْتُ المريض» ("I treated the patient"), though it may be on its regular sense, since each of them was asking something of the other gently: she asked the act from him and he asked abstention from her. The doubling in «غَلَّقَتْ» is for intensity, because of the multiplicity of rooms.

His saying: {هَيْتَ لَكَ}: the grammarians differed over this word, whether it is Arabic or arabized. It was said: arabized from Coptic, meaning "come here," said by al-Suddī. It was said: from Syriac, said by Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan. It was said: from Hebrew, its origin being «هَيْتَلَخ», that is, "come," and the Qurʾān arabized it; Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī said so. It was said: it is a dialect of Ḥawrān that reached the people of the Hijaz and they spoke it, its meaning being "come"; al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said so, and it is transmitted from ʿIkrima. The majority hold that it is Arabic. Mujāhid said: "It is a word of urging and approach; then in some dialects it is definitely a verb, in some a noun, and in some both are possible, and you will know that from the readings mentioned for it."

Nāfiʿ and Ibn Dhakwān read «هِيْتَ» with kasra on the hāʾ, a sākin yāʾ and fatḥa on the tāʾ. Ibn Kathīr read «هَيْتُ» with fatḥa on the hāʾ, a sākin yāʾ and ḍamma on the tāʾ. Hishām read «هِئْتَ» with kasra on the hāʾ, a sākin hamza and fatḥa or ḍamma on the tāʾ. The others read «هَيْتَ» with fatḥa on the hāʾ, a sākin yāʾ and fatḥa on the tāʾ. These are five readings among the seven.

Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū l-Aswad, al-Ḥasan and Ibn Muḥayṣin read with fatḥa on the hāʾ, a sākin yāʾ and kasra on the tāʾ. Al-Naḥḥās related that it was read with kasra on the hāʾ and the tāʾ with a sākin yāʾ between them. Ibn ʿAbbās also read «هُيِيْتُ» with ḍamma on the hāʾ, kasra on the yāʾ, then a sākin yāʾ, then ḍammated tāʾ, on the pattern of «حُيِيْتُ». Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read with kasra on the hāʾ, a sākin yāʾ and ḍamma on the tāʾ. These are four among the irregular, making nine readings. It is definitely a noun-verb (ism fiʿl) in all but Ibn ʿAbbās's reading «هُيِيْتُ» on the pattern of «حُيِيْتُ», and in all but the reading with kasra on the hāʾ, whether with yāʾ or with hamza: whoever put fatḥa on the tāʾ built it on fatḥa for lightness, like «أيْنَ» and «كَيْفَ»; whoever put ḍamma, as Ibn Kathīr, did so by likening it to «حيث»; and whoever put kasra did so on the original rule of the meeting of two sākins, like «جَيْرِ». And fatḥa and kasra on the hāʾ are two dialects.

It is definitely a verb in Ibn ʿAbbās's reading «هُيِيْتُ» on the pattern of «حُيِيْتُ», for in it it is a past passive verb attributed to the speaker's pronoun, from «هَيَّأْتُ الشيءَ» ("I prepared the thing"). It admits both in the reading of one who put kasra on the hāʾ and ḍamma on the tāʾ: it may be a noun-verb built on ḍamma like «حَيْثُ», and may be a verb attributed to the speaker's pronoun from «هاءَ الرجلُ يَهِيءُ» like «جاء يَجيء», and then it has two meanings. The first: that it means "his appearance became good." The second: that it means "he prepared himself." One says «هِئْتُ», that is, "my appearance became good" or "I prepared myself." Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed that this «هِئْتُ» be from «هاءَ يَهاء», like «شاء يشاء».

A group have criticized Hishām's reading with hamza and fatḥa on the tāʾ. Al-Fārisī said: "It resembles [that] the hamza and the fatḥa on the tāʾ were an error of the transmitter, because the address is from the woman to Yūsuf, and he was not prepared for her, by the evidence of His saying «وراوَدَتْه» and {أَنِّي لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بالغيب} [Yūsuf: 52]." A group followed him in that. Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: "The wording should be «هِئْتِ لي», and no one read it so." Also, the meaning is the opposite of it, because he kept fleeing from her and keeping away from her while she sought him, pursued him and tore his shirt, so how could he report that she had prepared herself for him?

Some of them answered these two difficulties by saying that the meaning is: "your matter has been made ready for me," because she was not able to be alone with him at every time; or the meaning is: "your appearance has become good."

And «لك» is attached to an omitted element by way of explanation, as if she said: "the speech is for you" or "the address is for you," as it is in «سقياً لك ورعياً لك». I say: the lām is attached to an omitted element in every reading except a reading in which it is established as a verb, for then it is attached to the verb, as there is no need to imply anything else.

Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The more likely is that the hamza is a substitute for the yāʾ, or is a dialect in the word that is a noun-verb, and it is not a verb, because that would require the address to be to Yūsuf, peace be upon him, which is invalid for two reasons. The first: he did not prepare himself for her; rather she prepared herself for him. The second: that he said «لك», and if the address were intended it would be «هِئْتَ لي»." I say: its answer has been given. As for his saying "the hamza is a substitute for the yāʾ," this is the reverse of the Arabs' language, since we know them to replace a sākin hamza with a yāʾ when what precedes it has kasra, as in «بير» and «ذيب», and they do not accept a yāʾ preceded by kasra turning into hamza, as in «مِيل» and «دِيك». Also, others have made the plain yāʾ with kasra on the hāʾ, as in the reading of Nāfiʿ and Ibn Dhakwān, possibly a substitute for the hamza, and they said: the discussion on it then returns to be like the discussion on Hishām's reading. Know that the reading that al-Fārisī found problematic is the well-known one from Hishām, while the ḍamma on the tāʾ is not well known from him, and I have mastered this in the commentary on «Ḥirz al-Amānī».

His saying: {مَعَاذَ الله} is accusative as a maṣdar with an omitted verb, that is, "I seek refuge with Allah, a refuge." One says «عاذ يَعُوذ عِياذاً وعِياذة ومَعاذاً وعَوْذاً». He said:

2764 - معاذَ الإِله أن تكونَ كظَبْيَةٍ ... ولا دُمْيَةٍ ولا عَقِيْلَةِ رَبْرَبِ
(God forbid that you be like a gazelle, or a statue, or the prize of a herd of wild cattle.)

His saying: {إِنَّهُ}: the hāʾ may be the pronoun of the situation (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) and what follows it a predicative sentence for it, and by "his lord" he means his master; and it may be that the hāʾ is the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted. And «ربِّي» may be its khabar, with «أَحْسَنَ» a necessary ḥāl clause, or it may be a mubtadaʾ, with «أحسن» a predicative sentence for it, the sentence being the khabar of «إنَّ». A group denied the first. Mujāhid, al-Suddī and Ibn Isḥāq said: it is very unlikely that a noble prophet would call a created being his lord, even in the sense of master, because he was not in reality a slave.

Al-Jaḥdarī and Abū l-Ṭufayl al-Ghanawī read «مَثْوَيَّ», turning the alif into yāʾ and assimilating it, like «بُشْرَيّ» and «هُدَيّ».

And {إِنَّهُ لاَ يُفْلِحُ}: this hāʾ is the pronoun of the situation only.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لولا أَن رَّأَى}: the answer to «لولا» is either preceding it, namely His saying «وَهَمَّ بها», according to one who permits the answer of conditional particles to precede them, or it is omitted, indicated by this, according to one who does not hold that. The two views and those to whom they are ascribed have been set out more than once, as in their saying «أنت ظالمٌ إن فعلْتَ» ("you are unjust if you do"), that is, "if you do, you are unjust," and you do not say that «أنت ظالمٌ» is the answer but that it indicates it. On this the pause is at His saying «برهان ربه», and the meaning is: "had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have inclined to her, but his inclining to her was prevented by the existence of seeing the proof of his Lord, so no inclination at all came from him," like your saying «لولا زيدٌ لأكرمتك» ("were it not for Zayd, I would have honoured you"), the meaning being that the honouring is prevented by the existence of Zayd. By this one escapes from the difficulty that is raised, namely: how is it fitting for a prophet to incline to a woman?

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: is His saying «وهمَّ بها» included under the oath in His saying {وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ} or outside it? I say: both are permissible, and it is the right of the reader, if he intends to exclude it from the scope of the oath and make it a separate statement, to pause at His saying {وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ} and begin His saying {وَهَمَّ بِهَا لولا أَن رأى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ}; and in it there is also an indication of the difference between the two inclinations. If you say: why did you make the answer of «لولا» omitted, indicated by «وهَمَّ بها», and why did you not make it the answer, preceding? I say: because the answer to «لولا» does not precede it, since it has the rule of a condition, and a condition has the first place in speech, and it together with the two sentences within its scope is like one word, and it is not permissible to put part of a word before another part; as for omitting part of it when evidence indicates it, that is permissible."

I say: his saying "as for omitting part of it" to the end is an answer to an implied question, namely: if the answer to the condition with the two sentences is in the position of one word, then nothing should be omitted from them, since nothing is omitted from a word. He answered that it is permissible when evidence indicates it. And it is as he said.

Then he said: "If you say: why did you make «لولا» attached to «هَمَّ بها» alone and did not make it attached to the whole of His saying {وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ وَهَمَّ بِهَا}? Because inclination does not attach to substances but to meanings, so the implication of intimate contact is necessary, and intimate contact is only between two together; so it is as if it were said: they both inclined to intimate contact, had not an obstacle prevented one of them." I say: well said, but Allah the Glorified has brought the two inclinations in detail, where He said: {وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ وَهَمَّ بِهَا}.

I say: al-Zajjāj did not approve of this statement, I mean the attachment of «لولا» to «همَّ بها», for he said: "Had the speech been «ولهمَّ بها», it would have been remote, so how with the lām dropped?" Al-Zajjāj means that it is not permissible that «وهمَّ بها» be the answer to «لولا», because if it were its answer it would be accompanied by the lām, as it is affirmative, and on the supposition that it were accompanied by the lām it would be remote from another side, namely the precedence of the answer over it.

The reply to what al-Zajjāj said is what I gave earlier from al-Zamakhsharī, that the answer is omitted, indicated by what precedes. As for his saying "had the speech been «ولهمَّ بها»," it is not obligatory, because whenever the answer to «لو» and «لولا» is affirmative both are permissible: the lām and its absence, although bringing the lām is the more frequent.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya also followed al-Zajjāj in this sense and said: "The saying of one who said that the speech was complete at {وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتَ بِهِ}, that the answer to «لولا» is in His saying «وهمَّ بها», and that the meaning is: had he not seen the proof he would have inclined to her, so Yūsuf, peace be upon him, did not incline" — he said: "this is a saying rejected by the language of the Arabs and by the sayings of the predecessors." As for his saying "rejected by the language of the Arabs," it is not so, because the pattern of this verse is the pattern of His saying: {إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِي بِهِ لولا أَن رَّبَطْنَا على قَلْبِهَا} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 10]; His saying «إن كادت» is either an answer, according to one who holds that, or an indication of the answer, and there is no departure in it from the speech of the Arabs. This is the sense of what al-Shaykh rejected him with. I say: perhaps Ibn ʿAṭiyya meant by departure from the language of the Arabs the bareness of the answer from the lām, on the supposition of the permissibility of its precedence, the point being that the lām was not found.

His saying: {كَذَلِكَ لِنَصْرِفَ}: there are aspects in this kāf. The first: that it is in the position of the accusative; al-Zamakhsharī implied: "We confirmed him with a confirmation like that." Al-Ḥawfī implied: "We showed him the proofs by that." Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied: "Our acts and decrees ran thus, so that We might turn away." Abū l-Baqāʾ implied: "We watch over him thus."

The second: that the kāf is in the position of the nominative; al-Zamakhsharī and Abū l-Baqāʾ implied: "the matter is like that." Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied: "his protection is thus." Al-Ḥawfī said: "the matter of the proofs is thus," then said: "The accusative is better, because prepositions require verbs or their meanings."

The third: that there is advancing and postponing in the speech, its implied form being: "she inclined to him and he inclined to her, thus; then He said: 'had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have been turned away from what he inclined to.'" This is Ibn ʿAṭiyya's text. It is nothing, for even granting the permissibility of advancing and postponing, there is no sense in what he mentioned.

Al-Shaykh said: "I say that the implied form is: 'like that seeing, or like that opinion, We show Our proofs so that We might turn away from him,' so the indication is made to the opinion or the seeing; and the governor of the kāf is among what His saying {لولا أَن رَّأَى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ} indicates, and «لِنَصْرِفَ» is attached to that verb that governs the kāf."

The maṣdar of «رأى» is «رُؤْية» and «رَأْي». He said:

2765 - ورأْيُ عَيْنَيَّ الفتى أباكا ... يُعطي الجزيلَ فعليك ذاكا
(And my own two eyes' sight of the youth, your father, giving lavishly — to you belongs that.)

Al-Aʿmash read «ليَصْرِفَ» with the yāʾ of the third person, the agent being Allah the Exalted.

His saying: {المخلصين}: this word, wherever it occurs, when defined with the article, was read with kasra on the lām by Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir, and the others read it with fatḥa. The kasra is as an active participle, with the object omitted, its implied form being "those who are sincere in their selves" or "in their religion"; and the fatḥa is as a passive participle, from «أَخْلصهم اللَّه», that is, "He chose them and selected them," or "He purified them from every evil."

The Kufans read in Maryam {إِنَّهُ كَانَ مُخْلِصاً} [Maryam: 51] with fatḥa on the lām in the sense given above, and the others with kasra in the sense given above.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {واستبقا الباب}: accusative either by omission of the preposition for latitude, since the original of «استبق» is to be made transitive with «إلى», or by its inclusion of the meaning of «ابتدرا» ("they hastened to"), so it governs a direct object.

His saying: {وَقَدَّتْ}: the sentence may be coordinated to «استبقا», that is, «اسْتَبَقَا وقَدَّتْ», and it may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, that is, «وقد قَدَّتْ». And «القَدُّ» is tearing in general. Some of them said: "«القَدُّ» is for what is torn lengthwise, and «القَطُّ» for what is torn crosswise."

semin-durr:26-26.t:
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "A group read «قُطَّ». Abū l-Faḍl ibn Ḥarb said: 'I saw in a codex «قُطَّ مِنْ دُبُر», that is, was torn.'" Yaʿqūb said: "«القَطُّ» is in sound skin and sound cloth." The poet said:

2766 - تَقُدُّ السُّلُوقِيَّ المُضاعَفَ نَسْجُهُ ... وتُوْقِدُ بالصُّفَّاحِ نارَ الحُبَاحِبِ
(It cuts through the Salūqī mail, double-woven, and kindles with the flat stones the fire of al-Ḥubāḥib.)

His saying: {مَا جَزَآءُ}: this «ما» may be negative, and may be interrogative; and «مَنْ» may be relative or an indefinite noun with a description. His saying {إِلاَّ أَن يُسْجَنَ} is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and since «أَن يُسجن» is equivalent to a maṣdar, the maṣdar was conjoined to it, namely His saying {أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ}. And «أو» is taken to carry its meanings, the most apparent being classification.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī read {أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيماً} in the accusative. Al-Kisāʾī analysed it on the implication of a verb, that is, "or that he be punished with a painful punishment."

His saying: {هِيَ}: he did not say «هذه» or «تلك», out of the extremity of his modesty, and it is a good courtesy, in that he used the wording of absence rather than presence. And «مِنْ أهلها» is an adjective of «شاهد», and it is what justifies the agent coming from the wording of the verb, since it is not permissible to say «قام القائم» or «قعد القاعد», for lack of benefit.

His saying: {إِن كَانَ}: this conditional sentence is either governed by an implied saying, its implied form being "he said: if...", according to the Basrans, or governed by «شَهِد», because it has the sense of saying, according to the Kufans.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِن دُبُرٍ} and {مِن قُبُلٍ}: the majority read all of this with two ḍammas, genitive and tanwīn, in the sense of "from behind" and "from in front," that is, from behind the shirt and in front of it, or Yūsuf. Al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, read with sukūn on the ʿayn for lightness, which is the dialect of the Hijaz and Asad. Ibn Yaʿmur, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, al-ʿUṭāridī and al-Jārūd read with three ḍammas, and it is also transmitted from al-Jārūd, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Ibn Yaʿmur with sukūn on the ʿayn and building both on ḍamma. The aspect of their ḍamma is that they made them like «قبل» and «بعد» in being built on ḍamma when cut off from annexation, so they made them ghāya (limit-words); the meaning of ghāya is that the muḍāf is made the limit of itself after the muḍāf ilayhi had been its limit. The original is that they are declinable, because they are two fully declinable nouns and are not adverbials. Abū Ḥātim said: "This is poor in Arabic; this building occurs only in adverbials."

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: from the front of the shirt and from its back. As for the indefiniteness, its meaning is: from a side called 'front' and from a side called 'back.' It is reported from Ibn Abī Isḥāq that he read «مِنْ قبلَ ومِنْ دبرَ» with fatḥa, as if he made them proper names for the two sides, so their diptote status is due to being proper names and feminine." The disagreement has already been given over «كان» falling within the scope of a condition: does it remain in its sense of the past, as al-Mubarrad held, or does it turn to the future like other verbs, the meaning being one of clarification?

His saying {فَكَذَبَتْ} and {فَصَدَقتْ} is on the implication of «قد», because it brings the past near to the present; this is when the past verb is fully inflecting; as for when it is fixed (jāmid), it needs no «قد», neither expressed nor implied.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يُوسُفُ} is a vocative from which the vocative particle is omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because he is a close addressee, alert to the speech, and in this there is a drawing near of him and a gentleness toward his station." End of quotation. The vocative particle may be omitted from every vocative except the majestic Name, generally the generic noun, the one called for help, the one lamented, the demonstrative noun according to the Basrans, and the pronoun when it is addressed.

The majority read the fāʾ of «يوسف» with ḍamma because it is a singular definite. Al-Aʿmash read it with fatḥa. It was said: this reading is not established from him; and on the supposition that it is established, Abū l-Baqāʾ gave two aspects for it. The first: that he brought it out on the original rule of the vocative, as it came in poetry:

2767 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
يا عَدِيَّاً لقد وَقَتْكَ الأوَاقي
(... O ʿAdī, the protectors have indeed guarded you.)

By "the original rule of the vocative" he means that it is a direct object, so its due is the accusative, like the verse he recited; and it happens that Yūsuf is a diptote, so its fatḥa is the fatḥa of iʿrāb. The second, which he made the more likely: that he paused on the word and then continued, treating continuation as pause, so he cast the vowel of the hamza onto the fāʾ and dropped it, and the pronunciation became «يوسُفَ اعْرض»; this is as it was related: «اللَّهَ اكبرَ اشْهدَ الاَّ», with continuation and fatḥa. I say: he means the fatḥa in the Majestic Name, in «أكبر», and in «اشهد»; for he supposed a pause on each of these words and cast the vowel of the hamza of each of the three words onto the sākin before it, and treated continuation as pause in that. What people related is only in «أكبر» specifically, because it is a likely place of pause, and this was given at the beginning of Āl ʿImrān.

It was also read «يوسُفُ أَعْرَضَ» with ḍamma on the fāʾ and «أعرض» as a past verb. Its analysis is that «يوسف» is a mubtadaʾ and «أَعْرض» is a sentence of verb and agent that is its khabar. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "There is weakness in it because of His saying «واستغفِري»; the more likely would be to have the fāʾ: «فاستغفري»."

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌ}: there are views on «النسوة». The well-known one is that it is a broken plural of paucity on the pattern «فِعْلة», like «الصِّبْيَة» and «الغِلْمَة». Some stated explicitly that it is not regular, and it has no singular of its own wording. The second: that it is a singular noun for the plural of «المرأة»; al-Zamakhsharī said so. The third: that it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ); Abū Bakr ibn al-Sarrāj said so, and likewise its sisters such as «الصِّيْبَة» and «الفِتْية». On every view, its femininity is not real, with regard to the group, and for this reason the feminine tāʾ was not attached to its verb. The well-known form has kasra on its nūn; ḍamma on it is possible in one dialect, and Abū l-Baqāʾ reported it as a reading, but I do not remember it; and when its nūn is given ḍamma it is a collective noun without disagreement. In the plural of multitude it is broken as «نِسْوان», and «النساء» is also a plural of multitude and has no singular of its own wording; so said al-Shaykh, and the implication of that is that «النساء» is not a plural of «نسوة», because of his saying "it has no singular of its own wording."

And «في المدينة» may be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «نسوة», which is the apparent view, or to «قال», which is not apparent.

His saying: {تُرَاوِدُ} is the khabar of «امرأة العزيز», and the imperfect was used to alert that the soliciting had become a disposition and habit of hers, rather than the past; so they did not say «راوَدَتْ». The lām of «الفتى» is a yāʾ, because of their saying «الفتيان» and «فُتَيّ»; and on this their saying «الفتوَّة» for the maṣdar is irregular.

His saying: {قَدْ شَغَفَهَا}: this sentence may be a second khabar, may be resumptive, and may be a ḥāl, either from the agent of «تُراوِدُ» or from its object. And «حبَّاً» is a tamyīz (specification), transferred from the agent function, the original being «قد شَغَفها حبُّه». The majority read «شَغَفها» with the dotted ghayn and fatḥa, in the sense of "it pierced the shighāf of her heart," taken from «الشَّغاف». «الشَّغاف» is the veil of the heart, a thin membrane. It was said: the black core of the heart. It was said: a disease that reaches the heart because of love. It was said: a thin membrane called "the tongue of the heart," which does not encompass it. The meaning of «شَغَفَ قلبَه» is: it pierced its veil, or it struck it and burned it with the heat of love; and it is from «شَغَفَ البعيرَ بالهِناء», when he coats it with tar and burns it. «المَشْغوف» is one whose heart love has reached. Al-Aʿshā said:

2768 - تَعْصِي الوُشاةَ وكان الحُبُّ آوِنَةً ... مِمَّا يُزَيِّنُ للمَشْغوف ما صنعا
(She disobeys the slanderers, and love at times is among the things that adorn for the love-stricken whatever he has done.)

And al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:

2769 - وقد حالَ هَمٌّ دونَ ذلك والِجٌ ... مكانَ الشَّغافِ تَبْتَغيه الأصابعُ
(And a piercing grief has come between that, lodged in the place of the shighāf, which the fingers seek.)

Thābit al-Bunānī read with kasra on the ghayn. It was said: it is the dialect of Tamīm.

The Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn and his son Muḥammad and his son Jaʿfar, al-Shaʿbī and Qatāda read with fatḥa on the undotted ʿayn, and it is related from Thābit al-Bunānī and Abū Rajāʾ also with kasra on the undotted letter. People differed over that. It was said: it is from «شَعَفَ البعيرَ», when he coats it with tar and burns it; al-Zamakhsharī said so and recited:

2770 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كما شَعَفَ المَهْنُؤْءَةَ الرجلُ الطالي
(... as the man who applies the tar burns the mangy camel smeared with it.)

People relate it only with the dotted letter and explain it as: her love struck the shighāf of her heart, that is, burned its veil, which is a thin membrane beneath it; «كما شَغَفَ», that is, as he burned and was thorough with the «مهنوءة», the one coated with «الهِناء», which is tar; and they do not recite it with the undotted letter.

Abū l-Baqāʾ, when he reported this reading, said: "From your saying «فلان مَشْعوفٌ بكذا», that is, infatuated with it; and on these views the meanings are close." Some of them differentiated between them. Ibn Zayd said: "«الشَّغَف», I mean with the dotted letter, is in love, and «الشَّعَفُ» in hatred." Al-Shaʿbī said: "«الشَّغَف» and «المَشْغوف» with the dotted ghayn are in love, and «الشَّعَفُ» is madness, and «المَشْعوف» is the mad one."

His saying: {مُتَّكَئاً}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the mīm, doubled tāʾ, fatḥa on the kāf, and hamza; it is a direct object of «أَعْتَدَتْ», that is, "she prepared and made present." «المتكأ» is the thing on which one reclines, such as a cushion and the like. It was said: «المتكأ» is a place of reclining. It was said: a food that is cut with cutting; this is the saying of Mujāhid. Al-Qutaybī said: "It is said «اتَّكَأْنا عند فلانٍ», that is, 'we ate.'"

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "From your saying «اتَّكَأْنا عند فلان», 'we ate,' by way of metonymy, because from «دَعَوْتَه ليَطْعَمَ عندك» ('you invited him to eat with you'): you provided for him a cushion to recline on. Jamīl said:

2771 - فَظَلِلْنا بنعمةٍ واتَّكَأْنا ... وشَرِبْنا الحَلالَ مِنْ قُلَلِهْ
(We spent the day in comfort and reclined, and drank what is lawful from its jars.)"

End of quotation. I say: his saying «وشَرِبْنا» supports the meaning of «اتَّكَأْنا» as "we ate."

Abū Jaʿfar and al-Zuhrī read «مُتَّكَا» with doubled tāʾ and no hamza, and there are two aspects in it. The first: that its origin is «مُتَّكَأ» as the majority's reading, and its hamza was only lightened, as they say «تَوَضَّيْتُ» for «تَوَضَّأْتُ», so it became on the pattern of «مُتَّقَى». The second: that it is «مُفْتَعَل» from «أَوْكَيْتُ القِرْبة», when you tie its mouth with the thong, so the meaning is: "she prepared something that they could support themselves upon, either by reclining or by cutting with the knife"; and this second analysis is Abū l-Fatḥ's.

Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Hurmuz read «مُتَّكاءً» with doubling and lengthening; it is like the majority's reading except that he prolonged the fatḥa so that an alif arose from it, like his saying:

2772 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ومِنْ ذَمِّ الرجالِ بمنتزاحِ
(... and far from the blame of men.)

and his saying:

2773 - يَنْباع مِنْ ذفرى غَضُوبٍ جَسْرَةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(It gushes from behind the ear of an angry, bold she-camel...)

and his saying:

2774 - أَعوذُ باللَّه مِنَ العَقْرابِ ... الشَّائِلاتِ عُقَدَ الأَذْنابِ
(I seek refuge with Allah from the scorpions that raise the knots of their tails.)

that is, «بمنتزح», «يَنْبَع» and «العقرب الشائلة».

Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Jaḥdarī and Abān ibn Taghlib read «مُتْكَاً» with ḍamma on the mīm, sukūn on the tāʾ and tanwīn on the kāf; likewise read Ibn Hurmuz, ʿAbd Allāh and Muʿādh, except that those two put fatḥa on the mīm. «المُتْكُ», with ḍamma and with fatḥa, is the citron, and it is said «الأُتْرُنْجُ»; they are two dialects, and they recited:

2775 - فَأَهْدَتْ مُتْكَةً لبني أبيها ... تَخُبُّ بها العَثَمْثَمَةُ الوَقاحُ
(She sent a citron to her father's sons, borne at a trot by the strong, hardy camel.)

It was said: rather it is a name for everything that is cut with a knife, such as citron and other fruits, and they recited:

2776 - نَشْرَبُ الإِثمَ بالصُّواعِ جِهاراً ... وترى المُتْكَ بيننا مُسْتعارا
(We drink wine openly from the goblet, and you see the «متك» circulating among us as a loan.)

It was said: it is from «مَتَك» in the sense of «بَتَك الشيءَ», that is, he cut it; on this, the mīm may be a substitute for the bāʾ, which is a regular substitution in the dialect of some people; and it is possible that it is from another root coinciding with this one. It was said: with ḍamma it is pure honey according to al-Khalīl, and the citron according to al-Aṣmaʿī. Abū ʿAmr reported the three forms for it, I mean ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra on the mīm; he said: it is the pure drink.

Al-Mufaḍḍal said: with ḍamma it is the table, or wine in the dialect of Kinda.

And His saying: {لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَئاً}: either he intends one reclining-place for each woman, as His saying indicates: {وَآتَتْ كُلَّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِّنْهُنَّ سِكِّيناً}, or he intends the genus.

«السِّكِّين» is masculine and feminine; al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said so, and al-Aṣmaʿī denied its feminine use. «السَّكِينة» is of the pattern «فَعِيلة» from «السكون». Al-Rāghib said: "It is so called because it removes the movement of the slaughtered animal."

His saying: {أَكْبَرْنَهُ}: the apparent view is that the hāʾ is the pronoun of Yūsuf. The meaning of «أَكْبَرْنَه» is: they magnified him and were stunned by his beauty. It was said: it is the hāʾ of pause. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It was said: «أَكْبَرْنَ» means «حِضْنَ» ('they menstruated') and the hāʾ is for pause; it is said «أَكْبَرَتِ المرأةُ» when she menstruates, and its reality is: she entered into maturity, because by menstruation she goes out of the limit of youth into maturity; and it is as if Abū l-Ṭayyib took from this explanation his saying:

2777 - خَفِ اللَّهَ واسْتُرْ ذا الجمالَ ببُرْقُعٍ ... فإنْ لُحْتَ حاضَتْ في الخُدورِ العواتِقُ
(Fear Allah and cover this beauty with a veil, for if you appear, the maidens in their chambers will menstruate.)"

End of quotation. That the hāʾ is for pause is refuted by the ḍamma on the hāʾ; had it been for pause it would be sākin. It may be said that he treated it like the hāʾ of the pronoun and treated continuation as pause in retaining it. Al-Shaykh said: "The consensus of the readers on ḍamma for the hāʾ in continuation is evidence that it is not the hāʾ of pause; for if it were the hāʾ of pause and a case of treating continuation as pause, the hāʾ would not be given ḍamma." I say: the hāʾ of pause is vowelled with the vowel of the pronoun hāʾ, treating it as such, and I have verified this in al-Anʿām; and they said the same about al-Mutanabbī's saying:

2778 - واحَرَّ قلباه مِمِّنْ قَلْبُه شَبِمُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Oh, the burning of my heart, for the sake of one whose heart is cold...)

since it was related with ḍamma on the hāʾ in «قلباه», and they made it the hāʾ of pause. It is possible that «أَكْبَرْنَ» means «حِضْنَ» and the hāʾ is not for pause, but made the pronoun of the maṣdar indicated by its verb, that is, «أَكْبَرْنَ الإِكبار». They recited, to show that «الإِكبار» means menstruation, the saying:

2779 - يأتي النساءَ على أَطْهارِهِنَّ ولا ... يأتي النساءَ إذا أَكْبَرْن إكبارا
(He comes to women during their periods of purity, and does not come to women when they menstruate.)

Al-Ṭabarī said: "The verse is fabricated."

His saying: {حَاشَ للَّهِ}: the grammarians counted «حاشى» among the particles that waver between being a particle and a verb: if it governs the genitive it is a particle, and if it governs the accusative it is a verb; and it is among the particles of exception. Sībawayh did not recognize its verbal status, though others did, and they related from the Arabs: «غَفَر اللَّه لي ولِمنْ سمع دعائي حاشى الشيطانَ وابنَ الأصبغ», in the accusative, and they recited:

2780 - حشى رَهْطَ النبيِّ فإنَّ منهمْ ... بُحوراً لا تكدِّرُها الدِّلاءُ
(Except the clan of the Prophet, for among them are seas that buckets do not muddy.)

with «رَهْط» in the accusative. And «حشى» is a variant of «حاشى», as will come. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«حاشى» is a word that gives the sense of exoneration in the section of exception; you say «أساءَ القومُ حاشى زيدٍ» ('the people did wrong, except Zayd'). He said:

2781 - حاشى أبي ثوبانَ إنَّ بهِ ... ضِنَّاً عنِ المَلْحاة والشَّتْم
(Except Abū Thawbān, for he is too miserly for reproach and abuse.)

It is a particle among the particles of the genitive, placed in the position of exoneration and clearing; so the meaning of «حاشى اللَّهِ» is: the clearing of Allah and the exoneration of Allah, and it is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd." Al-Shaykh said: "What he mentioned, that it gives exoneration in the section of exception, is unknown to the grammarians; there is no difference between your saying «قام القومُ إلا زيداً» and «قام القوم حاشى زيدٍ». When he gave the example «أساء القومُ حاشى زيدٍ» and understood from this example the clearing of Zayd from wrongdoing, he made that derived from it in every place. As for what he recited, «حاشا أبي ثوبان», this is how Ibn ʿAṭiyya and most grammarians recite it, but it is a verse in which they put the first half of one verse on the second half of another, in error, from two verses, which are:

2782 - حاشى أبي ثَوْبان إنَّ أبا ... ثَوْبانَ ليس ببُكْمَةٍ فَدْمِ
عمرَو بنَ عبدِ اللَّه إنَّ به ... ضِنَّاً عن المَلْحاةِ والشَّتْمِ
(Except Abū Thawbān — for Abū Thawbān is not a dumb, sluggish dolt — ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, for he is too miserly for reproach and abuse.)"

I say: his saying that the meaning mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī is unknown to the grammarians — they did not deny it; they simply did not mention it in their books, because most of their craft is in the making of the expressions rather than the meanings. When they mentioned «ليس», «لا يكون» and «غير» among the particles of exception, they did not mention their meanings, since their purpose was their equality with «إلا» in excluding, and that does not prevent an added meaning in those particles.

Al-Mubarrad and others, like Ibn ʿAṭiyya, claimed that its verbal status is definite when a preposition follows it, as in the noble verse. They said: because a preposition does not enter upon its like except for emphasis, as in his saying:

2783 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا لِلِما بهم أبداً دواءُ
(... and for what afflicts them there is never a remedy.)

and the saying of another:

2784 - فأَصْبَحْنَ لا يَسْأَلْنني عن بما به ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And they came to be asking me no more about what is in him...)

so it is definitely a verb, its agent being the pronoun of Yūsuf, that is, «حاشى يوسف», and «للَّه» is a preposition and genitive noun attached to the verb before it, the lām giving cause, that is, "Yūsuf kept far from committing what she accused him of, out of obedience to Allah and his standing with Him, or because of Allah's raising him above being accused of what she accused him of"; that is, he avoided disobedience for the sake of Allah.

People answered that by saying that «حاشى» in the noble verse is neither a particle nor a verb; rather it is a noun of a maṣdar, a substitute for the utterance of its verb, as if it were said "exoneration for Allah and clearing for Him," and it was not given tanwīn only out of regard for its origin from which it was transferred, namely the particle. Do you not see that they said «مِنْ عن يمينه», making «عن» a noun without declining it, and they said «مِنْ عليه», not retaining its alif with the pronoun, but leaving «عن» on its building, and turning the alif of «على» with the pronoun, out of regard for its origin? So answered al-Zamakhsharī, and al-Shaykh followed him without ascribing the answer to him. There is something to consider in it.

As for his saying "out of regard for its origin," it implies that it was transferred from particle status to noun status, and that happens only in the case of proper names, meaning that they name a person with a particle, and they have two doctrines about that: declension, and quotation (ḥikāya). That they transfer a particle to a noun, that is, make it a noun, is unknown. As for his citing «عن» and «على», it does not help him, because «عن», in the state of being a noun, is built only because of its resemblance to the particle in being set on two letters, not because it remains on its building. As for the turning of the alif of «على» with the pronoun, there is no indication in it, because we know this in what is of established noun status by agreement, like «لدى».

It is better to say: what appears in the answer to the majority's reading is that it is an accusative noun, as set out above, and the reading of Abū l-Simāl «حاشاً للَّه» in the accusative indicates it; only that they turned the tanwīn into alif as they turn it in pause, then treated continuation as pause, as they did in many places, some of which have been given and the like of which will come to you.

It was said in answer to that: rather «حاشا» was built, in its noun state, because of its resemblance to «حاشا» in its particle state in wording and meaning, as «عن» and «على» were built, for the reason we mentioned.

Some of them said: the lām is redundant. This is very weak; its place is poetry. Al-Mubarrad and his followers cited as evidence for its verbal status the occurrence of its imperfect. Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:

2785 - ولا أرى فاعِلاً في الناسِ يُشْبِهُهُ ... ولا أُحاشي من الأقوامِ مِنْ أَحَدِ
(And I see no doer among people who resembles him, and I exempt from the peoples no one.)

They said: the word's inflection from past to imperfect is definitely evidence of its verbal status. The majority answered that by saying that this is taken from the wording of the particle, as they said «سَوَّفْتُ بزيد» and «لَوْلَيْت له», that is, "I said to him: I will do (sawfa)" and "I said to him: if it were (law), if it were"; and this is of that kind, and it is possible.

Among those who preferred the verbal side was Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī; he said: "«حاش» in His saying «حاش للَّه» cannot be other than either the genitive particle in exception, or a verb on the pattern «فاعَل»; it cannot be the genitive particle because it does not enter upon its like, and because particles are not subject to omission unless they have doubling; so it is established that it is «فاعَل» from «الحشا», which means the side; the meaning is that he became in a «حَشاً», that is, in a side; and the agent of «حاش» is «يوسف», and the implied form is: 'he kept far from this matter, for Allah,' that is, for fear of Him.'"

His saying "a preposition does not enter upon its like" is granted, but it is not a preposition here, as was set out above. His saying "nothing is dropped from a particle except when it is doubled" is disputed, and what indicates it is their saying «مُنْ» for «منذ» when it governs the genitive, dropping its ʿayn, with no doubling. They said: what indicates that its origin is «منذ» with nūn is its diminutive «مُنَيْذ», and this is established in its chapter.

Abū ʿAmr alone read «حاشى» with two alifs: an alif after the ḥāʾ and an alif after the shīn, in the two occurrences of this sūra in continuation, and dropping it in pause, following the script, as we shall point out. The others drop the last alif in continuation and pause. As for Abū ʿAmr's reading, he brought the word on its original form. As for the others, they followed the script in that, and since the word is long, lightening it by omission was good, especially on the view of one who claims its verbal status, like al-Fārisī.

Al-Fārisī said: "As for the omission of the alif, it is like «لم يَكُ», «لا أَدْرِ», «أصاب الناسَ جُهْدٌ، ولَوْ تَرَ أهلَ مكة», and [his saying]:

2786 - وصَّانيَ العجَّاجُ فيما وَصَّني ...
(Al-ʿAjjāj charged me with what he charged me...)

in the poetry of Ruʾba," meaning: «لم يكن», «لا أدري», «ولو ترى», and «وصَّاني». Abū ʿUbayd said: "I saw it in the one said to be the Imām, the codex of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him: «حاش للَّه» without alif, and the other (occurrence) the same." Al-Kisāʾī related that he saw it in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh likewise. They said: on what Abū ʿUbayd and al-Kisāʾī said, this reading is preferred, and because six of the seven read it. Al-Farrāʾ reported that the full form is the dialect of some Arabs and the omission is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz; he said: "Among the Arabs is one who says «حشى زيد», meaning «حشى لزيد»." Al-Farrāʾ reported that the three forms are heard, but the dialect of the Hijaz is preferred in their view.

Al-Aʿmash, with a group, read «حشى للَّه» with both alifs dropped, and it has been mentioned that al-Farrāʾ related it as a dialect of some Arabs, and on it is his saying:

2787 - حشى رَهْطِ النبيِّ. . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Except the clan of the Prophet...)

the verse (as above). Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read «حاشى اللَّهِ» with the Majestic Name in the genitive, and there are two aspects in it. The first: that it is a noun annexed to the Majestic Name [like «سبحان اللَّه», and this is al-Zamakhsharī's choice. The second: that it is a particle of exception governing the genitive of what follows, and al-Fārisī held this]; and in making «حاشى» a genitive particle meant for exception there is something to consider, since nothing has preceded in the speech from which the Majestic Name would be excepted, unlike «قام القومُ حاشى زيد».

Know that when the grammarians mentioned this particle, they made it among the words that waver between verbal and particle status, according to one who affirmed its verbal status, and made it in that like «خلا» and «عدا», according to one who affirmed the particle status of «عدا». It would have been fitting for them to mention it among those wavering among noun, verb and particle status, as they did with «على», saying that it is a genitive particle in «عليك», a noun in the saying «مِنْ عليه», and a verb in the saying:

2788 - عَلاَ زيدُنا يومَ النَّقا. . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Our Zayd rose up on the day of al-Naqā...)

although there is something to consider in it, which I have given fully elsewhere; its summary is that «على» in its verbal state is other than «على» in its non-verbal state, by the evidence that the alif of the verb is converted from a wāw, and inflection and derivation enter it and not the other two. A defender of al-Fārisī may rely on this and say: if «حاشى» in the majority's reading were a noun, the grammarians would have mentioned that in its wavering between particle and verb; since they did not mention it, it indicates that it is not a noun.

Al-Ḥasan read «حاشْ» with sukūn on the shīn in continuation and pause, as if he treated continuation as pause. Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported from al-Ḥasan that he read «حاشى الإِله», saying: "dropped from «حاشى»," meaning that he read with the last alif dropped, and what the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» stated explicitly indicates it, for he said: "with the alif dropped," then said: "and this indicates that it is a genitive particle governing what follows. As for «الإِله», he disassimilated it, and it is a maṣdar put in the place of the passive participle, its meaning being 'the worshipped,' and the alif of «حاشى» was dropped for lightness."

Al-Shaykh said: "What Ibn ʿAṭiyya and the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said, that the alif of «حاشى» is dropped in al-Ḥasan's reading, is not definite, unless it is reported from him that he pauses in this reading with sukūn on the shīn; if nothing is reported from him on that, it is possible that the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two sākins, since the original is «حاشى الإِله», then he transferred (the vowel), dropping the hamza and vowelling the lām with its vowel, and did not take this vowelling into account because it is incidental, just as it is dropped in «يَخْشى الإِله», and had he taken the vowel into account, the alif would not have been dropped."

I say: the apparent view is that al-Ḥasan pauses in this reading with sukūn on the shīn, and it is supported by the fact that he put sukūn on the shīn in the other transmission from him; so when something that admits interpretation is brought, it should be taken on what is stated explicitly. And the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ»'s saying "this indicates that it is a genitive particle governing what follows" is not sound, because of what was said that had it been a genitive particle it would be used for exception and nothing precedes from which to except by its genitive noun.

Know that the lām entering the Majestic Name is attached to an omitted element by way of explanation, as it is in «سقياً لك ورعياً لزيد», according to the majority; as for al-Mubarrad and al-Fārisī, it is attached to «حاشى» itself because it is an explicit verb for them both; and it has been mentioned that some claimed it to be redundant.

His saying: {مَا هذا بَشَراً}: the majority apply «ما» as working, in the Hijazi dialect, which is the purest dialect; the dialect of Tamīm is non-operation. The verification of this has been given at the beginning of al-Baqara, together with what I recited about it, namely his saying:

2789 - وأنا النذيرُ بحَرَّةٍ مُسْوَدَّةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And I am the warner of a black lava-field...)

the two verses. Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported that no one read except in the Hijazi dialect. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Whoever read according to his natural speech of the Banū Tamīm read «بشرٌ» in the nominative, and this is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya's claim that it was not read so is not granted.

The majority read «بَشَراً» with fatḥa on the bāʾ, as one word. Al-Ḥasan and Abū l-Ḥuwayrith al-Ḥanafī read «بشرى» with kasra on the bāʾ, the bāʾ being the preposition entering on «شِرى», so they are two words, a preposition and its genitive noun, and there are interpretations of it. The first: "this is not something bought," putting the maṣdar in the place of the direct object, like «ضَرْب الأمير» ("the Emir's striking"). The second: "this is not something sold," which is also a maṣdar in the place of the direct object, except that the meaning differs. The third: "this is not for a price," meaning that he is too exalted for any of these things to be done to him.

ʿAbd al-Wārith related from Abū ʿAmr, like the reading of al-Ḥasan and Abū l-Ḥuwayrith, except that he read from him «إلا مَلِك» with kasra on the lām, the singular of «الملوك»; they denied him the lowliness of slaves and affirmed for him the honour of kings.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned the kasra on the lām from al-Ḥasan and Abū l-Ḥuwayrith. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "On this «مَلِك» was read with kasra on the lām," as if he understood that whoever read with kasra on the bāʾ read with kasra on the lām too, for the harmony between the two meanings. Al-Zamakhsharī did not mention this reading with kasra on the bāʾ at all; rather it is understood from his words that he did not come across it, for he said: "It was read «ما هذا بشرى», that is, 'he is not a slave owned and base; this is only a noble angel.' You say «هذا بشرى», that is, 'obtained through purchase,' meaning bought; and you say «هذا لك بشرى أم بِكِرا؟». But the reading (of the majority) is the better, for its agreement with the codex and the correspondence of «بشر» to «ملك»."

His saying "for its agreement with the codex" means that the script is «بشراً» with alif, not with yāʾ, and had the meaning been «بشرى» it would have been written with yāʾ. And his saying "and the correspondence" is evidence that he did not come across the kasra on the lām from one who read with kasra on the bāʾ.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فذلكن} is a mubtadaʾ and the relative is its khabar. She pointed to him with the pointing used for the distant, although he was present, to magnify him and exalt him, so as to show her excuse in her infatuation.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed that «ذلك» may be a pointing to the love of Yūsuf, with the pronoun in «فيه» returning to the love, so that «ذلك» would be a pointing to something absent in its proper sense. I say: by "absent" he means "distant"; otherwise pointing is only ever to something present, in general.

His saying: {مَآ آمُرُهُ}: there are two aspects in «ما». The first: that it is a maṣdar particle. The second: that it is a relative, and it is the direct object of «يفعلْ». The hāʾ in «آمُرُه» admits two aspects. The first: return to the relative «ما» when we make it mean "that which." The second: return to Yūsuf. Al-Zamakhsharī did not allow its return to Yūsuf unless «ما» is made a maṣdar, for he said: "If you say: does the pronoun in «آمُره» return to the relative or to Yūsuf? I say: rather to the relative, and the meaning is «ما آمُرُ به», the preposition having been omitted, as in his saying:

2790 - أَمَرْتُكَ الخيرَ. . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I commanded you the good...)

and it is possible to make «ما» a maṣdar particle, so that it returns to Yūsuf, its meaning being: 'and if he does not do my command to him,' that is, what my command requires and entails." I say: on this the first object is omitted, its implied form being «ما آمُره به», and it is the pronoun of Yūsuf.

And the sīn in «استعصم» has two aspects, the first being that it is not on its regular sense of seeking, but that «استفعل» here has the meaning of «افتعل», so «استعصم» and «اعتصم» are one. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الاستعصام» is a form of intensification that indicates thorough refusal and strong self-guarding, as if he were in a state of protection and striving to increase from it; like «استمسك», «استوسع الفَتْقُ», «استجمع الرأيَ» and «استفحل الخطبُ»." So he returned the sīn to its regular sense of seeking, which is a good meaning; for this reason Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He sought protection, held fast to it, and disobeyed me."

Al-Shaykh said: "What the morphologists mentioned about «استعصم» is that it corresponds to «اعتصم», so «استفعل» in it corresponds to «افتعل», and this is better than making «استفعل» in it for seeking, because «اعتصم» indicates the existence of his taking protection, whereas seeking protection does not indicate its attainment. As for its being a form of intensification indicating striving to increase protection, the morphologists did not mention this meaning for «استفعل». As for «استمسك», «استوسع» and «استجمع الرأيَ», «استفعل» in them corresponds to «افتعل», the meaning being «امتسك», «اتَّسع» and «اجتمع». As for «استفحل الخطبُ», «استفعل» in it corresponds to «تفعَّل», that is, «تَفَحَّل الخطب», like «استكبر» and «تكبَّر»."

The majority read «وليَكونَنْ» with the nūn lightened, and they pause on it with alif, treating it like tanwīn; for this reason they drop it after ḍamma or kasra, as «هل تقومون» and «هل تقومين» for «هل تَقُومُن» and «هل تقومِن»; and the nūn that appears in pause is the nūn of the nominative, which they restored when what required its omission is absent; I have set this out earlier.

A group read it with the nūn doubled, which diverges from the script of the codex, as it is written with an alif in it, because pause on it is thus, as in his saying:

2791 - وإياكَ والمَيْتاتِ لا تَقْرَبَنَّها ... ولا تَعْبُدِ الشيطانَ واللَّهَ فاعبدا
(Beware of carrion, do not go near it, and do not worship Satan; worship Allah!)

that is, «فاعبدَنْ», so he turned it into alif, and this is one of the views on the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

2792 - قِفا نَبْكِ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Halt, you two, let us weep...)

and he treated continuation as pause.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {رَبِّ السجن}: the majority read with kasra on the bāʾ because it is annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker, with the kasra sufficing in place of it, which is the purest usage. And «السجن» with kasra on the sīn and nominative nūn, as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar «أحبُّ». «السِّجْن» is detention, and the meaning is: entering the prison.

Some of them read «رَبُّ» with ḍamma on the bāʾ and genitive nūn, on the basis that «ربُّ» is a mubtadaʾ and «السجنِ» is genitive by annexation, and «أحبُّ» is its khabar, the meaning being: "meeting the keeper of the prison and suffering at his hands is dearer to me."

ʿUthmān and his client Ṭāriq, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Zuhrī, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Ibn Hurmuz and Yaʿqūb read with fatḥa on the sīn, and the rest like the majority. «السَّجْن» is a maṣdar, that is, "confinement is dearer to me," and «إليَّ» is attached to «أحبُّ». It has already been mentioned that the agent here is governed by «إلى» and the object by lām. In reality, «أَفْعَل» here is not of the elative in its proper sense, because he never loved what they called him to; rather these are two evils and he preferred one of the two evils to the other.

His saying: {أَصْبُ}: the majority read with the bāʾ lightened, from «صَبا يَصْبو», that is, "his longing grew tender." «الصَّبْوة» is inclination toward desire, and from it comes «الصَّبا» (the east wind), because souls incline (taṣbū) to it for the sweetness of its breeze and its comfort. One says «صَبَا يَصْبُو صَباءً وصُبُوَّاً» and «صَبِيَ يصبى صَبَاً», and «الصِّبا» with kasra is diversion and play.

A group read «أَصَبُّ» with the bāʾ doubled, from «صَبَبْتُ صَبابة» ("I was ardent in love"), so I am «صَبٌّ». And «الصَّبابَة» is tenderness of longing and its excess, as if, from the excess of his love, he pours (yanṣabbu) toward what he desires as water pours.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ بَدَا}: there are four aspects about its agent. The best of them: that it is a pronoun returning to «السَّجن» with fatḥa on the sīn, that is, "the imprisoning of him appeared to them," and the word «السِّجن» in the majority's reading indicates this, by implication, and the word «السَّجن» in the reading of one who put fatḥa on the sīn. The second: that the agent is the pronoun of the maṣdar understood from the verb «بدا», that is, «بَدا لهم بداءٌ» ("a change of mind appeared to them"), and the poet stated it explicitly in his saying:

2793 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... بَدا لك في تلك القَلوص بداءُ
(... a change of mind about that young she-camel occurred to you.)

The third: that the agent is an implied element which the context indicates, that is, "an opinion appeared to them." The fourth: that the sentence «لَيَسْجُنُنَّه» itself is the agent, and this is among the principles of the Kufans.

And «حتى» marks the limit of what precedes it. His saying «لَيَسْجُنُنَّه», on the view of the majority, is the answer to an omitted oath, and that oath and its answer are governed by an implied saying, and that implied saying is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, that is, "such and such appeared to them, as they said: By Allah, they will imprison him for a time."

Al-Ḥasan read «لَتَسْجُنُنَّه» with the tāʾ of the second person, and there are two interpretations in it. The first: that they addressed one another with that. The second: that al-ʿAzīz was addressed with it, as a magnifying of him.

Ibn Masʿūd read «عتى», turning the ḥāʾ of «حتى» into ʿayn, and he taught it to others, and that reached ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who wrote to him: "This Qurʾān was revealed in the dialect of Quraysh, so teach people in their dialect." I say: the substitution of ʿayn for ḥāʾ is a Hudhalī dialect.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَآ} is resumptive, with no position, and it cannot be a ḥāl, because the two did not say that at the time of entering; nor can it be an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because entering does not lead to the dream. And «إني» and what is within its scope are in the position of the accusative, governed by the saying.

And «أراني» here is transitive to two objects, according to some, treating dream-seeing as knowledge-seeing, so the sentence of His saying «أَعْصِرُ» is in the position of the second object; and for one who disallows that, it is in the position of ḥāl for him. Dream-seeing was also treated like knowledge-seeing in the identity of its agent and object as two attached pronouns, and from this is the noble verse; for the agent and the object are identical in meaning, since both refer to the speaker, and they are two attached pronouns. Similar is «رَأَيْتُك في المنام قائماً» ("I saw you in the dream standing") and «زيدٌ رآه قائماً» ("Zayd saw himself standing"), and that is not permissible apart from what is mentioned; you do not say «أَكْرَمْتُني», nor «أكرمْتُك», nor «زيد أكرمه»; if you intend that, say «أكرمتُ نفسي» or «إياي ونفسك», or «إياك ونفسَه», or «إياه». The verification of this has been given before.

When the hamza of transfer enters this dream-verb, it becomes transitive to a third, and this has been given in His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ يُرِيكَهُمُ الله فِي مَنَامِكَ قَلِيلاً} [al-Anfāl: 43], "and had He shown you them as many."
