«الخَمْر» is grapes; it is called that metaphorically, because it comes to be that, as one thing is named by another in view of what it was, as in His saying: {وَآتُواْ اليتامى} [al-Nisāʾ: 2] ("and give the orphans [their property]"); and the metaphor of this one is nearer. It was said: rather «الخمر» is grape in reality in the dialect of Ghassān and Azd ʿUmān. From al-Muʿtamir: "I met a Bedouin carrying grapes in a vessel and said: what are you carrying? He said: «خمراً»."

The reading of Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh, «أَعْصِر عنباً», does not indicate synonymy, since it intends explanation and not recitation, as in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh «فوق رأسي ثريداً», for he intended only explanation.

And «تأكل الطير» is an adjective of «خبزاً». «فوق» may be an adverbial of the carrying and may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl of «خبزاً», because in origin it is an adjective of it. As for the pronoun in His saying «نَبِّئْنا بتأويله», al-Shaykh said: "It returns to what they narrated to him, treated like a demonstrative noun, as if it were said «بتأويل ذلك»." Al-Zamakhsharī preceded him in this, and he made it a question and answer. Another said: "He made the pronoun singular only because each of them asked about his own dream, so it is as if each of them said: tell us the interpretation of what I saw."

semin-durr:37-37.t:
And «تُرْزَقانه» is an adjective of «طعام». His saying «إلا نَبَّأْتُكما» is an exception from a void (istithnāʾ mufarragh). For the sentence after it there are two aspects. The first: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and this is allowed from an indefinite because of its being specified by the description. The second: that it is in the position of the nominative as a second adjective of «طعام», the implied form being: "no food provided to you will come to you except while it informs of its interpretation, or while it is informed of its interpretation." And «قبل» is apparently an adverbial of «نَبَّأْتكما», and it may be attached to «تأويله», that is, "I informed you of its interpretation, which occurs before its coming."

His saying: {إِنِّي تَرَكْتُ}: this may be resumptive, by which he informs about himself. It may be an explanation for His saying {ذلكما مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِي ربي}, that is, "my abandonment of the worship of other than Allah is a cause of His teaching me that"; and on both aspects it has no grammatical position. And «لا يؤمنون» is an adjective of «قوم». He repeated «هم» in His saying {وَهُمْ بالآخرة هُمْ كَافِرُونَ}. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "To indicate that they in particular are disbelievers in the Hereafter, and that others are believers in it." Al-Shaykh said: "«هم», in our view, does not indicate particularity." I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not say that «هم» indicates particularity; he said only "the repetition of «هم» is to indicate", so it is the repetition that gives the particularity, and it is a good meaning, which the people of rhetoric (ahl al-bayān) understood.

semin-durr:38-38.t: The Kufans gave sukūn to the yāʾ of «آبائي», and it is also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr. And «إبراهيم» and what follows it are a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or accusative as praise.

semin-durr:1-1.t: Discussion of the like of His saying «تلك آياتُ» has already been given at the beginning of Yūnus.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قُرْآناً}: three analyses are permitted in it. One: it is a badal from the pronoun of «أَنْزَلْناه», or a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa) from it, and the pronoun in «أَنْزَلْناه» on these two views refers to «الكتاب». It was also said: «قُرْآناً» is a direct object and the pronoun in «أَنْزلْناه» is the pronoun of the maṣdar.
«عربيَّاً» is an adjective of the Qur'an. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قُرْآناً» if it carries a pronoun, meaning if we make it a ḥāl interpreted as a derived word, that is, "We sent it down gathered, while being Arabic." Al-ʿarabī is attributed to the Arabs because it was sent down in their language. The singular of al-ʿarab is ʿarabī, as the singular of al-Rūm is Rūmī. ʿArabah, with fatḥa on the rāʾ, is the region of the abode of Ismāʿīl the Prophet, peace be upon him. The poet said:
2377 - وعَرْبَةُ أرضٌ ما يُحِلُّ حرامَها ... مِنَ الناسِ إلا اللَّوْذَعِيُّ الحُلاحِلُ
(ʿArbah is a land whose sanctity none of the people violates but the sharp, noble chief.)
He put sukūn on its rāʾ by necessity; so al-ʿarabī may be attributed to this locale.
[Translator's note: the verse number is printed as 2377 in the source, where the sequence suggests 2733; it is reproduced as written.]

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَحْسَنَ القصص}: in the accusative of «أحسنَ» there are two analyses. [One]: that it is accusative as a direct object, but only if you make al-qaṣaṣ a maṣdar standing in the place of the object, like al-khalq in the sense of "the created," or you make it faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl like al-qabaḍ and al-naqaṣ in the sense of "the seized" and "the diminished," that is, "We relate to you the best of the things related." Two: that it is accusative as a clarifying maṣdar (maṣdar mubayyin), if you make al-qaṣaṣ a maṣdar not intended as the object, and the thing related is then omitted, that is, "We relate to you the best relating." «أَحْسَنَ» may be an elative (afʿal tafḍīl) in its basic sense, or may be a mere description by beauty, belonging to the chapter of annexing the attribute to what it describes, that is, "the beautiful narrative."
His saying: {بِمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ}: the bāʾ is causal and is attached to «نَقُصُّ», and «ما» is a maṣdar particle, that is, "because of Our revealing."
His saying: {هذا القرآن}: two analyses are permitted in it. One, which is the apparent: it is accusative as the direct object of «أَوْحَيْنا». Two: the matter belongs to the chapter of tanāzuʿ, I mean between «نَقُصُّ» and «أَوْحَيْنا», for each of them seeks «هذا القرآن», and the matter is one of the second operator acting. This arises only if we make «أَحْسَنَ» accusative as a maṣdar and do not supply an omitted object for «نَقُصُّ».
His saying: «وَإِن كُنتَ» to the end: its like has preceded it.
[Translator's note: the source has a stray slash after «يكونَ» in the first line, a page-break mark, not translated.]

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ قَالَ}: regarding its operator there are several analyses, the most apparent being that it is accusative by {قَالَ يابني} [Yūsuf: 5], that is, "Yaʿqūb said: 'O my little son,' at the time of Yūsuf's saying to him such and such." This is the easiest of the analyses, since in it «إذ» remains an adverbial of past time. It was also said: its governor is «الغافلين»; so said Makkī. It was also said: it is accusative by «نَقُصُّ», that is, "We relate to you the time of his saying such and such," and in this «إذ» is taken out of the past and out of being an adverbial; and if you supply the object as omitted, that is, "We relate to you the state at the time of his saying," it must be taken out of the past. It was also said: it is accusative by an implied verb, that is, "remember." It was also said: it is accusative as a badal from «أَحْسَنَ القصص», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "because the time includes the narrative, which is the thing related."
His saying: {ياأبت}: Ibn ʿĀmir read with fatḥa on the tāʾ, and the others with kasra. This tāʾ is a substitute for the yāʾ of the first person, which is why the two cannot be combined except by necessity, and this is specific to two expressions: yā abat and yā amat. It is not permitted in other nouns; if you said «يا صاحِبَتِ» it would not be permitted at all, just as the words "mother" and "paternal uncle" are specific to a ruling in a case like «يا بن أُمّ». The combination of this tāʾ with either the yāʾ or the alif is permitted by necessity, as in his saying:
2734 - يا أَبَتا عَلَّكَ أو عَساكا
(O my father, perhaps you, or may it be you...)
and the saying of another:
2735 - أيا أَبَتا لا تَزَلْ عندَنا ... فإنَّا نخافُ بأنْ نُخْتَرَمْ
(O my father, do not leave us, for we fear we shall be cut off.)
and the saying of another:
2736 - أيا أبتي لا زِلْتَ فينا فإنَّما ... لنا أَمَلٌ في العيشِ ما دُمْتَ عائِشا
(O my father, may you never cease to be among us, for we have hope in life as long as you live.)
Al-Zamakhsharī's statement suggests that combining the tāʾ and the alif is not by necessity, for he said: "If you ask: what is this kasra? I say: it is the kasra that was before the yāʾ in your saying «يا أبي», and was moved back to the tāʾ because the feminine tāʾ requires that what precedes it be with fatḥa. If you ask: why did the kasra not drop in favour of the fatḥa that the tāʾ requires, leaving the tāʾ sākin? I say: that is impossible in it because it is a noun, and nouns are due to be vowelled because of their originality in case-inflection; sukūn on the yāʾ is allowed, although its basic rule is to be vowelled, for lightening, because it is a soft letter, whereas the tāʾ is a sound letter like the kāf of the pronoun, so it must be vowelled. If you ask: combining this tāʾ with this kasra resembles combining the substitute with what it substitutes for, because it is in the position of the yāʾ when you say «يا غلامِ»; so as «يا أبتي» is not permitted, «يا أبتِ» is not permitted. I say: the yāʾ and the kasra before it are two things, and the tāʾ is a substitute for one of the two things, namely the yāʾ, while the kasra is not addressed; so the substitute and what it substitutes for are not combined, except when the tāʾ and the yāʾ are combined, and nothing else. Do you not see their saying «يا أبتا», where the alif is a substitute for the yāʾ, how combining it with the tāʾ was allowed and was not counted as combining the substitute and what is substituted for? The kasra is more remote than that. If you ask: the kasra in «يا غلامِ» indicated the annexation because it is the companion of the yāʾ and its neighbour; so if it indicates the same in «يا أبت», then the substituted tāʾ is idle, and its existence is like its absence. I say: rather its state with the tāʾ is as its state with the yāʾ when you say «يا أبي»."
Likewise the Shaykh's statement, for he said: "This tāʾ is a substitute for the yāʾ of annexation, so the two do not combine, but it combines with the alif that is a substitute for the yāʾ. He said:
2737 - يا أَبَتا عَلَّكَ أو عَسَاكا"
There is something to consider in this, in that the alif is like the yāʾ, being a substitute for it, so the two ought not to be combined.
The origin of this tāʾ is for the feminine. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is this tāʾ? I say: a feminine tāʾ that stands as a substitute for the yāʾ of annexation, and the proof that it is a feminine tāʾ is its changing into a hāʾ in pause." I say: what he mentioned about its changing into a hāʾ in pause is how Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read, while the others paused on it with the tāʾ, as if they treated it like the tāʾ of annexation (tāʾ al-ilḥāq) in bint and ukht. Among those who stated explicitly that it is for the feminine is Sībawayh, for he said: "I asked al-Khalīl about the tāʾ in «يا أبت», and he said: 'It is like the tāʾ in khāla and ʿamma,'" meaning that it is for the feminine; and what also indicates that it is for the feminine is their writing it as a hāʾ; and the analogy of one who pauses with the tāʾ is that he write it as a tāʾ, like bint and ukht.
Then al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how is it permissible to attach the feminine tāʾ to a masculine? I say: as it is permitted in your saying «حمامة ذَكَر», «وشاةٌ ذَكَر», «ورجلٌ رَبْعَة», and «وغلام يَفَعَة»." I say: he means that it was brought merely to feminise the word, as in the cited words. Then al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why was it permissible to substitute the feminine tāʾ for the yāʾ of annexation? I say: because the feminine and annexation correspond in that each of them is an addition joined to the noun at its end." I say: this is a remote analogy, not acted upon by the skilled, for it is called the formal resemblance (al-shabah al-ṭardī), meaning a resemblance in form.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«يا أَبَت» was read with the three vowels." As for the fatḥa and the kasra, I have attributed them to their readers; as for the ḍamma, it is very strange, and it resembles one who builds the vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the first person on ḍamma, like the reading of one who read, and it will come, Allah willing, {قَالَ رَبُّ احكم} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 112] with ḍamma on the bāʾ; its justification will come there, and why we said that it is annexed to the yāʾ and did not make it a single word without annexation.
The justification of the kasra on this tāʾ has already been given by what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned, that it is the kasra before the yāʾ moved back to the tāʾ. This is one of the two doctrines; the other doctrine: it is an extraneous kasra brought to indicate the yāʾ that it replaces; and it is not a disagreement of substance.
As for the fatḥa, it has four analyses, of which al-Fārisī mentioned two. One: that he made do with the fatḥa in place of the alif, meaning the alif converted from the yāʾ, as the other made do with it in place of it in his saying:
2738 - ولَسْتُ براجعٍ ما فاتَ منِّي ... بلَهْفَ ولا بلَيْتَ ولا لَوَنِّي
(I shall not retrieve what has passed me by with "alas" or "would that" or "if only I...")
and as it is made do with in place of it in «يا بن أمَّ» and «يا بنَ عمَّ», as given earlier. Two: that it was shortened (tarkhīm) by dropping the tāʾ, and then the tāʾ was inserted with fatḥa; this is as al-Nābigha said:
2739 - كِليْني لِهَمٍّ يا أُمَيمَةَ ناصِبِ ... وليلٍ أقاسِيه بطيءِ الكواكبِ
(Leave me to a toilsome care, O Umayma, and to a night I endure, slow in its stars.)
with fatḥa on the tāʾ of «أُمَيْمة», as I have mentioned to you.
Three: what al-Farrāʾ, Abū ʿUbayd, Abū Ḥātim and Quṭrub in one of his two statements mentioned, namely that the alif in «يا أبتا» is the alif of lamentation (nudba), which he then dropped, making do with the fatḥa in its place. This may help in answering the objection about combining the substitute and what is substituted for. Some have rejected this doctrine, saying that the place is not a place of lamentation.
Four: that the origin is «يا أبةً» with tanwīn, and the tanwīn was dropped because the vocative is a chapter of omission; Quṭrub held this in his second statement. This has been rejected on the ground that the tanwīn is not dropped from the accusative vocative, as in «يا ضارباً رجلاً».
Abū Jaʿfar read «يا أبي» with the yāʾ, not substituting the tāʾ for it.
Al-Ḥasan and Ṭalḥa ibn Sulaymān read: «أحدَ عْشر» with sukūn on the ʿayn, as if they intended by this lightening to alert that the two words are made one word.
His saying: {والشمس والقمر}: two analyses are permitted. One: the wāw is conjunctive, and it may then be of the chapter of mentioning the specific after the general by way of detail, because the sun and the moon entered into His saying {أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً}; so it is like His saying {وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ} [al-Baqara: 98] after His saying «وملائكتِه». It may also not be so, the wāw being for conjoining something different, so that he saw the sun and the moon in addition to the eleven, unlike the first, in which he saw the eleven, and among them the sun and the moon. Both possibilities are transmitted from the exegetes, and among those who transmitted them is al-Zamakhsharī.
The second analysis: the wāw is the wāw of accompaniment (maʿa). But it is the weaker, because whenever conjunction is possible without weakness or damage to the meaning, it is preferred to accompaniment; and on this it is like the analysis before it, in the sense that he saw the sun and the moon in addition to the eleven stars.
His saying: {رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ}: this admits two analyses. One: it is a sentence repeated for emphasis when the separation by objects grew long, so it was repeated, as «أنكم» was repeated in His saying {أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتٌّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَاباً وَعِظاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُّخْرَجُونَ} [al-Muʾminūn: 35]; so said the Shaykh, and the verification of this will come, Allah the Exalted willing. Two: it is not an emphasis, and al-Zamakhsharī leaned to this, for he said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of repeating «رأيتُهم»? I say: it is not a repetition; it is a resumptive speech on the supposition of a question, being an answer to it, as if Yaʿqūb, peace be upon him, had said to him at His saying {إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً والشمس والقمر}: 'How did you see them?', asking about the state of seeing them, so he said: 'I saw them prostrating to me.'"
I say: this is the more apparent, because whenever the speech revolves between taking it as emphasis or as establishing something new, taking it as the second is preferable.
«ساجدين» is an adjective pluralised with the plural of rational beings. It was said: because he treated them as rational beings in attributing their action to them, he pluralised them with their plural; and a thing may be treated as another thing if it shares in some attribute.
The seeing here is a seeing in a dream, and it has already been given that it governs two objects, like the seeing of knowing; and on this the second object of {رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً} would have been omitted, but omitting it by abbreviation only (iqtiṣār) is impossible, so only omission by condensation (ikhtiṣār) remains, which is rare or impossible according to some.
[Translator's note: the source has stray slashes at "ذكرْتُها ... /" and "أَنَّكُمْ / إِذَا", which are page-break marks, not translated. In the third paragraph of Quṭrub's analyses, the source prints «با أبتا» with bāʾ, evidently for «يا أبتا»; it is translated as «يا أبتا».]
